title: Allow passing CLI arguments to autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

It's crucial for apps with background behavior (no window, tray icon only) to update themselves seamlessly without interrupting the user and resume work after update as soon as possible. Nobody likes having their work interrupted when an application they aren't using suddenly restarts and displays its window on top of others. The resulting frustration may be so severe that it even prompt the user to completely abandon the application and uninstall it immediately.

Developers need a way to customize the startup behavior of the updated version. The most common requirement for a seamless background update is to prevent the updated application from spawning a new window if no windows were open before the update. The best way to achieve this is to pass CLI arguments to the updated application and handle them in the new process.

The problem is that `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` does not provide this capability

### Proposed Solution

Implement the ability to pass CLI arguments to autoUpdater.quitAndInstall() via an optional Options object.

### Alternatives Considered

1) **Using the `app.relaunch()`**: Ultimately, this method could be used to launch any executable following the main process termination. And it also allows for the passing of CLI arguments. The main disadvantage of this workaround is that it does not respect the new version prepared by the `autoUpdater`, which results in two application instances being launched: the old one and the updated one. You could fix this by manually providing the execPath to the Squirrel.Windows main executable. However, **this isn't a proper solution because app.relaunch() isn't intended for this responsibility**. Communicating with the underlying updating framework is solely the responsibility of the autoUpdater.
2) **Using a temp file**: While transferring data via a temporary file is possible, its main drawback is extremely low performance. This method introduces an additional delay in application window initialization, especially when checking a flag to determine if the window should be created at startup.

An API function  `Menu.getContextMenu()` as a counterpart to `Menu.getApplicationMenu()`.

title: Configurable type for webContents
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`webContents` gets assigned a `type` on creation. For `BrowserWindow` and `BrowserView` this type is `window` or `browserView`. Webviews always get the type `webview` (this is a hardcoded string: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/browser/guest-view-manager.ts#L102C5-L102C20 )

Because of that `webview` type, `webContents` for webviews are excluded when getting the list of pages through Puppeteer: https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.browser.pages which will only list the `page` type webContents, which it seems both `window` and `browserView` resolve to.

I encountered this issue when trying to set up [chrome-devtools-mcp](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/) to work with [Polypane](https://polypane.app). In Polypane, webviews are conceptually pages but since they are excluded from Puppeteers `browser.pages()` call, they do not show up in the MCP. Having more control over the types of webContents would allow my app to work with this tooling.

### Proposed Solution

It would be nice if there was some way to set the type of a `webview` to (resolve to) `page` rather than `webview`. I'm not too concerned with how, but here are a few options:

- `webContent`s already have a [getType()](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents#contentsgettype) method, add a setter.
- Extend the webview tag with a new `type` attribute that can be set to `page` that in turn overwrites the type on the guestView when specified.

These could both either be set as strings, or a number that refers to a pre-specified value (backgroundPage = 0, window = 1 etc). 

An alternative would be a boolean attribute or method to set the type of a webview to `page` when specified or `webview` when not.

### Alternatives Considered

Over in Chrome land, both the `background_page` and `webview` types are not a concern anymore so they might prefer to not make this change.

Other Linux ### Operating System Version Arch Linux (all distros are affected) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version N/A ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior The notification should simply fail to send ### Actual Behavior The app freezes for 1 minute ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/Vendicated/6f8d74229835950e1aeb5f43b74e1f92 ### Additional Information The root issue seems to be that `notify-send hi` will fail and get stuck until it times out after 1 minute. So the suggested fix is to make sure that notify-send is called asynchronously instead of waiting for it to exit. This issue doesn't happen on Chromium. This issue was already reported in the past but got automatically closed due to the tested Electron version no longer being supported: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/21912 This is a widespread issue that affects every Electron app. See for example: - https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Desktop/issues/2567 - https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Discord#Discord_freezes_after_getting_pinged_or_messaged Reproducing this is a bit inconsistent. For example I can't reproduce on Hyprland with no Notification daemon, but can reproduce on KDE Plasma with Notifications disabled. ## Reproduction Steps (KDE Plasma) 1. Install and run KDE Plasma 2. Right click the little Tray caret and click "Configure System Tray" 3. In "Entries", set "Notifications" to Disabled 4. Log out and back in 5. Run the attached Fiddle and click the Show Notification button 6. Observe that the App becomes unresponsive 7. Run `notify-send hi` in a terminal 8. Observe that it freezes until it times out

The existing native print dialog should be brought to the foreground and receive focus, allowing the user to interact with it.

### Actual Behavior

The print dialog remains in the background, out of view. The user cannot see the dialog appear on the screen, giving the impression that the print button is broken or unresponsive. A new dialog is not created (which is correct behavior for modal dialogs), but the existing one is not focused.

body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Originating issue: Element Desktop https://github.com/element-hq/element-desktop/issues/2689 

I was forwarded to upstream as this appears an Electron issue: About 1 1/2 years ago, I noticed that I could no longer launch Element Desktop with my tried & tested firejail configuration. While it launched, it failed to read the configuration / authentication data from the jail.
It turned out that for this to work, I was no longer able to block DBUS (`env DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=none firejail [..]`)

I consider this a security risk because: When DBUS is available, applications that launch other applications (in my case: Element Desktop launching a web browser for authentication to homeservers) will launch them outside the jailed context, giving them full access to the user home directory. In the case of a web browser, this exposes the user space to security flaws exploited by any website that is opened from an unjailed browser.

When DBUS is disabled, applications are launched within the same jailed context, and this security risk goes away / becomes acceptable.

In the referenced issue, I was informed that this likely results from the use of electron's safeStorage, and sure enough, as soon as I used the option to disable safeStorage (`~/.config/Element/electron-config.json`, setting: `safeStorageBackend: "plaintext"`), I could again launch the application in a jailed configuration with DBUS disabled.


### Proposed Solution

I would like to kindly request that the electron team investigates whether it is possible to make safeStorage work *without* DBUS available in a sandbox (e.g. firejail), thereby enabling both safeStorage *and* keeping further applications launched from a jailed application inside that same jail.

### Alternatives Considered

Currently working: disable DBUS but accept that safeStorage is not available.

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: No reliable way to detect rendering completion for large images in offscreen mode with hardware acceleration disabled
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Amazon Linux 2023, Kernel 6.1.119-129.201.amzn2023.x86_64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A - This issue exists across all tested versions

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When capturing a large image (256MB PNG, 11994x8000 pixels) in offscreen rendering mode with hardware acceleration disabled, there should be a reliable way to detect when rendering is complete before calling webContents.capturePage() or listening to the paint event.

**Expected behavior:**
1. Image loads completely in the DOM (img.complete === true)
2. Rendering pipeline finishes processing the large image
3. A deterministic signal or event indicates rendering completion
4. paint event provides a fully-rendered bitmap

Ideal API would be:
- A reliable event like webContents.on('render-complete', ...) 
- Or capturePage() that waits until rendering is fully complete
- Or a method like await webContents.waitForRenderComplete()

### Actual Behavior

**Problem**: There is no reliable way to know when rendering is actually complete for large images in offscreen mode.

**Current situation:**
1. img.load event fires successfully
2. img.complete === true and img.naturalWidth/Height are correct
3. paint events start firing immediately via webContents.invalidate()
4. BUT: Early paint events contain mostly empty bitmaps (all zeros)
5. After unpredictable time (5-15 seconds), paint events suddenly contain the actual rendered image
6. No way to distinguish "rendering in progress" vs "rendering complete" paint events

**Impact on production:**
- We serve 1000s of users generating images from templates
- Cannot reliably capture completed renders
- Users receive corrupted/incomplete images
- Must use unreliable workarounds (see below)

**Current workaround (unreliable):**

```
// Sample first 100 pixels and check if non-zero
let nonZeroCount = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < 400; i += 4) {
  if (bitmap[i] !== 0 || bitmap[i+1] !== 0 || bitmap[i+2] !== 0) {
    nonZeroCount++;
  }
}
const nonZeroRatio = nonZeroCount / 100;

// Hash bitmap and compare with previous
const hash = crypto.createHash('md5').update(sample).digest('hex');
if (nonZeroRatio > 0.1 && hash === previousHash) {
  // Assume rendering is complete
}
```

**Why this workaround is insufficient:**
- Pixel sampling is unreliable (what if image has black regions?)
- Hash comparison can stabilize on partially-rendered state
- No guarantee that "stable hash" = "fully rendered"
- Performance overhead of hashing large bitmaps
- Race conditions in multi-image scenarios

**Environment constraints:**
- Running on AWS C7i instances (no GPU)
- Must use app.disableHardwareAcceleration() for CPU-only rendering
- offscreen: true required for headless operation
- Cannot use setTimeout/delays in production (unreliable and slow)

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Requested solutions (any of these would help):**
1. Option A: Add webContents.waitForRenderComplete() async method
2. Option B: Add boolean flag to paint event: (event, dirty, image, isRenderComplete)
3. Option C: Add render-complete event after renderer finishes all pending work
4. Option D: Add webContents.getRenderingState() to query if rendering is in progress

**Environment details:**
- Electron: 39.1.2
- Chromium: 142.0.7444.134
- Node.js: 22.21.1
- OS: Amazon Linux 2023

No

### Expected Behavior

When launching an Electron application via Playwright's electron.launch() API (which uses the inspector protocol with --inspect=0 flag), the application should start successfully and remain running for automated testing.


### Actual Behavior

The Electron process crashes immediately with SIGTRAP signal after the debugger attaches:

```
  <launched> pid=366007
  [err] Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  [err] For help, see: https://nodejs.org/en/docs/inspector
  <ws connecting> ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  <ws connected> ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  [err] Debugger attached.
  <ws disconnected> code=1006 reason=
  <kill>
  <will force kill>
  <process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGTRAP>
```

This causes all Playwright-based E2E tests to fail.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

#### Steps To Reproduce

  1. Create a minimal Electron application
  2. Install Playwright: npm install --save-dev playwright@1.56.1
  3. Create a test file that launches Electron via Playwright:

     ```javascript
     const { _electron: electron } = require('playwright');
     const path = require('path');
     
     async function test() {
       const electronApp = await electron.launch({
         args: [
           path.join(__dirname, 'main.js'),
           '--no-sandbox',
           '--disable-gpu'
         ]
       });
   
       // Process crashes before reaching here
       await electronApp.close();
     }
   
     test();
     ```

  4. Run with Electron 39.2.0: Process crashes with SIGTRAP
  5. Downgrade to Electron 39.1.2: Process launches successfully

#### Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears to be caused by PR #48703 ("Automatically focus DevTools when element is inspected or breakpoint is triggered"), which was included in 39.2.0.

When Playwright connects via the inspector protocol, the new automatic DevTools activation logic tries to activate/focus a DevTools window that doesn't exist in the Playwright test environment, causing the crash.


#### Impact

This regression breaks all Playwright-based testing for applications that upgrade to Electron 39.2.0, affecting CI/CD pipelines and automated testing workflows.

title: Modal BrowserWindow: multiple show() calls leave parent disabled after close (refcount issue)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Version 10.0.26200.6899]

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.1.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When a modal BrowserWindow is created with a parent and modal: true:

1. The parent window should be disabled while the modal is shown.
2. After the modal is closed, the parent should become fully usable again (interactive, focusable),
3. This should hold even if show() has been called more than once on the modal (for example: once immediately, once in ready-to-show).

### Actual Behavior

If show() is called more than once on the modal window, closing the modal leaves the parent in a permanently disabled state:

- The parent cannot be interacted with (no mouse or keyboard interaction).
- It behaves as if a modal is still open and blocking it, even though the modal window is closed.

If, instead, I call hide() before close(), the parent becomes usable again. That suggests a reference-count mismatch for modal children on the parent window.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/gdavidkov/64ed0deb5c169e5a57de4e152be0e1b7

### Additional Information

Every call to Show() on a modal window increments the parent’s num_modal_children_, but the count is only decremented in Hide(). Close() does not adjust this counter.

So if show() is called multiple times on the same modal window, the parent’s num_modal_children_ can remain > 0 after the modal is closed, leaving the parent disabled.

This feels related to the changes in:

[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48770](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48770?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48865](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48865?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

and is similar in effect to the older issue:

[https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8768](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8768?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Workaround

Ensure that either:

- show() is called only once on the modal, or
- Call hide() before close():
 This brings the parent back to a usable state.

### Problem Description

My company is building a couple of Electron apps, packaged with electron-builder, targeting multiple platforms, among them Linux. The apps  install (from both deb and rpm) and work fine on multiple Linux distros. When testing on RHEL10, however, we noticed that we get an error during installation of the rpm:

```
Error: 
 Problem: conflicting requests
  - nothing provides libXScrnSaver needed by XXX from @commandline
```

This is caused by electron-builder defaulting the dependencies for rpm to include libXScrnSaver, which is no longer installed by default in RHEL10 and in fact is not even available anymore.

Redefining the dependencies to be the ones listed in electron-builder docs as default, minus libXScrnSaver, seem to work fine. The rpm now installs and the app runs, and even `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`, which I understood to be the reason for why libXScrnSaver is required, seems to be working. There does not appear to be any `libXss.so.*` anywhere in the system either so it really does seem like this library is not needed.

Further, checking what libs are needed using readelf -d shows a bunch of libraries, but not `libXss.so.*`.

This begs the question, is libXScrnSaver actually needed anymore? And what are the exact library requirements for an Electron app on Linux? I was trying to find this information, but was unable to.

Asking this in the electron-builder project I got this answer:

> This might be a better question to ask in upstream electron project.
> 
> Happy to update the default config used in electron-builder, but I'm guessing it'll require semver checks on the electronVersion as to what libs are deprecated or no longer required. So getting that clarity upfront will make any changes here more streamlined of a discussion

So I am now asking here: What are the exact library requirements for an Electron app on Linux?

### Proposed Solution

Please provide a list of dependencies needed for Electron apps on Linux.

### Alternatives Considered

Went with the defaults of electron-builder, but this results in the application not being able to install on RHEL10.

title: Decide TypeScript support in preloads since v40
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Node.js has enabled TypeScript type stripping by default in v24 of the runtime and mark it as stable in v25.2. It means that Electron v40 would support this feature by default too. But as soon as Electron has custom loader for preload scripts which has partial Node.js (CommonJS) semantic it should be decided whether enable type stripping in preloads or not. In my opinion not having TypeScript enabled could lead to unwanted inconsistency in the code, which is run on Electron's side. Today there are three modifications of JS which developers should use in Electron: 1. Node.js (CommonJS, ESModules), 2. Electron's Preload Scripts 3. Chromium's JS (in webpages and extensions). With partial TypeScript support the difference between them would grow further

In my opinion it could be confusing for developers too as soon as they see `require` in preload scripts and decide it is a Node.js/CommonJS module, which has TypeScript support

Another problem is that it would lead to unexpected behavior when `webPreferences.nodeIntegration` is turned on and node integration would work differently

Also it would make users to keep using builder for preloads (when it's not needed for main code), what looks excessive

### Proposed Solution

TypeScript stripping should be enabled in preload scripts. It should be done in the same way it realized in Node.js to reduce inconsistencies in bahavior. It also would reduce the amount of software needed to run Electron with TypeScript

### Alternatives Considered

Leave TypeScript enabled in main code and use preloads in its current view

### Additional Information

_No response_

# Electron Bug Report: `require('electron')` Returns Executable Path Instead of API Objects on Windows

## Summary

On Windows, when running Electron applications, `require('electron')` incorrectly resolves to the npm package's `node_modules/electron/index.js` which exports the path to the executable (`electron.exe`), instead of being intercepted by Electron's internal module loader to provide the Electron API objects (`app`, `BrowserWindow`, etc.).

This causes a critical failure where all Electron applications fail to start with:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'whenReady')
```

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10/11
- **Node.js**: v20.18.0 and v22.18.0 (tested both)
- **npm**: 10.9.3
- **Electron**: v31.7.7 and v39.2.2 (both affected)
- **Package Manager**: npm (also tested with bun v1.3.1, same issue)

## Expected Behavior

When `require('electron')` is called from within an Electron main process:

1. Electron's internal module loader (`c._load` in `node:electron/js2c/node_init`) should intercept the require call
2. Return the Electron API object containing `{ app, BrowserWindow, ipcMain, dialog, ... }`
3. Allow the application to start normally

## Actual Behavior

1. `require('electron')` resolves to `node_modules/electron/index.js`
2. That file returns the string path: `"C:\\path\\to\\node_modules\\electron\\dist\\electron.exe"`
3. Destructuring `const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')` results in `undefined` values
4. Application crashes when trying to call `app.whenReady()`

## Reproduction

### Minimal Reproduction Repository

Project structure:
```
project/
├── package.json
├── electron/
│   └── main.cjs
└── node_modules/
    └── electron/
```

### Step 1: Create package.json
```json
{
  "name": "electron-bug-test",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "electron/main.cjs",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "electron": "^31.7.7"
  }
}
```

### Step 2: Create electron/main.cjs
```javascript
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

console.log('Type of require("electron"):', typeof require('electron'));
console.log('Value:', require('electron'));
console.log('app:', app);
console.log('BrowserWindow:', BrowserWindow);

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  console.log('Electron started successfully');
});
```

### Step 3: Install and Run
```bash
npm install
npm start
```

### Expected Output:
```
Type of require("electron"): object
Value: [object Object]
app: [Function: app]
BrowserWindow: [Function: BrowserWindow]
Electron started successfully
```

### Actual Output:
```
Type of require("electron"): string
Value: C:\path\to\node_modules\electron\dist\electron.exe
app: undefined
BrowserWindow: undefined

C:\path\to\electron\main.cjs:7
app.whenReady().then(() => {
    ^

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'whenReady')
    at Object.<anonymous> (C:\path\to\electron\main.cjs:7:5)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1484:14)

title: Allow clicking through areas of a webContentView
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

We want to build an Electron app that offers external web content (inside a webContentView) in a section of a BaseWindow. Above that, we want to offer our custom UI that surrounds the web app content.

### Proposed Solution

There should be a mechanism inside webContentView that allows the dev to define that clicks on a certain area are pass-through to the next lower view. This way, we can keep the UI on top of everything with native performance of the actual web content.

One way to implement the check: A CSS-Class similar to "app-region: drag" that allows to define if an area of the app catches the whole event or let's the event pass through to the next layer. Alternatively (though inconsistent with existing similar functions), we could offer some function in the main process API for WebContentsView to add a "pass-through" area.

Technically, we could extend the respective functions of the Chromium "View" base class to make extra checks for these areas (and then return "no hit" if such an area is the one clicked).

### Alternatives Considered

There is no functionality in Electron to accommodate this use case. Existing hacks like forwarding mouseEvents to other webContentViews come with limitations and edge-cases, and stacking multiple windows with "setIgnoreMouseEvents" feels like the worst of all hacks.

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Electron Version

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro 19045.2965

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.6.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron is detected as a Chrome-based browser.

### Actual Behavior

Electron is detected as a Safari-based browser.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When changing the "ProductName" of electron.exe using [rcedit](https://github.com/electron/rcedit):
```ps1
rcedit-x64.exe electron.exe --set-version-string ProductName Foo
```

The user-agent changes from something like
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/142.0.7444.175 Electron/39.2.3 Safari/537.36
```
to
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/39.2.3 Safari/537.36
```

As you can see both the `Chrome` and `Electron` versions are removed, which means user-agent-based browser detections thinks the browser is a Safari browser (https://bowser-js.github.io/bowser-online/).

This seems to have changed from v36.6.0 to v36.7.0:
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.7103.177 Electron/36.6.0 Safari/537.36
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/36.6.0 Chrome/136.0.7103.177 Electron/36.6.0 Safari/537.36
```

```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.7103.177 Electron/36.7.0 Safari/537.36
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/36.7.0 Safari/537.36
```

I think at least the `Chrome` version should be included by default.

I also found it weird that there is no mention of this in the release notes for v36.7.0, so I don't think this change was on purpose: https://releases.electronjs.org/release/v36.7.0

title: Handling Relative Paths for Local File Loading via Custom Protocol after registerFileProtocol Deprecation
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I am encountering an issue when attempting to load local files, particularly an index.html file, within an <iframe> using a custom protocol registered via protocol.handle.

The context is the upcoming deprecation of protocol.registerFileProtocol(), prompting migration to protocol.handle().

Problem
When a custom scheme is handled with protocol.handle, it is treated as a network request. This behavior prevents the resolution of relative paths within the loaded file, which is crucial for handling static assets.

Example:

A custom scheme is used to load an HTML file: <iframe src="custom://contents/index.html"></iframe>

The index.html file attempts to load a resource using a relative path: <video src="./assets/sample.mp4"></video>

The Electron/Chromium networking stack resolves the resource URL incorrectly as: custom://contents/index.html/assets/sample.mp4

This resolution logic mimics a standard server hosting environment where the path is appended, which is unsuitable for local file paths where the parent directory structure should be preserved.

Current Workarounds & Concerns
Using the file:// Protocol: Loading assets directly via file:// would resolve relative paths correctly, but this often requires setting webSecurity: false in the webPreferences of the BrowserWindow.

Web Security Risk: Disabling webSecurity poses significant security risks, especially in contexts where arbitrary or untrusted content might be loaded.

Question / Feature Request
How can a custom scheme registered with protocol.handle be configured to resolve relative paths and treat the request as a local file protocol (file:// behavior) for nested resources, without compromising security by globally disabling webSecurity?

A mechanism to properly handle the base URL and relative path resolution for assets served from the local file system using protocol.handle is urgently needed before registerFileProtocol is fully deprecated.

### Proposed Solution

A parameter (e.g., type: 'network' | 'file') should be added to the handler options.

### Alternatives Considered

or other method?..

title: Support for multiple user profiles
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Introduce native support for multiple user profiles within the application, similar to Chrome/Chromium profile behavior. Each profile should maintain completely isolated sessions, storage, cookies, cache, and authentication state.

Without proper profile isolation, users must frequently log in and out, risking session conflicts and data leakage.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a profile system backed by Electron’s `session` partitions:
Each user profile maps to a unique persistent partition (e.g., `persist:userId`)

Full isolation of:
 - Cookies
 - LocalStorage / IndexedDB
 - Cache
 - Authentication tokens
 - Profiles persist across application restarts
 - Everything on application layer

Ability to:
 - Create new profiles
 - Switch between profiles without restarting the app
 - Delete profiles safely

### Alternatives Considered

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

last known working version could not be determined because the application failed on every tested version.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

The application is expected to launch, initialize the Chromium renderer process successfully, and display the fully styled Graphical User Interface (GUI) as designed.

The main Electron window should open and present the complete application UI, which includes the styled form fields, and correctly colored buttons (green for Save, indigo for Preview).

The application should not display a blank white screen or an unstyled, bare HTML interface.

The application's internal JavaScript logic (for generating the manifest object) and the secure IPC bridge (window.fileAPI) should initialize without error.

### Actual Behavior

When the application is launched, the following happens:

1.  The main Electron window opens successfully.
2.  The application **fails to render any styling or layout** from the fully embedded CSS.
3.  The user interface is displayed as **plain, unstyled HTML text** (white background, default black font, unstyled buttons).
4.  There is **no crash log or error message** generated; the Chromium renderer process silently fails to apply the styles, indicating a deep-seated system conflict during graphical initialization.

This behavior persists even when launching with the most permissive flags: `npx electron . --no-sandbox --disable-site-isolation-trials --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity`.


Here is the diagnostic timeline section in a single markdown block, exactly as it appears in the final bug report:

```markdown
#### C. Final Electron Failure (The System Conflict)

Despite the code being proven correct and all components being embedded, the failure persists in the native Electron window.

| Step | Command Executed | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cache Clear & Relaunch** | `rm -rf ~/.config/flatpak-manifest-builder` then `npx electron . --no-sandbox` | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
| **Final Nuclear Launch** | `npx electron . --no-sandbox --disable-site-isolation-trials --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity` | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
| **CSS Fix** | All CSS was **embedded directly** into `index.html` to eliminate all external file access conflicts. | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## 🔗 Testcase Gist URL

**N/A (System-Level Conflict)**

A simple Electron Fiddle link cannot be provided because the application code has been confirmed to be **100% functional** and bug-free (tested working perfectly via `http-server` in Chrome and Firefox).

The failure is a **deep incompatibility** between the Chromium renderer (used by Electron v39) and the core Fedora/Gnome system libraries. **The bug cannot be reproduced in the clean, isolated context of Electron Fiddle**; it requires the specific library environment of the host system to fail.

We request attention based on the extensive diagnostic evidence provided in the "Diagnostic Timeline" section above.

body:

### Electron Version

36.9.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows, macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS Tahoe, Win11, Win10

### What arch are you using?

Other (specify below)

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.7.4

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon`  should be able to take in a guid of format `{<guid>}` in addition to `<guid>`

Root cause is in additional information

### Actual Behavior

when passing a guid into `NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon` of the format `{<guid>}`, it errors out with `Invalid GUID format - GUID must be a string`

Root cause is in additional information

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/a0d983e4b53432b236499cf76638ead4dd3d2c46 added a change where `NotifyIconHost::CreateNotifyIcon` takes in a base::Uuid GUID as opposed to a UUID GUID.

The gin_converter/guid_converter for UUID GUID has input sanitization that removes { & } from the outside of the GUID (Windows wraps GUIDs in braces).
```
if (!guid.empty()) {
      if (guid[0] == '{' && guid[guid.length() - 1] == '}') {
        guid = guid.substr(1, guid.length() - 2);
      }
    }
```

Since we switched to using a base::Uuid GUID, & its gin convert does not hav ethis input sanitization, existing electron users that take in a guid of the format `{ guid }` are met with an error `Invalid GUID format - GUID must be a string` because the converter returns an empty string.

Type check should pass with latest `@types/node` versions.
The following should have no errors:
```
mkdir electron-type-error
cd electron-type-error
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm i typescript electron
npx tsc --init --skipLibCheck false
echo "import electron from 'electron'; console.log(electron.shell);" > main.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
```

### Actual Behavior

Fails as of `@types/node@22.19.3` with:
```
node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712:17 - error TS2687: All declarations of 'noDeprecation' must have identical modifiers.

1712                 noDeprecation?: boolean;
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~

node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712:17 - error TS2717: Subsequent property declarations must have the same type.  Property 'noDeprecation' must be of type 'boolean', but here has type 'boolean | undefined'.

1712                 noDeprecation?: boolean;
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738:5
    25738     noDeprecation: boolean;
              ~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    'noDeprecation' was also declared here.

node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738:5 - error TS2687: All declarations of 'noDeprecation' must have identical modifiers.

25738     noDeprecation: boolean;
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~


Found 3 errors in 2 files.

Errors  Files
     2  node_modules/@types/node/process.d.ts:1712
     1  node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:25738

```

Seems like @types/node [added](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/pull/74184) `noDeprecation` as an optional field, but electron defines it as required.

### Problem Description

 The current Node.js script that spawns and manages the Electron process works correctly, but it can be improved for robustness, safety, and maintainability.
Some edge cases (like spawn failure or multiple event listeners) are not fully handled.

### Proposed Solution

Use child.once() instead of child.on() for lifecycle events

Handle the exit event in addition to close

Add a listener for the error event on the spawned process

Refactor signal handling to avoid repetition

### Alternatives Considered

Prevents accidental multiple event triggers

Avoids silent crashes if Electron fails to start

Improves code readability and intent

Makes the process lifecycle handling more production-safe

### Additional Information

The child process lifecycle should be handled safely and deterministically

Spawn failures should be caught and reported clearly

Event listeners should be registered only once

Signal handling should be concise and easier to extend

Make `Session#clearHostResolverCache()` clear Renderer's DNS cache

Yes

### Expected Behavior

### Summary

### Actual Behavior

### Summary
On macOS 26.2 Tahoe (latest official release), multiple Electron-based applications are being **force-terminated by the system (SIGKILL)** without generating crash reports. These terminations happen even with the latest versions of the applications and with up-to-date macOS.

This behaviour goes beyond UI lag/stutter described in other issues (e.g., #48311). In my case, apps such as VS Code, Slack, Chrome, and other Electron apps are killed by the OS abruptly without crash logs, often correlated with sustained WindowServer activity.

I have collected sysdiagnose output showing high WindowServer involvement shortly before the terminations. This appears to be a system resource / compositor rendering interaction issue rather than an app-specific crash.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Boot macOS 26.2 Tahoe on Apple Silicon (M4/Mx).
2. Open multiple Electron-based applications (VS Code, Slack, Chrome, etc.).
3. Work normally (code editing, multiple windows, no special operations).
4. After some time, one or more apps are killed by the OS without warnings or crash reports.

### Expected Behavior
Electron apps should not be abruptly terminated by the OS without crash reports. Users should be able to work without unexpected force quits.

### Actual Behavior
Apps are abruptly terminated (SIGKILL) by the system. No crash report is generated in Console for these terminations.

### Context
Related Electron compatibility discussions include performance and rendering issues on macOS 26 (e.g., #48311), but this report reflects **forced termination behaviour**, which has not been documented in existing open issues:

• Strange global lag / WindowServer issues — https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48311 :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}  
• VS Code GPU/WindowServer behaviour discussions — https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/267022 :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}  
• Community confirmation of macOS 26 + Electron compatibility problems — https://www.reddit.com/r/MacOS/comments/1nj0jb5/do_not_update_to_macos_26_if_you_use_vscode/ :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

### Additional Files / Logs
I have attached the sysdiagnose archive, including `RunningBoard` priority samples, `jetsam_priority.csv`, and `top.txt`, which show:
- WindowServer high rendering involvement
- Lack of memory pressure or crash logs
- Force terminated Electron processes

Please let me know if additional logs or a reproducible test case is needed.

title: Support `resign-key` and `become-key` events on `BrowserWindow` (macOS)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, Electron’s `BrowserWindow` exposes `focus` and `blur` events, but it does not expose the native macOS `NSWindow` events for `windowDidBecomeKey` and `windowDidResignKey`.

While `focus` and `blur` often correlate with key status, they are not semantically identical, especially when building floating panels, overlays, or "spotlight-like" interfaces (`NSPanel`).

### Proposed Solution

Expose the native [`windowDidBecomeKey`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindowdelegate/windowdidbecomekey(_:)) and [`windowDidResignKey`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindowdelegate/windowdidresignkey(_:)) events as `become-key` and `resign-key` (or similar) on the `BrowserWindow` instance. We noticed that `BrowserWindow::OnWindowIsKeyChanged(bool is_key)` already exists in `electron_api_browser_window.cc` ([source link](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/809ab09b6f5ede0a9f9b0fcc0e9c33ff971277f2/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc#L188)), but it does not appear to be mapped to a public-facing event that consumers can listen to.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Native Modules:** We are currently using a native module to access `NSWindowDelegate` methods directly.
- **Using `blur` event:** It does not map 1:1 with `resignKey` behavior in multi-window setups.

### Additional Information

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 version 25H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior When middle clicking a hyperlink, or CmdOrCtrl + left clicking a hyperlink, a new tab can be opened in the background in Chrome. As for Electron, these open a new BrowserWindow by default that loads the URL, if windowOpenHandler is not overwritten by `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler`. ### Actual Behavior Override windowOpenHandler by `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler`. Customize the `createWindow` method, where users want to create a WebContentsView or BrowserView instead of a BrowserWindow to load the URL, so that it can be displayed somewhere else on the original window. This works fine if we are left clicking a hyperlink with `target="_blank"`, but fails to construct a WebContentsView if we are middle clicking or CmdOrCtrl + left clicking it (to be more specific, when `disposition` is `background-tab`), because `options.webContents` is undefined for the latter two situations. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/z0gSh1u/ec10a10a5c1515101af66b1600f27049 ### Additional Information Can be reproduced on macOS too.

title: Window freezes on macOS when failing to enter fullscreen (regression)
body:

### Electron Version

39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

37.7.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

1. User begins swiping between virtual desktops (see #43112 for some context).
2. Electron window requests fullscreen.
3. The window fails to enter fullscreen mode (due to being halfway between two virtual desktops), but remains usable.

### Actual Behavior

Upon failing to enter fullscreen mode, the contents of the window freeze. In the attached example gist, this is visible in two distinct ways:
- The red border around the window disappears on the right and bottom sides, which I believe is due to the contents of the window being rendered as if it is fullscreened.
- The animated spinning box freezes.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/cptpcrd/bf28bf81d7cd4c4f4197367b54c708ba

### Additional Information

I have bisected this down to a regression that first appeared between v37.7.0 and v37.7.1, specifically in #47151 (and its backports).

As best as I can tell, following the failed fullscreen transition, the OS briefly reports the window as first occluded (which causes `OnWindowHide` to run), then visible (which previously caused `OnWindowShow` to run, but following #47151 now does nothing). It seems that the mismatched calls cause Chromium to think the page is hidden and thus does not need to be rendered.

This change fixes the issue for me locally (though it also means `WebContents::WasShown` runs twice back-to-back when `Show` is called, which I suspect is undesirable):

```diff
--- a/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc
+++ b/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc
@@ -280,6 +280,7 @@ v8::Local<v8::Value> BrowserWindow::GetWebContents(v8::Isolate* isolate) {
 }
 
 void BrowserWindow::OnWindowShow() {
+  web_contents()->WasShown();
   BaseWindow::OnWindowShow();
 }
 
```

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 25H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Intuitively, `setBounds` is related to positions and has nothing to do with the favicon. So `page-favicon-updated` event should not be emitted when calling `setBounds` with a new `bounds` on a WebContentsView. ### Actual Behavior Construct a WebContentsView, listen its `page-favicon-updated` event, add it to the main window, and `loadURL` for like `https://electronjs.org`. Then call `setBounds` with a new `bounds` on the WebContentsView, `page-favicon-updated` will be triggered. This doesn't occur on all websites, but many websites have this problem, including `https://github.com`. Usually this won't lead to noticeable problems. But if the user wants to auto resize the WebContentsView when the main window resizes, `setBounds` will be frequently called and a series of `page-favicon-updated` event will be emitted, even if the favicon urls array is not changed. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/z0gSh1u/72fe6f155e1f145385461853d7ef2782 ### Additional Information Can be reproduced on macOS too.

I'd like an API that allows me to show a window without focusing it or bringing it to the foreground. This could either be a new window method, or a parameter on `showInactive` that disables foregrounding.

### Expected Behavior

Description: I am reporting a critical performance issue with the Discord macOS client (Electron-based) that leads to system instability and I/O timeouts on Intel-based MacBooks. As an electronics engineer, I have verified this is NOT a hardware failure.

Hardware Validation:

    Storage: M.2 SATA SSD via PCIe adapter.

    Physical Layer: Double-sided gold-plating on adapter contacts (Gold-to-Gold interface) to ensure zero oxidation and minimal contact resistance.

    Power Stability: Added 3x tantalum capacitors (500uF each) on the VCC line to filter transient spikes and stabilize voltage during high I/O bursts.

    Stress Test: Passed 40GB small-file sequential and random write tests without errors.

    Conclusion: Hardware is 100% stable; failure occurs only under Discord's specific I/O pattern.

Technical Observations: The Discord client (specifically Discord Helper processes) initiates an aggressive pattern of synchronous SQLite commits and fsync calls. On systems where the I/O latency is slightly higher than native Apple NVMe (e.g., AHCI/SATA protocols over PCIe bridges), this "flooding" of the command queue leads to a driver-level timeout (AppleStorageDevice). This results in the partition table being dropped or a full Kernel Panic.

Proposed Fix:

    Implement better batching for SQLite transactions to reduce the frequency of fsync.

    Introduce a "Low I/O Mode" for older Intel Mac hardware.

    Optimize Chromium's cache management to be less aggressive on APFS metadata updates.

### Actual Behavior

body:

### Electron Version

32.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

ventura

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

16.0.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Reproduction Update: I have successfully reproduced the I/O saturation using a standalone Electron Fiddle script.

Monitoring with fs_usage on macOS confirms that Electron is triggering massive amounts of fcntl <FULLFSYNC> calls. On my hardware configuration (high-quality external controller), each FULLFSYNC takes approximately 14-18ms.
Plaintext

20:12:02.301507  fcntl  F=39  <FULLFSYNC>  0.014464  Electron.2091985
20:12:02.320365  fcntl  F=39  <FULLFSYNC>  0.013900  Electron.2091985

This confirms that the issue is not specific to Discord's business logic, but rather how Electron/Chromium manages the I/O queue when multiple FULLFSYNC requests are issued in a short window. The lack of proper backpressure leads to a driver-level timeout (Kernel Panic).

### Actual Behavior

I have monitored the execution of the Fiddle reproduction script. The results are conclusive: aggressive I/O operations through Electron's fs module lead to a cascade failure of other Electron internal services.

Specifically, during the FULLFSYNC flood (latencies of 14-18ms per call), the Network Service crashes repeatedly:
Plaintext

[22262:0115/201214.919853:ERROR:content/browser/network_service_instance_impl.cc:613] Network service crashed, restarting service.

This confirms that the I/O blocking is so severe that it starves the Chromium IPC/Network stack, causing internal timeouts. This is the exact state that precedes the Kernel Panic I've been experiencing. It's not a Discord bug; it's a fundamental issue with how Electron handles I/O pressure on macOS when hardware latency deviates from standard internal SSD profiles.

https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/49407

### Problem Description

_This is just an interesting observation and doesn't introduce any harm. So feel free to investigate or ignore it._

When running `electron --run` in cmd.exe in Windows Terminal with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` env, it writes newlines (`\n`) as the character ◙ ([INVERSE WHITE CIRCLE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alt_code#:~:text=INVERSE%20WHITE%20CIRCLE)). For reference, `\n` is `String.fromCharCode(10)` and the white circle can be input by Alt+10 in old MS systems.

For testing this behavior, install electron to PATH, prepare a package.json and script:

```cmd
@REM node_shim.cmd
@echo off
setlocal

set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
call electron %*
```

```js
// package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "foo": "node_shim foo.js"
  }
}

// foo.js
console.log('aaa\nbbb\nccc')
```

Run `node_shim --run foo` returns:

```
aaa◙bbb◙ccc◙
```

If you replace the `node_shim` above with `node` (so do not invoke electron), the output is correct.

Environment:
- Windows 11
- Electron 40
- Node.js 25 (for correct behavior)

### Proposed Solution

Investigate what happens on `--run` with electron.

### Alternatives Considered

N/A

### Additional Information

This only happens when electron is used as node and invoked with `--run`.

I happens to find this issue when I was trying to use _only_ electron to develop something.

body:

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (10.0.26100 Build 26100)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The `exit` event in `utilityProcess` should include the correct exit code for the process, regardless of how it exits.

### Actual Behavior

If you clone the attached gist and run `npm install && npm run build && npm run start`, you get the following output:
```
Utility process exited with code: 18446744072635812000
```

This also happens if you use the `exit()` function from `cstdlib`, but not if you call `process.exit(0xC0000AA0)` in `utility.js` for some reason.

The correct decimal value would be `3221228192`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/rf-/bbe5ecede1f2b10ac2bed4c46ac66509

### Additional Information

I started looking into this because of a user report about a utility process crash. The logs reported the exit code `18446744072635812000`, which seemed weirdly high and isn't documented anywhere.

I think the issue here is that [exit codes on Windows are 32-bit unsigned integers, a.k.a. `DWORD`s](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-getexitcodeprocess), but [they get passed from Chromium to Electron as `int`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/patches/chromium/feat_enable_passing_exit_code_on_service_process_crash.patch) and then eventually get turned into 64-bit values by first extending the "signed" integer to 64 bits and then reinterpreting it as an unsigned value.

This works fine if the code is low enough to be interpreted as a positive `int`, but if it's interpreted as a negative `int` it gets mangled by the extension to 64 bits. Here's some Rust demonstrating this process:
```
let a: u32 = 0xC0E90002;
println!("{a:x} {a}"); // c0e90002 3236495362

let b: i32 = a as i32;
println!("{b:x} {b}"); // c0e90002 -1058471934

let c: i64 = b as i64;
println!("{c:x} {c}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 -1058471934

let d: u64 = c as u64;
println!("{d:x} {d}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 18446744072651079682
```

Then of course it gets turned into a 64-bit float by JavaScript, which loses precision since the value is so high. This is unfortunate since there are [70 different `NTSTATUS` codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-erref/596a1078-e883-4972-9bbc-49e60bebca55) that yield my original error code when sent through this process.

I haven't looked too closesly at the relevant code on the Electron side, but I think the fix would just be to immediately cast the `int` value we get from Chromium to a `uint` so that subsequent conversions don't misinterpret the value?

### Problem Description

as per #19429 - there currently is no way to prevent alt+space in windows from opening the system context menu 

even using webContents.on("before-input-event")... though, even if it did, its less than ideal as preventing a keyDown event means that the keyUp will never fire, as per #37336

### Proposed Solution

#19429 proposes allowing an override specifically for alt+space, but I think it might be more meaningful to have the alt+space get routed through the existing "before-input-event" event, as it is more semantically appropriate and (hopefully) should allow the actual relevant keyboard events through.

### Alternatives Considered

I feel the only viable alternative would be as #19429 suggests: have a specific option to override the alt+space keyboard combination, but I think that's less than ideal for the aforementioned reasons.

I have tried using a global hotkey and an accelerator key, but neither were able to allow the key event through to the browser window.

macOS

### Operating System Version

Tahoe: Version 26.2 (25C56)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

There should be a way to allow package directories (like `.ufo`, `.bundle`, etc.) to be:
- Visible and selectable when matching a filter extension
- Selected via double-click (same as regular files)

### Actual Behavior

I'm building a font editor where I need to load [ufo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Font_Object) files (which are directories).

When using `dialog.showOpenDialog()` with filters that include a package directory extension (e.g., `.ufo`), there's no way to allow users to both:
1. See the package directory as selectable (not greyed out)
2. Double-click to select it (rather than navigating into it)

## Attempts and results

### 1. With filters only

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory"],
  filters: [{ name: "Fonts", extensions: ["ufo"] }],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` directories are greyed out and cannot be selected.

### 2. With `treatPackageAsDirectory`

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory", "treatPackageAsDirectory"],
  filters: [{ name: "Fonts", extensions: ["ufo"] }],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` directories are selectable via single-click + Open button, but double-clicking navigates into the directory instead of selecting it.

### 3. Without filters

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory"],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` can be selected, but so can any other file type, which is not an ideal experience for a user.

### Problem Description

In CI, when tests are flaky and fail, we need to re-run them manually. This is annoying, costs time, and costs computing hours.

### Proposed Solution

Chromium has a nice solution where if a test fails, CI re-runs that single specific test automatically before reporting failure.

If we adopted that for Electron, we'd save maintainers time and we'd reduce our cloud bill. (We'd re-run just the failed test, not the whole test suite.)

Re-run all tests automatically as a first step. Would already be better than the current solution.

Unknown

### Expected Behavior

Running an Electron app from the command line should not print code signing errors when the code signature is valid.

### Actual Behavior

When running VS Code (or any Electron app) from the CLI, the following error is printed to stderr:

```
[0204/102237.819836:ERROR:electron/shell/common/mac/codesign_util.cc:109] SecCodeCheckValidity: Error Domain=NSOSStatusErrorDomain Code=-67062 "(null)" (-67062)
```

Error code -67062 = `errSecCSSignatureInvalid`

However, the code signature is actually **valid** according to macOS:

```
$ codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/Visual\ Studio\ Code.app
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: valid on disk
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: satisfies its Designated Requirement

$ spctl --assess --verbose /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
```

This appears to be Electron's internal `SecCodeCheckValidity` call in `codesign_util.cc` failing on macOS 26, even though the signature is valid.

### Expected Behavior

Electron v40 supports macOS 12 and above. Native Node modules should also be built with support for macOS 12 and above.

Native modules are built with support for macOS 13.5 and above.

They do not work on macOS 12–13.5.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Repro:

```bash
npx create-electron-app@latest my-app --template=webpack
cd my-app
npm i fs-xattr
npm start
otool -l node_modules/fs-xattr/build/Release/xattr.node
```

The output includes:

```
    minos 13.5
      sdk 26.2
```

Some libs work around it, e.g., [better-sqlite3](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3/blob/27cb07b5926652ae0e601dc26a35714128692f18/deps/common.gypi#L59).

We might want to lower it again in Electron for as long as we support macOS <= 13.4.

title: feat: Automated Spell Check for Blog Content (Typos Detection)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, there is no automated mechanism to catch spelling mistakes specifically in blog content. As a result, typos often go unnoticed during development and code review, and eventually get merged into production. This affects the professionalism, readability, and quality of the website.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an automated spell-check step in the CI/CD pipeline that:

- Runs on every pull request that modifies files inside /blog/** (or relevant blog directory).
- Uses a tool like typos (or an equivalent spell-checker).
- Fails the CI check if critical spelling errors are detected.
- Allows a configurable ignore list (.typos.toml) for valid technical terms, names, or abbreviations.
- Provides clear, actionable error messages pointing to the exact file and line with the typo.

### Alternatives Considered

- Manual review by maintainers: Rejected because it does not scale and increases workload.
- GitHub issue templates only: Helpful but does not prevent duplicate submissions.
- Strict issue submission rules: Too restrictive and may discourage contributions.

### Additional Information

- This feature would be especially useful for large repositories with frequent contributions.
- Can be implemented using GitHub Actions with existing tools like issue similarity bots or custom scripts.
- Similar functionality is used in repositories like Kubernetes and TensorFlow.

### Problem Description

This is inspired by #1219, and is a potential duplicate of it (but with a wider scope). Right now [our documentation on the use of `window.open` in the renderer](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.2.1/docs/api/window-open.md#windowopenurl-framename-features) reads as follows:
> Electron will parse [`BrowserWindowConstructorOptions`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/browser-window-options) out of this list where possible, for convenience. For full control and better ergonomics, consider using `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` to customize the BrowserWindow creation.

### Proposed Solution

The "where possible" here is a bit vague and while the push towards `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` is probably warranted, I believe the docs could be improved by more explicitly calling out [what feature strings we actually support there (which is arguably more limited than what the wording here would suggest).](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.2.0/lib/browser/parse-features-string.ts#L78)

### Alternatives Considered

We could also just continue to let the encouragement to use `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` do the heavy lifting for us and not bother with explaining the specific inner workings of a less-capable feature.

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

If `useSharedTexture` is enabled, shared texture should be created with same directx texture flags for any `pixelFormat` in `OffscreenSharedTexture` object.

### Actual Behavior

Shared textures are created with different directx texture flags.

To be specific
* Shared texture with `pixelFormat: bgra` is created only with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` flag as stated documentation.
* Shared texture with `pixelFormat: rgbaf16` is created with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` and `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_KEYEDMUTEX` flags. So `IDXGIKeyedMutex` must be acquired and locked. Without this, all GPU operations, such as copying and drawing, will perform as if the texture were transparent, without any error.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Shared textures should be created using same flags, or at least the differences should be clearly stated in the documentation.

title: `webUtils.getNativeVideoFrameHandle(frame)` for Zero-Copy VideoFame GPU Handoff
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, high-performance video applications in Electron (e.g., those using node-av, ffmpeg, or custom C++ encoding/AI pipelines) lack a supported way to access the underlying GPU handle of a VideoFrame directly from Renderer process to send it to the main process.

It is a primary bottleneck in high-performance scenarios of encoding video frames created by the renderer process.



### Proposed Solution

Proposed API Expanding the [webUtils](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-utils)) module to provide a bridge between WebCodecs/MediaStream frames and native system handles.

```ts
  const handle = webUtils.getNativeVideoFrameHandle(videoFrame);
  
  if (handle) {
    // Zero-copy: only the handle travels over IPC
    ipcRenderer.send('process-gpu-handle', handle.iosurface); // platform specific handles, same as shared texture
  }
```

### Alternatives Considered

Moving frames from the Renderer to the Main process currently requires one of:

CPU Readback: Using copyTo() to move pixels to an ArrayBuffer. This is extremely expensive at 4K/60fps and negates the benefits of hardware decoding.

Private Hacks: Disabling the sandbox to use Node.js native addons that attempt to "guess" memory offsets of Chromium's internal media::VideoFrame objects. This is fragile across Electron versions and insecure.

Using `paint` event with shared textures. It works, but even if high fpu values on browser window, waiting for paint event often takes ~8-20ms for large textures which is quite bad considering I already have `VideoFrame` created in the renderer process, so what I need is already in GPU memory, I don't need a separate one from the paint event which is equal to the one I have already

### Additional Information

Electron's internal C++ implementation would likely unwrap the blink::VideoFrame, access its media::VideoFrame, and extract the gfx::GpuMemoryBuffer.

Security: By implementing this in webUtils, Electron maintains the security model. The Renderer never sees the raw pointer, only a system-level ID that the Main process (trusted) can resolve.

title: GPU process hangs on Linux when argv contains both spaces and multi-byte UTF-8 characters
body:
## Description

On Linux, when an Electron app is launched with command-line arguments containing **both** a space and a multi-byte UTF-8 character (emoji, CJK, etc.), the GPU subprocess fails to initialize and the process hangs indefinitely. This does not occur on Windows.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Works (no spaces in argument with emoji)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello🎉world"

# Hangs indefinitely (space + emoji in same argument)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello 🎉 world"

# Works (spaces but no emoji)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello world"
```

The GPU process logs:
```
ERROR:components/viz/service/main/viz_main_impl.cc:189] Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization
```

Confirmed via `strace -f`: child/zygote processes hang while reading `/proc/self/cmdline`.

## Environment

- **OS**: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8.0, Docker container with no GPU hardware)
- **Electron**: 33+ (via Obsidian 1.12.1, but reproducible with any Electron app on Linux)
- **GPU**: None (software rendering) — but the bug is in command-line parsing, not GPU initialization itself

## Root Cause Analysis

The bug is in `base/command_line.cc` in `AppendSwitchesAndArguments` and `SetProgram`:

```cpp
// Windows — Unicode-aware ✅
arg = CommandLine::StringType(TrimWhitespace(arg, TRIM_ALL));

// Linux/POSIX — ASCII-only, byte-by-byte ❌
TrimWhitespaceASCII(arg, TRIM_ALL, &arg);
```

`TrimWhitespaceASCII` operates byte-by-byte on what it assumes is an ASCII string. When arguments contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (3+ bytes, e.g., emoji `0xF0 0x9F 0x8E 0x89`), it doesn't understand character boundaries.

The chain of events:

1. CLI launches with emoji + spaces in argv
2. Zygote forks a GPU child process
3. Child calls `CommandLine::InitFromArgv()` → `AppendSwitchesAndArguments` runs `TrimWhitespaceASCII` on each argument byte-by-byte
4. `SetProcessTitleFromCommandLine` flattens all args into a single space-separated string and writes it over the original argv memory via `setproctitle`
5. `/proc/self/cmdline` now contains corrupted data
6. GPU subprocess reads corrupted command line → switches like `--type=gpu-process` are malformed → GPU initialization fails → process hangs

### Why each condition is required:

- **Without spaces**: `TrimWhitespaceASCII` has nothing to trim, multi-byte bytes (all > 0x7F) pass through unmodified
- **Without multi-byte UTF-8**: Pure ASCII, byte-level operations work correctly
- **With both**: Byte-level trimming near space + multi-byte boundaries corrupts string length calculations, which cascades through `setproctitle` into corrupted `/proc/self/cmdline`

### Why Windows is unaffected:

- Uses `TrimWhitespace` (Unicode-aware) instead of `TrimWhitespaceASCII`
- Does not use the zygote/fork model
- Does not have `setproctitle` or `/proc/self/cmdline`

## Suggested Fix

Use `TrimWhitespace` (or a UTF-8-aware equivalent) instead of `TrimWhitespaceASCII` on POSIX in `base/command_line.cc`. The ASCII-only assumption is incorrect on modern Linux systems where argv can contain arbitrary UTF-8.

## Real-World Impact

This affects any Electron-based CLI tool on Linux that accepts user content as arguments (e.g., note-taking apps, automation tools). Users cannot pass emoji or CJK characters with spaces in command-line arguments without the process hanging.

## Related Reports

- [Obsidian Forum: CLI command hangs with multibyte characters](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/cli-command-hangs-when-creating-notes-with-multibyte-characters-cjk-unicode/111035)
- [Chromium discussion: GPU process fails with multibyte username](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-discuss/c/4OgTFSPxP68)

### Problem Description

For security purposes, we should have a fuse to disable all Node.js flags in production applications.

The more [Node.js flags](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/command-line-switches#nodejs-flags) we expose, the higher the risk. In production apps, you'd usually want to disable all Node.js flags anyways.

### Proposed Solution

Add a fuse to disable all Node.js flags.

Similar to the [`nodeCliInspect` fuse](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/fuses#nodecliinspect), but for _all_ handling of Node.js flags.

### Alternatives Considered

- Not adding any Node.js flags to Electron at all. However, those flags can make development easier.
- Changing the existing `nodeCliInspect` fuse.

### Additional Information

_No response_

No

### Expected Behavior

It should be possible to initialize a child window with a specific `zoomFactor` using the `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` object returned from a window open handler.

### Actual Behavior

Given this window open handler:
``` typescript
mainWindow.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(() => ({
  action: 'allow',
  overrideBrowserWindowOptions: {
    webPreferences: {
      zoomFactor: 2
    }
  }
}))
```
the specified `zoomFactor` doesn't seem to have any effect. Calling `webContents.setZoomFactor()` in `did-create-window` also doesn't work; it seems necessary to wait for a later event like `did-finish-load`.

### Testcase Gist URL

### Additional Information

In the test app, opening a window with `window.open()` uses the default zoom level, while opening one with `new BrowserWindow()` uses the zoom level specified in the constructor options.

Note that after going through the `new BrowserWindow()` path or setting the zoom level manually, the `window.open()` window will continue to use the updated zoom level (so it's not resetting the `zoomLevel` to default, just ignoring it).

title: Wayland: Non-BMP Unicode input truncated (U+1Fxxx → U+Fxxx) when typing via keyboard
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

Bundled with Signal 7.89.0 (see Additional info)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Linux mace.inner.sanctum 6.18.9-200.fc43.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Feb  6 21:43:09 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Typing Unicode characters outside the BMP (e.g. U+1F448 👈, U+1F91F 🤟) via keyboard input should insert the correct Unicode character, as provided by the Wayland input system (UTF-8 text).

### Actual Behavior

When typing certain non-BMP Unicode characters via keyboard input, the resulting character is incorrect and appears truncated:
        Intended: U+1F448 (👈)
        Actual: U+F448 ()
    This pattern is consistent for characters in the U+1Fxxx range, which appear to be truncated to U+Fxxx.
    The issue only occurs with direct keyboard input.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I’m using Signal Desktop 7.89.0 (Flatpak from Flathub), which bundles Electron internally, so I don’t have the exact Electron version available.
However, I have reproduced the same behavior in a standalone Chromium build (RPM, not Flatpak), so this does not appear to be specific to Signal.
---
I investigated this using wev on Wayland and confirmed that the system is producing correct UTF-8 input.

Example:

```
sym: U1F448 (16905288), utf8: '👈'
sym: U1F91F (16906527), utf8: '🤟'
```

This indicates:

- XKB is correctly configured
- libxkbcommon is producing correct Unicode
- Wayland is delivering correct UTF-8 text

Despite this, Electron-based applications appear to ignore the provided UTF-8 and instead derive characters from the keysym, resulting in incorrect truncated codepoints (e.g. U+1F448 → U+F448).

Additional observations:

- Clipboard paste produces correct characters
- Compose sequences produce correct characters
- Only direct key input is affected

This suggests a keysym-to-character conversion path that does not correctly handle non-BMP Unicode.

---
This is my first bug report ever. I hope I did this correctly. I consulted ChatGPT to help me find where and how to tell someone about this. I’m here in good faith, I care about getting this right, and I’m open to correction.
