title: [Bug]: Notification 'click' never emitted on macOS for banners presented while the app is frontmost
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the contributing guide and searched existing issues: no macOS report of this exists (the post-migration notification regressions on file are Windows-only, e.g. #51147, #51650).

### Electron Version

42.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.7.1 (any 41.x — the pre-UNUserNotificationCenter backend)

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a notification banner emits `click` on the `Notification` instance regardless of whether the app is frontmost. This was the behavior of the `NSUserNotification` backend, whose delegate fired `didActivateNotification` on `ContentsClicked` independent of focus (and presented foreground notifications via `shouldPresentNotification: YES`).

### Actual Behavior

Since the migration to `UNUserNotificationCenter` (#47817, shipped in 42), a banner presented while the app is frontmost (via `willPresentNotification` → `Banner | List | Sound` in `shell/browser/notifications/mac/notification_center_delegate.mm`) just dismisses when clicked: macOS never invokes `didReceiveNotificationResponse` for it, so `NotificationClicked()` never runs and no `click` is emitted.

Clicking the same notification while the app is backgrounded or minimized works (the normal delivered-notification activation path).

Ruled out: this is not the garbage-collection issue (#16922) — references are retained — and not the unsigned-build case (the app is code-signed and notifications display and emit `show` normally).

### Testcase Gist URL

Not reproducible in Fiddle: since 42, macOS notification events require a code-signed app. Steps with a signed build:

1. On 42.1.0, while the app window is focused, `new Notification({title: 'x'}).show()` (delayed a few seconds behind a timer) with a `click` listener attached and the reference retained.
2. Click the banner → no `click` event.
3. Same steps with the app unfocused or minimized → `click` fires.
4. Same steps on 41.x → `click` fires in all cases.

### Additional Information

We hit this in production (Basecamp Desktop): users reported notification clicks "doing nothing", exactly and only when the window was active. Downgrading to 41.7.1 restored the old behavior, which is our current mitigation.

Reading the 42-x-y delegate code, the dispatch itself looks correct (`UNNotificationDefaultActionIdentifier` → `NotificationClicked()`, identifier lookup intact) — the response callback simply never arrives from macOS for foreground-presented banners. If that's an OS-level contract of `UNUserNotificationCenter`, it would be worth documenting as a breaking change of the migration; if there's a way to opt foreground banners back into response delivery, even better.

🤖 Drafted with AI assistance; the analysis above was verified against the `42-x-y` sources.

### Expected Behavior
Calling `app.dock.bounce('critical')` once while the app is in the background should bounce the dock icon continuously until the app becomes active or the request is cancelled.

### Actual Behavior
The dock icon bounces continuously for ~1 minute, then visibly drops to ~2 bounces per minute even though the app has not been activated and no focus events fire. Each call succeeds and returns a valid ID. Other apps have reported related bouncing issues (Signal Desktop #652, Mattermost Desktop #693) but report a complete stop rather than throttling — possibly because they do not restart the bounce on an interval as we do.

title: EventTarget.dispatchEvent() silently invokes zero listeners in a renderer when it coincides with a Debugger.pause (breakpoint) transition
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2 x64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

A `"message"` event dispatched via `EventTarget.dispatchEvent()` should always invoke its registered listeners.

### Actual Behavior

In a renderer with `nodeIntegration: true`, when `dispatchEvent()` is called **from a Node.js `net` socket `'data'` callback** and the call **coincides with the V8 inspector transitioning into a paused state** (a breakpoint being hit, or `Debugger.pause` via DevTools / the DevTools Protocol), `dispatchEvent()`:

- returns `true` (i.e. runs to completion), but
- **invokes none of the registered listeners** — even listeners that are never removed,

while a **plain function call on the very next line still executes**. So the JS thread is not frozen; specifically the *listener-invocation* step inside `dispatchEvent` is skipped.

Observed log (the anomaly always lands immediately after a pause is issued):

```
[main] Debugger.pause #857
[renderer] *** ANOMALY *** msg-17032: dispatchEvent returned notCanceled=true, but EventTarget listeners did NOT run (internal=false, external=false); plain callback ran=true. [message #17032]
```

- `notCanceled=true` — the dispatch algorithm completed normally.
- `internal=false external=false` — neither registered `"message"` listener ran (no `removeEventListener` is ever called; tracked listener count stays at 2).
- `plain callback ran=true` — the direct `onMessage(msg)` call on the next line executed.

This was originally hit in a real app where protobuf messages arriving over a socket were decoded and "dispatched" but the registered handlers never ran — **only while debugging with breakpoints**. It is intermittent: the drop happens only when a `dispatchEvent` call lands on a pause transition (observed anywhere from ~40 to ~860 pauses into a run).


### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/rconde01/electron-intermittent-dispatch-event-bug

### Additional Information

### How to run

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

The app opens a hidden renderer (`nodeIntegration: true`, `contextIsolation: false`) running a `MessageSocket extends EventTarget` pipe **server**; the main process streams length-prefixed messages to it and repeatedly issues `Debugger.pause`/`Debugger.resume` via `webContents.debugger`. For each message the renderer dispatches a `CustomEvent` and also calls a plain callback, then reports an `*** ANOMALY ***` if `dispatchEvent` returned but the listeners didn't run. It exits `0` and prints `REPRODUCED: …` on the first anomaly, or exits `1` after the timeout.

It is timing-sensitive — **if a run times out, run it again** (a clean run does not mean the bug is absent). Tunables are at the top of `main.js`.

## Additional Information

### It is not a V8/Node bug — it requires Blink

A pure-Node control (`node-only/` in the testcase) runs the identical logic — a `net` server, `class … extends EventTarget`, `dispatchEvent` per message — with a Worker thread driving the V8 inspector against the main thread (`inspector.Session.connectToMainThread()` + `Debugger.pause`/`resume`). Run under Electron's own bundled Node via `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` — i.e. **the same V8 build (14.8) as the failing renderer, without Blink** — it does **not** reproduce:

| Configuration | V8 | Real main-thread pauses | Ano

title: Support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

[Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)](https://blog.google/security/protecting-cookies-with-device-bound-session-credentials/) is a Chromium feature that binds session cookies to a device-specific cryptographic key, mitigating cookie theft. DBSC shipped as enabled-by-default in Chromium 150, and works correctly in Chrome Dev (currently Chromium 151).

However, DBSC does not appear to function in Electron 43.0.0-beta.1 (which bundles Chromium 150). When a server responds with a `Secure-Session-Registration` header, Electron never initiates the DBSC registration flow; i.e., no request is made to the server's registration endpoint. The "Device bound sessions" panel present in Chrome Dev's DevTools (Application tab) is also absent in Electron's DevTools. The feature appears to be entirely non-functional.

I've tested both with and without explicit feature flags (`--enable-features=DeviceBoundSessions,DeviceBoundSessionsDevTools,EnableBoundSessionCredentialsSoftwareKeysForManualTesting,PersistDeviceBoundSessions`) with no change in behavior. The same server setup works correctly in Chrome Dev, where the registration endpoint is called and the session is bound as expected.

Environment:
- Electron 43.0.0-beta.1
- macOS Tahoe 26.5

### Proposed Solution

Enable DBSC support in Electron, matching the behavior of Chromium 150+. Specifically:
- Honor `Secure-Session-Registration` and `Secure-Session-Challenge` response headers to initiate the registration and refresh flows.
- Create and manage device-bound keys via the platform's secure key storage (Secure Enclave on macOS, TPM on Windows).
- Include `Sec-Secure-Session-Id` and `Secure-Session-Response` headers on subsequent requests for bound sessions.

Ideally this would work out of the box, as it does in Chrome, without requiring feature flags.

### Alternatives Considered

- Enabling via Chromium feature flags: Attempted with both Electron 42 and 43 using various combinations of `--enable-features flags`. No effect.
- Implementing session binding at the application level: This would require managing cryptographic keys and intercepting network requests manually, defeating the purpose of a browser-native solution and losing the security guarantees of platform-level key storage.

### Additional Information

- DBSC is particularly relevant for Electron apps that handle sensitive authenticated sessions, as it provides protection against cookie theft/exfiltration attacks.
- It's unclear whether DBSC is intentionally excluded from Electron's Chromium build or unintentionally non-functional. Any guidance on status or planned support would be appreciated.

title: BrowserWindow 'ready-to-show' never emitted when webContents.setZoomFactor() is called on a hidden window before first paint (regression in 40.x)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.4.0 (also reproduces on 41.7.2 and 40.10.3)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.8.10

### Expected Behavior

A `BrowserWindow` created with `show: false` emits `ready-to-show` after the renderer's first paint, even if `webContents.setZoomFactor()` is called on the still-hidden window shortly after `did-finish-load` — this worked on Electron ≤ 39.

### Actual Behavior

When `webContents.setZoomFactor()` is called on a hidden (`show: false`) window in the gap between `did-finish-load` and the window's first paint, **`ready-to-show` is never emitted** — the window stays invisible forever. This happens **even when the new zoom factor is identical to the current one** (i.e. a semantic no-op call; in our case the same value that was already passed as `webPreferences.zoomFactor`).

Observed state while stuck:

- `did-finish-load` fires normally
- `webContents.isLoading()` → `false`, `isCrashed()` → `false`, page title set, renderer fully interactive
- `win.isVisible()` → `false`, `ready-to-show` listener never invoked (verified registered before `loadFile`)
- Calling `win.show()` manually works fine and shows correct content

Version matrix (identical app code, only the Electron binary swapped):

| Electron | ready-to-show | window visible |
|---|---|---|
| 39.8.10 | emitted | yes |
| 40.10.3 | never | **no** |
| 41.7.2 | never | **no** |
| 42.4.0 | never | **no** |

So the regression was introduced in 40.x.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_ — the suppression is timing-sensitive: in a bare `main.js` with a trivial or even artificially heavy page, calling `setZoomFactor()` synchronously in `did-finish-load` or via `setTimeout(0–200ms)` did **not** reproduce; the real-world trigger is a renderer that calls a zoom IPC during its framework boot (the call lands after `did-finish-load` but before the hidden window's first compositor frame). A reliable public reproduction with exact steps is below; happy to help narrow this down to a Fiddle.

### Additional Information

Reliable reproduction with a small open-source app (MIT):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher
cd SimLauncher
git checkout v0.9.10          # last release before our workaround; package.json pins electron ^39
npm install
npm run build
npx electron out/main/index.js     # Electron 39: window appears
npm install -D electron@42.4.0
npx install-electron
npx electron out/main/index.js     # Electron 42: window NEVER appears
```

The trigger inside the app: the renderer's boot calls a `set-zoom` IPC whose handler runs `webContents.setZoomFactor(factor)` on the still-hidden window ([`src/main/ipc/config.ts`, `set-zoom` handler](https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher/blob/v0.9.10/src/main/ipc/config.ts)). The factor equals the construction-time `webPreferences.zoomFactor` (both read the same persisted store), so the call is a no-op value-wise. Commenting out that single `setZoomFactor` line makes `ready-to-show` fire normally on 40–42; restoring it suppresses the event again — bisected via env-flag toggles of individual boot steps, this one line is the sole trigger.

Workaround we shipped (works): skip same-value `setZoomFactor` calls, plus a `did-finish-load` + timeout fallback that shows the window if `ready-to-show` never arrives — https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher/pull/487.

User impact before the workaround: app "starts minimized"/invisible reports from production

title: Attempting to show a message box segfaults when using Qt backend
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux (X11, KDE Plasma 6)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Showing a message box should work with both GTK and Qt backends.

### Actual Behavior

When Electron/Chromium is built with `use_qt6=true` ([as Arch Linux does](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/electron42/-/blob/42.3.0-1/PKGBUILD?ref_type=tags#L613)), attempting to show a message box in Electron segfaults when Chromium uses its Qt backend, which it does by default on KDE. Forcing the GTK backend with `--ui-toolkit=gtk` works around the issue. This does not affect upstream binaries as Electron [defaults to](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.4.0/build/args/all.gn#L50-L52) `use_qt5 = false` and `use_qt6 = false`.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The issue can be reproduced with the following code:
```js
const { dialog } = require("electron");
dialog.showMessageBox({ message: "test" });
```

I believe it is caused by [this cast](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.4.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_gtk.cc#L47) in `GetGtkUiPlatform`  which assumes `linux_ui` always points to a `GtkUi` instance. The function then calls `GtkUi::GetPlatform` on that object to get `GtkUiPlatform* platform`. I have determined with gdb that the segfault happens on [this line](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/148.0.7778.180/ui/gtk/gtk_util.cc#L214) in Chromium's `gtk::SetGtkTransientForAura` ([called here](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.3.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_gtk.cc#L121-L122) in the `GtkMessageBox` constructor) when it tries to call `platform->SetGtkWidgetTransientFor`. Since `platform` is not actually a `GtkUiPlatform` pointer, this tries to jump to an invalid address leading to a segfault.

title: requestSingleInstanceLock(additionalData): second instance gets the lock and SIGKILLs the first when additionalData.argv has ≥9 elements
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (build 25F80)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A second app instance that calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock(additionalData)
should always return false, exit, and cause the first (already-running) instance
to receive the 'second-instance' event, regardless of how many elements
additionalData.argv contains. The first instance should keep running.


### Actual Behavior

When additionalData carries an argv array with 9 or more elements:

- The SECOND instance gets `requestSingleInstanceLock() === true` so both
  instances believe they hold the lock.
- The FIRST (running) instance is SIGKILLed. The events 'before-quit'/'will-quit'/'quit'
don't fire, and no crash report is generated.

The first instance logs:

  [ERROR:chrome/browser/process_singleton_posix.cc:779] additional_data_size exceeds payload length
  <electron path> exited with signal SIGKILL

With 8 or fewer argv elements everything works fine. But 9 or more causes this behavior.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Can't repro via Electron fiddle because repro requires 2 instances.

package.json
```
{ 
  "name": "esb", 
  "version": "1.0.0", 
  "main": "main.js" 
}
```

main.js
```
const { app } = require('electron')

const extra = process.argv.slice(2) // trailing CLI args -> additionalData.argv

const gotLock = app.requestSingleInstanceLock({ argv: extra })

console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] lock => ${gotLock} (additionalData.argv length = ${extra.length})`)

app.on('before-quit', () => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] before-quit`))

app.on('second-instance', () => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] second-instance (correct)`))

if (!gotLock) { 
  app.quit() 
}
else { 
  app.whenReady().then(() => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] primary ready`)); 
  setInterval(() => {}, 1 << 30) 
}
```

### Electron Version

41.0.0 through 42.4.1 (latest stable at time of filing). Also reproduces on v43.0.0-alpha.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Window 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.8.5 (and the rest of the 40.x line) for the duplexMode / printBackground options. See the separate note below on default-duplex inheritance, which is longstanding.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

For `webContents.print()` (silent path):

- Passing `duplexMode: 'longEdge' | 'shortEdge' | 'simplex'` should take effect.
- Passing `printBackground: true` should print background graphics.
- This is how 40.x behaves.
- Also, omitting `duplexMode` should letting the printer/driver default duplex apply during silent printing


### Actual Behavior

Since 41.0.0, in `webContents.print()`:

1. An explicitly supplied `duplexMode` is **ignored** — the job always prints simplex.
2. An explicitly supplied `printBackground` is **ignored** — backgrounds are never printed.

(Both options still work in `printToPDF()`, which is a different, separately-normalized code path.)

3. `duplexMode` defaulting to simplex when no value is supplied. There is no way to request "use the printer's configured default."

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Root Cause

In `shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc`, `WebContents::Print` reads several caller options out of the JS `options` dictionary using Chromium's internal **print-settings key constants** instead of the public JS option names.

The JS layer does not rename options: `WebContents.prototype.print` in `lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts` passes the caller's `options` object straight to the native `_print` binding (only `pageSize` is transformed into `mediaSize`). So native receives the public names, e.g. `duplexMode` and `printBackground`.

Most option reads survive only because the Chromium key string coincidentally equals the JS option name:

| JS option | native reads under | string value | matches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `printing::kSettingColor` | `"color"` | yes |
| `landscape` | `printing::kSettingLandscape` | `"landscape"` | yes |
| `deviceName` | `printing::kSettingDeviceName` | `"deviceName"` | yes |
| `scaleFactor` | `printing::kSettingScaleFactor` | `"scaleFactor"` | yes |
| `pagesPerSheet` | `printing::kSettingPagesPerSheet` | `"pagesPerSheet"` | yes |
| `collate` | `printing::kSettingCollate` | `"collate"` | yes |
| `copies` | `printing::kSettingCopies` | `"copies"` | yes |
| **`duplexMode`** | `printing::kSettingDuplexMode` | **`"duplex"`** | **no** |
| **`printBackground`** | `printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds` | **`"shouldPrintBackgrounds"`** | **no** |

The string values are from Chromium `printing/print_job_constants.cc`.

Because the JS object never contains a `"duplex"` or `"shouldPrintBackgrounds"` key, those two reads never match and always return their fallbacks (`kSimplex` / `false`), which are then written into the settings.

**40.8.5 (working):**

```cpp

const auto duplex_mode = options.ValueOrDefault(
    "duplexMode", printing::mojom::DuplexMode::kSimplex);
settings.Set(printing::kSettingDuplexMode, static_cast<int>(duplex_mode));
```

**41.0.0+ (broken):**

```cpp
// Duplex type user wants to use.
const auto duplex_mode = options.ValueOrDefault(

      )

_No response_

This is a problem I hit with the Flatpak version of Signal when saving files through
the Linux file-chooser portal — it looks like it can be fixed in Electron's Linux
dialog code (details below). Reproduced with the LXQt portal backend, but the
malformed request is sent regardless of backend.

This report was drafted with AI assistance; the `dbus-monitor` capture is from my
own machine and the code references point to the linked diffs, so it can all be
verified directly.

## Summary

On Linux, `dialog.showSaveDialog` / `dialog.showOpenDialog` with a **directory-less
`defaultPath`** (a bare filename — which the docs explicitly permit) sends
`current_folder="."` in the xdg-desktop-portal `SaveFile` request. The relative `.`
is not a usable directory: the dialog opens at a broken location (shown as
`file:.`), and on stricter portal backends the suggested filename is dropped too.
macOS and Windows handle the identical input correctly.

## Platform

- Linux, Wayland
- xdg-desktop-portal FileChooser interface v4
- Reproduced with the LXQt portal backend (empty filename **and** `file:.`). The
  malformed `current_folder="."` is produced by Electron/Chromium and sent to

Minimal main-process snippet:

```js

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  // bare filename, no directory — allowed per the docs

### Electron Version

37.10.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test.

This uses Electron's `BrowserWindow` API (`enableLargerThanScreen`, `showInactive`, `setBounds`, `getBounds`) and I do not know of a direct equivalent surface in Google Chrome to create a transparent frameless native window spanning arbitrary display bounds.

### Expected Behavior

A frameless transparent `BrowserWindow` created with valid virtual-screen bounds should remain at the requested bounds after being shown.

In the repro environment, `screen.getAllDisplays()` reports this layout:

```text
Primary built-in Retina display: bounds { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1512, height: 982 }, scaleFactor: 2
External display A:             bounds { x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 2560, height: 1440 }, scaleFactor: 1
External display B:             bounds { x: 800, y: -1440, width: 2560, height: 1440 }, scaleFactor: 1
```

The virtual display union is:

```text
{ x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
```

After creating and showing a single `BrowserWindow` at that union rectangle, `win.getBounds()` should continue to report:

```text
{ x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
```

The same should hold after explicitly reapplying the same bounds with `setBounds()` while the window is already visible.

### Actual Behavior

The window initially reports the requested bounds correctly. Shortly after `showInactive()` emits `show`, Electron emits a native `move`/`moved` event and `getBounds()` jumps to a different position while preserving width/height:

```text
requested: { x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
actual:    { x: -3520, y: -2422, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
```

Example output from the standalone repro:

```text
PROBE before-showInactive {"t":152,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE after-showInactive {"t":152,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE event-show {"t":163,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE event-move {"t":208,"bounds":{"x":-3520,"y":-2422,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-3520,-2422]}
PROBE event-moved {"t":208,"bounds":{"x":-3520,"y":-2422,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-3520,-2422]}
```

This is not caused by app code reapplying incorrect bounds. In `PROBE_MODE=passive`, the script does not call `setBounds()` after `showInactive()`, but the native `move` event still occurs.

If the correct bounds are explicitly reapplied after the window is already visible, the synchronous read-back is correct, then the same delayed native move happens again:

```text
PROBE after-reapply-1500ms {"t":1675,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE event-move {"t":1783,"bounds":{"x":-3520,"y":-2422,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-3520,-2422]}
```

No `display-metrics-changed` event fires during the move.

The trigger appears to be a single frameless window spanning the seam between display rows with different `scaleFactor` values: the external displays are above the primary display (`y < 0`, scale factor 1), while the primary Retina display starts at `y = 0` (scale factor 2). title: [Feature Request]: Allow customization of `chrome.*` extension APIs
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The [Electron docs](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/extensions) explicitly state it's a non-goal to support all extension capabilities. This makes sense, since many APIs (e.g. `chrome.tabs.create()`) don't have a clear representation at the Electron platform level.

But applications should be able to customize these API behaviors to suit their needs and provide richer support for more extensions.

### Proposed Solution

Something like a preload script whereby applications can extend or modify the `chrome.*` APIs to suit their needs. This allows high flexibility for applications to control the behavior while keeping the bulk of the maintenance cost (supporting new APIs etc) off of Electron.

### Alternatives Considered

Expose first-class APIs to register handlers for chrome extension APIs. This gives a clear surface for applications and may allow cleaner implementation (e.g. return a WebContents -> Electron converts it to the `Tab` interface for you) but puts a heavy maintenance burden on Electron.

title: GPU/renderer process crashes with EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT (0x80000003) on Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200.8655) — sandbox init failure, regression after June 2026 cumulative update
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.6.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2, Build 26200.8655 (UBR 8655). Cumulative updates KB5094135 (2026-06-09) and KB5094126 (2026-06-10) installed.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — crashes began 2026-06-16, immediately after the June 2026 cumulative update; the Electron app versions were unchanged across that boundary.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The GPU (and renderer) child process launches normally under the sandbox.

### Actual Behavior

The GPU process is killed by EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT (0x80000003 / exit_code=-2147483645) immediately on launch, **before any GPU vendor DLL is loaded**. The browser process retries 6 times within ~0.3s and then self-terminates.

Browser process log (captured with --enable-logging=stderr --v=1):

​```
[ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:996] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[WARNING:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1438] The GPU process has crashed 1 time(s)
... (repeats up to 6 times) ...
[FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
​```

WER signature: faulting module = the app exe itself (statically-linked Chromium), exception code 80000003, identical fault offset across 70+ crash reports.

**A/B isolation (this is the key evidence):**
- Default (GPU sandbox ON): GPU process dies with 0x80000003, 6 times → browser gives up.
- `--disable-gpu-sandbox`: GPU process **survives** (falls back to swiftshader-webgl). No 0x80000003.
- For Notion, `--disable-gpu-sandbox` keeps the main process alive but the **renderer** still crashes (white screen); only `--no-sandbox` makes the renderer survive.

So: sandbox ON → child process dies during sandbox init; sandbox OFF → it lives. This points to a sandbox-init incompatibility, not a GPU driver fault (no vendor DLL is even loaded at crash time) and not third-party DLL injection (the sandboxed children can't be injected).

Google Chrome 149 on the same machine is unaffected — likely because its newer Chromium already handles the changed Windows behavior.

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU (driver 32.0.15.9174) + AMD Radeon 610M (32.0.13034.7001), hybrid graphics laptop.

title: Drop support for Linux distributions that are EOL
body:
Our docs for Linux support:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f02df6edb4ada66fa3c76c851ffff5fd9a2916cd/README.md?plain=1#L42-L45

For example, [Debian 10](https://www.debian.org/releases/buster/) is EOL. Ubuntu 18 is, too.

Dropping support needs to be done in a major version.

We might want to change our support policy and wording here to say that we support all versions of Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian that are still supported by the disto makers.

That said, we might want to avoid limiting support to specific distributions. Because what about Arch, OpenSUSE, RHEL, etc.?

We might also want to stop mentioning which Ubuntu version our binaries are built on.

### Electron Version

42.4.0; Reproduced in shipping apps on current Electron/Chromium builds (OpenAI Codex, Anthropic Claude desktop).  Codex: Version 26.616.81150 Claude 1.15200.0 (250bae) 2026-06-23T05:40:53.000Z

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (build 26100.8655)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a top-level `BrowserWindow` is hidden in response to a close (e.g. the app intercepts `close` and calls `win.hide()` to keep running in the background), the window should relinquish foreground activation and clear its focused accessibility state. Windows then activates the next window in the Z-order, and that window's process emits `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND`, so assistive technology (Narrator, JAWS, NVDA) follows focus to the new foreground.

### Actual Behavior

On Alt+F4, the window's pixels disappear but it is **hidden, not destroyed**, and it **never relinquishes foreground activation or its focused accessibility state**:

- The top-level window fires `EVENT_OBJECT_HIDE` while still reporting `STATE_SYSTEM_FOCUSED` (state `0x168004`).
- The render-widget child is reparented offscreen (`0x118000`) and moved to the origin.
- No `EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROY` is fired.
- No `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND` to any successor window is fired.
- `GetForegroundWindow()` immediately after the close still returns the now-invisible window's HWND (also visible inline in the events' `ForegroundWnd` field).

Because foreground is never released, Windows never activates a successor, so no process emits a foreground/focus event. Screen readers have nothing to follow and keep reading the closed app. With Narrator, "Say current line" (Insert+Up) still reads the closed window's chat content after the window is gone.

[Bug]: globalShortcut.register() returns true before the Wayland portal bind resolves
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (also 42.5.1 with the portal path enabled via flags)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (GNOME Wayland, gnome-shell 50.1, xdg-desktop-portal 1.21.1)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

On the Linux Wayland portal path, an app can find out whether a `globalShortcut.register()` call actually resulted in a bound shortcut — or at minimum, `register()`/`isRegistered()` should not report success when the portal denied the bind.

### Actual Behavior

On Wayland, `globalShortcut` goes through the `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts` portal (`GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux`). The portal's `BindShortcuts` call is asynchronous and consent-gated (GNOME shows a dialog before binding), so the synchronous boolean returned by `register()` cannot be truthful on this path: `GlobalShortcut::Register()` returns `true` as soon as the command set is handed to the listener via `OnCommandsChanged()`, before the bind resolves. `isRegistered()` is equally misleading — it only consults the local command map.

If the portal later replies with an error — e.g. GNOME 50.0/50.1 rejects `BindShortcuts` for any app id that fails `g_application_id_is_valid()` (see gnome-control-center `global-shortcuts-provider`; relaxed in 50.2), or the user dismisses the consent dialog — the result dies in `GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux::OnBindShortcuts()` as a `LOG(ERROR)`. Nothing reaches `ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener` observers, so Electron has no way to surface it even if it wanted to.

Observed on an Ubuntu 26.04 VM with stock Electron binaries (`GlobalShortcutsPortal` + `GlobalShortcutsPortalPreferredTrigger` enabled):

```
# invalid app id (dashed desktopName, no dot): register() lies, portal denies
20:32:28 REGISTER Control+Shift+F9 -> true
dbus: error_name=org.freedesktop.portal.Error.NotAllowed reply_serial=23
(shortcut never fires, no dialog shown)

# valid reverse-DNS desktopName (com.example.MyApp.desktop): works end to end
20:41:49 REGISTER Control+Shift+F9 -> true
20:44:34 FIRED Control+Shift+F10        # after one consent dialog
20:46:38 REGISTER ... -> true            # relaunch: silent re-bind, persists
```

Apps cannot distinguish three genuinely different states: **bound**, **pending consent**, and **denied**. That matters in practice — "shortcut silently doesn't work" is indistinguishable from "user hasn't clicked the consent dialog yet".

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Surfacing the bind result needs a small Chromium patch: `OnBindShortcuts()` receives the response but `ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener` has no observer/callback for it today.

Proposed minimal API (shape open for discussion): keep `register()` synchronous — its boolean means "request submitted" on this path — and add a module event that fires when the portal resolves the bind:

```js
globalShortcut.on('registration-resolved', (accelerator, bound) => {
  // bound === false: portal denied (invalid app id, user dismissed dialog, ...)
})
```

Alternatives considered: a promise-returning `registerAsync()`, or a callback in an options object. On non-portal platforms the event could fire immediately with the `register()` result, keeping it usable cross-platform.

Draft PR with plumbing to follow; API shape needs API WG input.

title: A configurable build system using a file like electron.config.js
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

While working on several Electron projects, I noticed that many desktop applications don't actually use a large portion of the Chromium features that are included by default.

Applications such as launchers, utilities, configuration tools, local dashboards, media managers, or internal business software often only need the rendering engine and a few web APIs. Features like the built-in PDF viewer, Wallet, Translate, Media Router, and similar browser functionality may never be used, yet they are still bundled with every application.

It would be nice if developers had a way to avoid shipping optional Chromium features that their application doesn't need.

### Proposed Solution

One possible approach would be to introduce a build configuration file, something similar to `electron.config.js`, where developers could enable or disable supported Chromium components before packaging.

For example:

```js
module.exports = {
  chromium: {
    pdfViewer: false,
    wallet: false,
    translate: false,
    mediaRouter: false,
    autofill: false
  }
};
```

If no configuration file is present, Electron would continue to behave exactly as it does today.

Only components that are considered optional and safe to exclude would be configurable. Anything required by Electron or Chromium would simply remain enabled.

### Alternatives Considered

I also thought about having separate Electron distributions, such as a "minimal" build and a "full" build.

However, I think a configuration-based approach would be more flexible. Different applications have different requirements, so allowing developers to choose which optional features they need seems more practical than maintaining multiple Electron distributions.

### Additional Information

I understand that Chromium has many internal dependencies and that not every feature can simply be removed.

The goal isn't to make every Chromium component optional, but to provide a supported way to exclude features that are already considered optional.

Even if only a small number of components could be configured this way, it could still help reduce application size and avoid shipping functionality that some applications will never use.

title: [Bug]: globalShortcut portal path collapses F-key and punctuation accelerators to the same command id
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (any version with the Wayland GlobalShortcuts portal path)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Any Linux Wayland session using the org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts path

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Expected Behavior

Registering two shortcuts like `Ctrl+F9` and `Ctrl+F10` on the Wayland portal path binds two distinct portal shortcuts.

### Actual Behavior

`GlobalShortcut::Register` builds the portal command id from `extensions::Command::AcceleratorToString(accelerator)`, which only supports A–Z, 0–9, comma, period, arrows, Home/End/PgUp/PgDn, Space, Tab, Insert/Delete, and the media keys — everything else (all F-keys, Escape, Enter, most punctuation, numpad) returns an empty string. All such accelerators therefore collapse to the same empty command id and the same fake extension id, colliding in `command_callback_map_` and in the portal session: only the last registered shortcut of that class is actually bound, and its activation runs the last-registered callback.

Observed empirically: registering `Control+Shift+F9` produces a portal command whose id is derived from an empty accelerator string.

### Additional Information

Two possible directions: extend the stringification used for portal command ids to cover all registrable accelerators (needs to stay stable across versions, since the portal persists binds keyed by these ids), or key commands by something independent of the accelerator (with a migration for existing persisted binds). Related plumbing work: #52218.

body:

25H2

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should launch normally.


Maybe duplicate of : https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/52098
https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51761

Affected applications:

* Obsidian 1.12.7
* Signal Desktop 8.17.0
* Discord (latest)

Not affected:

* Visual Studio Code 1.126.0

## Environment

* OS: Windows 11 Pro
* Build: 26200.8737
* GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070
* Driver: 32.0.31021.5001
* Secondary GPU: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics






### Actual Behavior

## Actual Behavior

Multiple Electron applications terminate during startup.

The logs consistently end with:

```text
[FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415]
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

Signal additionally reports repeated GPU process failures before aborting:

```text
GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
```

Windows Event Viewer records Application Error (Event ID 1000) with exception code:

```
0x80000003
```

The faulting module is the application executable itself (e.g. `Obsidian.exe`, `Signal.exe`).

## Reproduction

Launching Obsidian normally:

```powershell
& "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Obsidian\Obsidian.exe"
```

Results in:

* application exits almost immediately
* log ends with `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`

The same behavior is observed with Signal Desktop and Discord.

## Startup Flag Testing

### `--in-process-gpu`

Launching with:

```text
--in-process-gpu
```

changes the behavior:

* the process no longer exits immediately
* however, the application window is not rendered correctly (GUI is missing / blank)

### Four-flag combination

Launching with:

```text
--disable-gpu
--disable-gpu-compositing
--disable-software-rasterizer
--in-process-gpu
```

changes the behavior further.

In Safe Mode, this combination allows the UI to render instead of immediately terminating.

Outside Safe Mode, startup behavior changes, but rendering is still incomplete or absent.

The fact that `--in-process-gpu` consistently changes the failure mode suggests the issue is related to Chromium's GPU process initialization.

## Diagnostics Already Performed

* Updated AMD driver to latest available version
* `sfc /scannow`
* Windows Defender scan
* Malwarebytes scan
* HDR disabled
* Safe Mode testing
* AMD Radeon Software terminated
* DxDiag reports no display or DirectX problems

None of the above resolved the issue.

If there are additional Chromium or Electron logging flags that would help diagnose why the GPU process exits, I would be happy to collect and provide them.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Visual Studio Code launches normally on the same machine.

This suggests the issue is not a complete Electron failure, but may depend on the Electron/Chromium version or GPU initialization path used by different applications.

title: [Bug]: macOS: every keystroke in any input/textarea recreates a native autofill popup NSWindow, blocking the browser process 100-260 ms per key on macOS 26 (worst with CJK IME)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.3 (the relevant code is unchanged on `main`)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — the popup churn exists in all recent versions; it became user-visible on macOS 26, where window ordering waits on synchronous WindowServer transactions.

### Expected Behavior

Typing into an `<input>` or `<textarea>` that has no datalist suggestions should not create or destroy native windows, and should not block the browser process.

### Actual Behavior

Every keystroke that changes the value of a focused `<input>`/`<textarea>` (with the caret at the end) makes the renderer send `ElectronAutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup` **with an empty suggestion list**, and the browser process destroys and recreates a native autofill popup `NSWindow` each time. On macOS 26, each of those window-ordering operations blocks `CrBrowserMain` for 50–350 ms in a synchronous WindowServer transaction. Since `CrBrowserMain` routes all input events, **every window and input of the app stutters**.

CJK IME users are hit hardest: apps that type into a hidden textarea (e.g. xterm.js terminals) never change the textarea value for plain keys (keydown is `preventDefault()`ed), but **IME preedit lives in the textarea and changes its value on every keystroke** — so composition triggers the churn on every key. This was discovered while investigating Japanese-IME typing jank in [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) (an Electron-based terminal/agent app), where the jank affects the whole UI while composing.

Root cause chain (all verified):

1. **Renderer** — `AutofillAgent::ShowSuggestions` (`shell/renderer/electron_autofill_agent.cc`) reaches `ShowPopup(element, {}, {})` for any editable with a non-empty value and caret at end, **even when there are zero datalist suggestions** — including `<textarea>`, which can never have any. `TextFieldValueChanged` fires per keystroke (and per `compositionupdate` during IME composition).
2. **Browser** — `AutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup` (`shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver.cc`) calls `AutofillPopup::CreateView` (`shell/browser/ui/autofill_popup.cc`), which unconditionally `Hide()`s the previous popup and creates + shows a new native child window — even for an empty list. Net effect: one NSWindow destroy + create + order-in per keystroke.
3. **macOS 26** — `sample(1)` of the browser process during typing shows `CrBrowserMain` blocked in:

   ```text
   -[NSWindow _doOrderWindow:]
     -[NSCGSWindow(NSCGSWindowOrdering) isOrderedIn]
       SLSWindowIsOrderedIn (SkyLight)
         SLSConnectionSynchronizeSLSCATransaction
           _SLSTransactionWaitSource → mach_msg2_trap   ← 1961 of 2006 samples
   ```

Evidence from a real 90 s Japanese-typing session in Orca (`devtools.timeline` + `toplevel` + `latencyInfo` trace): 74 `Receive mojo message` tasks ≥ 30 ms tagged `electron.mojom.ElectronAutofillDriver` on `CrBrowserMain`, totalling **10.1 s** with a **263 ms** max; 15 of 23 keydowns with > 100 ms `InputLatency::RawKeyDown` overlapped one of those tasks. Renderer-side handlers took 1–2 ms — the latency is entirely browser-process dispatch delay.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/hirorocky/82b35c2604e29b80883921b806a711ac

### Additional Information

The testcase needs no IME: it synthesizes composition updates via `webContents.debugger` (`Input.imeSetComposition`) into

title: Allow monospaced digit fonts for menu item labels on macOS
body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description On macOS, menu item labels are rendered with the system menu font, whose digits are proportional. So any menu showing a column of numbers comes out jagged, because e.g. `11:15` renders narrower than `09:45`: There's currently no way around this: `MenuItem.label` maps to `NSMenuItem.title`, and Electron exposes neither `attributedTitle` nor any font option. In a native app this is a one-liner: set `attributedTitle` with `monospacedDigitSystemFontOfSize:`, the SF variant with tabular figures that's otherwise identical to the menu font. #22363 solved the same problem for the tray title with `tray.setTitle(title, { fontType: 'monospacedDigit' })`. Menu item labels never got the equivalent, so a tray calendar can align its countdown but not the time column in its dropdown. ### Proposed Solution The same `fontType` option on `MenuItem`, macOS-only like `toolTip`: ```js new MenuItem({ label: "11:15 Doctor's appointment", fontType: 'monospacedDigit' }) ``` The implementation looks small: when the option is set, `electron_menu_controller.mm` renders the label via `attributedTitle` with the corresponding font variant, analogous to the `fontType` handling in `tray_icon_cocoa.mm`. Supporting both tray values (`monospaced` and `monospacedDigit`) keeps the two APIs symmetric. ### Alternatives Considered - Padding with figure spaces (U+2007): Still unequal widths, the digits themselves are proportional - Unicode fullwidth/monospace digits: Wrong font, looks out of place - Pre-rendering the time column into template `NativeImage` icons: What we ship today – works well, but adds a lot of machinery for one line of AppKit ### Additional Information I attached [menu-item-font-type.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29671470/menu-item-font-type.patch) mirroring the `toolTip` per-item plumbing and the tray `fontType` implementation. It was drafted with Claude Fable 5, and I'm currently unable to build Electron locally – so it's untested. Happy to open a PR from it so CI can validate it, or for a maintainer to adopt or rework it instead.

title: [Bug]: chrome.webRequest is schema-registered but has no bindings in MV3 service workers, crashing worker registration
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

An MV3 extension with the `webRequest` permission can register observational listeners (e.g. `chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.addListener(...)`) in its background service worker, as it can in Chrome.

### Actual Behavior

The `webRequest` API feature/schema is registered — `typeof chrome.webRequest === 'object'` inside the worker — but the renderer bindings module resources are missing from the resource bundle:

```
ERROR:extensions/renderer/resource_bundle_source_map.cc:72] NOTREACHED hit. Module resource registered as "webRequest" not found
ERROR:extensions/renderer/resource_bundle_source_map.cc:72] NOTREACHED hit. Module resource registered as "webRequestEvent" not found
"(BLESSED_EXTENSION context for <id>) No source for require(webRequest)"
```

As a result `chrome.webRequest` is an empty object, `chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` is `undefined`, the worker throws at top level, and MV3 service worker registration fails entirely:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'addListener')
Service worker registration failed. Status code: 15
```

Because the registration failure takes the whole worker down, any real-world extension whose worker touches `chrome.webRequest` at startup is completely non-functional (observed with NordPass, whose action button is driven by its worker). This half-registered state is arguably worse than the API being absent — extensions that feature-detect `chrome.webRequest` pass the check and then crash.

Full log: see the gist.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/dep/ec59df61562cfb3af21031a660e733b4

### Additional Information

- Follow-up to the MV3 support push in #37876 (https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/37876#issuecomment-1656808686) — service worker registration, `chrome.scripting`, and `chrome.tabs` all work great now; `chrome.webRequest` appears to be the next-most-impactful gap for MV3 extensions.
- `chrome.declarativeNetRequest` is entirely `undefined` in the same context (expected, since it is not on the supported-API list, but noting it since MV3 network-observing extensions typically need one of the two).
- Prior art: #2115 (2016 request for `chrome.webRequest.*`, closed), #19447 (//extensions integration tracking issue, closed).
- Two plausible resolutions from the outside: (a) pack the `webRequest`/`webRequestEvent` custom-bindings resources and wire the browser-side `WebRequestAPI`/event router so the API actually works, or (b) stop registering the schema so the API is cleanly absent and feature-detection in extensions behaves. (a) is obviously the dream. 🙏

title: [Bug]: macOS main process crashes with NSInvalidArgumentException when notification icon attachment creation fails
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.5.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41 (any version before the UserNotifications framework rewrite in #47817)

### Expected Behavior

If creating the `UNNotificationAttachment` for the notification icon fails (e.g. the image cannot be persisted to disk), the notification should be delivered without the icon, and the app should not crash.

### Actual Behavior

The browser process crashes with an uncaught Objective-C exception before the notification is delivered:

```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException',
reason: '*** -[__NSPlaceholderArray initWithObjects:count:]: attempt to insert nil object from objects[0]'

Thread 0 Crashed (CrBrowserMain):
  +[NSArray arrayWithObjects:count:]
  Electron Framework ...
  __CFRUNLOOP_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_SOURCE0_PERFORM_FUNCTION__
  ...
  NSApplicationUncaughtExceptionHandler → SIGTRAP (exit code 133)
```

**Root cause** — in [`shell/browser/notifications/mac/cocoa_notification.mm`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.5.2/shell/browser/notifications/mac/cocoa_notification.mm), the attachment factory (image task runner) explicitly returns `nil` on failure:

```objc
return (attachment && !error) ? attachment : nil;
```

…but the reply callback on the UI thread uses the result without a nil check:

```objc
content.attachments = @[ attachment ];  // @[nil] → NSInvalidArgumentException
```

`NotificationImageRetainer::RegisterTemporaryImage` writes the icon under `<user data dir>/Notification Resources/`; any I/O failure there (`CreateDirectory` / `CreateTemporaryFileInDir` / `WriteFile`), or `+[UNNotificationAttachment attachmentWithIdentifier:URL:options:error:]` returning an error, produces the `nil` that crashes the process.

We captured two production crashes of our app with identical stacks at this location (long-running instance in the background; an incoming message triggered a notification with an icon), and then reproduced it deterministically.

This is a regression from the UserNotifications framework rewrite in #47817 (first shipped in v42); the pre-rewrite `NSUserNotification` path used `setContentImage:` and had no attachment array. The code on `main` is unchanged and has the same problem.

I'm happy to submit a PR — the fix is a nil-guard that falls back to delivering the notification without the attachment.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/litujia1007/0cffd6eacaf21fb5d9b7c3f248af8936

### Additional Information

The gist is deterministic: it occupies the `<userData>/Notification Resources` path with a plain file so the image retainer's `CreateDirectory` fails, then shows a notification with an icon. On 42.5.2 (darwin/arm64) it crashes with the exception above before delivery (exit code 133). Removing the `icon` option makes the exact same scenario survive.

title: [Feature Request]: per-session opt-out for the Touch ID WebAuthn platform authenticator
body:
# Feature Request: per-session opt-out for the Touch ID WebAuthn platform authenticator

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`app.configureWebAuthn({ touchID: { keychainAccessGroup } })` enables the macOS Touch ID platform authenticator globally: `ElectronWebAuthenticationDelegate::GetTouchIdAuthenticatorConfig` reads a static access group, so every `Session` — including non-persistent ones — gets a working platform authenticator.

The credential *metadata secret*, however, is per-`BrowserContext`: it's read from (or generated into) the context's `PrefService` (`shell/browser/webauthn/electron_authenticator_request_delegate.cc`). For an in-memory session (`session.fromPartition('private')` without `persist:`), that secret is regenerated on every launch. The result for a browser-style app with private/incognito windows:

- A passkey **created** in the non-persistent session is written to the Secure Enclave / keychain permanently, but its metadata can never be unsealed after the app quits — the credential is orphaned forever, and the keychain item leaks (accumulates) with no way for the site or user to know.
- The UX is silently broken: the ceremony succeeds, the site believes the user has a passkey, and after relaunch sign-in fails with no explanation.

Apps can't defend against this today:

- The access group is app-global static state — there is no per-session configuration, so a private session can't be excluded.
- Renderer-side interception of `navigator.credentials.create()` is bypassable and wrong-layer.
- Calling `app.configureWebAuthn({})` dynamically around private-session requests would race concurrent normal-session ceremonies.

### Proposed Solution

Any of these would solve it (in rough order of preference):

1. A per-session switch, e.g. `session.setWebAuthnTouchIdEnabled(false)` or an option on `fromPartition`, honored by returning `std::nullopt` from `GetTouchIdAuthenticatorConfig` for that context.
2. `app.configureWebAuthn` accepting a session filter/predicate.
3. At minimum: skip the Touch ID authenticator for contexts whose `PrefService` is in-memory (i.e. never able to persist the metadata secret), or document the hazard in the `configureWebAuthn` docs.

### Alternatives Considered

Documented the behavior to users as "passkeys created in private tabs are lost on quit" (shipping that today), but the orphaned Secure Enclave keychain items still accumulate and the site-side UX remains misleading.

### Additional Information

Observed on Electron 43.1.0 in a browser shell (one default session + one non-persistent session for private tabs), macOS, signed build with the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement + embedded Developer ID provisioning profile. Happy to PR this if maintainers agree on the API shape.

43.1.0

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When no locale data is available for the app's target locale, Electron should either log a clear diagnostic (e.g. `Error: No locale file found for "en"`) before the renderer fails, or surface a specific reason via `render-process-gone` — not fail silently with only a bare exit code.

### Actual Behavior

The app crashes on launch with only this single line printed to console:
```text
RENDERER GONE: crashed -1073741819
```
No stack trace, no `uncaughtException`, no additional detail from `render-process-gone`, and nothing else logged from the main process. After extensive testing, this is confirmed to be the *only* output ever produced under this failure mode.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This isn't a bug in application code, so it isn't reproducible as an Electron Fiddle gist. It surfaces from a *packaging-time* misconfiguration: `electron-builder` accepts an invalid `electronLanguages` value (`["en"]` instead of `["en-US"]`) and silently ships a build with an empty `locales/` directory, with no error or warning at build time. That's tracked as a bundler-side bug here: [electron-userland/electron-builder#10006](https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/10006).

This issue is scoped specifically to Electron's *runtime* behavior once that state exists: when `locales/` is empty, the app crashes with no diagnostic information whatsoever, regardless of how it got that way (bad bundler config, manual deletion, corrupted install, etc.). Since the failure mode is state-based rather than code-based, the clearest minimal repro is a standalone project rather than a Fiddle:

https://github.com/poran-dip/electron-crash

Steps: 
1. `git clone https://github.com/poran-dip/electron-crash.git`
2. `pnpm install`
3. `pnpm build`
4. run the packaged app
5. observe the crash with no console output beyond the exit code.

Exit code `-1073741819` corresponds to `0xC0000005` (STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION), suggesting a native-level crash when the renderer attempts to read nonexistent locale data, rather than a graceful failure.

Environment:
- Electron: 43.1.0
- Windows 11, version 25H2 (build 10.0.26200)
- node: 24.18.0

title: WebFrameMain.postMessage throws synchronously on disposed frame — asymmetric with send()/executeJavaScript, no 'destroyed' event lets consumers unsubscribe
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

30+

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 22H2, build 19045.6466

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not applicable — bug is architectural (contract asymmetry). PR #31401 is a partial mitigation for the sticky-disposed sub-case only

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`WebFrameMain.postMessage`, sync property accessors, and `executeJavaScript` on a disposed frame should degrade **uniformly** — either all silently drop (parity with `send()`), or all reject a promise, or all fire a JS-visible event that lets defensive consumers unsubscribe before the next microtask can dispatch. Whichever is chosen, the same disposed frame should not produce three different failure modes across three call sites in the same JS session.

Additionally: a `WebFrameMain` should emit a `'frame-disposed'` (or `'destroyed'`) event when `MarkRenderFrameDisposed()` runs, giving RxJS pipelines a `takeUntil(fromEvent(frame, 'frame-disposed'))` primitive that closes the race at the app-code layer without TOCTOU-vulnerable polling.

### Actual Behavior

`postMessage` and every sync accessor throw the exact string `"Render frame was disposed before WebFrameMain could be accessed"` via `gin_helper::ErrorThrower::ThrowError()`. The JS wrapper for `postMessage` in `lib/browser/api/web-frame-main.ts` has no try/catch (`send()` does, `postMessage` doesn't). The throw escapes the caller's callback, and in the RxJS-pipeline case tears down the subscription that fed the UI, producing a permanently blank Docker Desktop dashboard while the engine backend runs normally.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Summary

`WebFrameMain.prototype.postMessage` throws a synchronous V8 exception (`"Render frame was disposed before WebFrameMain could be accessed"`) when a caller-held wrapper is dispatched to after the underlying `RenderFrameHost` has been disposed. The throw is undefendable from downstream code because:

1. The disposal contract is **asymmetric** across the WebFrameMain API surface:
   - `send()` swallows the throw into `console.error` (JS-wrapper try/catch)
   - `postMessage()` propagates
   - `executeJavaScript()` rejects a promise
   - Sync accessors (`.url`, `.origin`, `.processId`, `.frameToken`, `.name`, `.routingId`, `.top`, `.parent`, `.frames`, `.framesInSubtree`, `.visibilityState`, `.osProcessId`) throw synchronously
2. No JS-visible `'destroyed'` / `'disposed'` event fires on the WebFrameMain instance — `MarkRenderFrameDisposed()` only flips a bool + tears down the Mojo pipe. Downstream consumers have no first-class signal to unsubscribe on; `isDestroyed()` is TOCTOU on the UI thread that also runs `MarkRenderFrameDisposed`.
3. Consequence: any consumer that captures a `WebFrameMain` reference and dispatches to it from a delayed callback (RxJS `debounceTime`/`auditTime`/`delay`/`observeOn(asapScheduler)`, `mergeMap`/`switchMap` over async work, `setTimeout`, promise continuation) is guaranteed to hit `CheckRenderFrame()` on a stale wrapper whenever the RFH turned over in between. The throw propagates out of the callback and tears down its host subscription/observer — for RxJS, the subscription transitions to `_error` and the source is unsubscribed forever, wedging any UI dependent on that pipeline in an empty state.

title: Renderer CHECK crash in blink::V8MetricsRecorder::GetUkmRecorderAndSourceId during full GC when a service-worker preload realm context exists (MV3 extension SW)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.5.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.0.1 (25A362), arm64

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_Unknown — likely none since service-worker preload realms were introduced_

### Expected Behavior

A renderer process hosting a chrome-extension MV3 background service worker, with a service-worker preload script registered via `session.registerPreloadScript({ type: 'service-worker', ... })`, survives V8 full GC cycles.

### Actual Behavior

The renderer crashes with `EXC_BREAKPOINT` (CHECK failure) whenever a **full GC cycle** completes in the service-worker isolate while the Electron **service-worker preload realm context** is among the isolate's contexts. In our production browser (bundled MV3 extension whose SW does frequent `ipcRenderer.invoke` work) this reproduces reliably within minutes-to-hours of browsing; we have a series of Crashpad minidumps, all identical.

Symbolicated crashing stack (Electron 42.5.2 dSYM, Chromium 148.0.7778.271), innermost first:

```
0  <ICF-deduplicated function>                                  (crash, EXC_BREAKPOINT)
1  blink::V8MetricsRecorder::GetUkmRecorderAndSourceId          v8_metrics.cc:662
2  blink::V8MetricsRecorder::AddMainThreadEvent(v8::metrics::GarbageCollectionFullCycle const&, ContextId)
3  v8::internal::GCTracer::StopCycle
4  v8::internal::GCTracer::NotifyFullSweepingCompletedAndStopCycleIfFinished
5  v8::internal::Heap::EnsureSweepingCompleted
6  v8::internal::Heap::CollectGarbage
7  v8::internal::HeapAllocator::CollectGarbageAndRetryAllocation
8  v8::internal::HeapAllocator::AllocateRawSlowPath
9  v8::internal::Factory::NewJSObject / NewJSPromiseWithoutHook
10 v8::Promise::Resolver::New
11 gin_helper::PromiseBase::PromiseBase                          promise.cc:66
12 (anonymous namespace)::IPCBase<IPCServiceWorker>::Invoke      (electron_api_ipc SW binding)
```

The renderer command line includes `--service-worker-preload`.

### Analysis

`V8MetricsRecorder::GetUkmRecorderAndSourceId` resolves the GC event's `ContextId` back to a `v8::Context` and then calls `blink::ExecutionContext::From(context)` → `context->UkmRecorder()` (v8_metrics.cc:660-663 in Chromium 148):

- For blink-created contexts this is fine.
- For **Electron's service-worker preload realm context**, the blink embedder-data slot (`kV8ContextPerContextDataIndex`) does not contain a blink `ScriptState`. `ExecutionContext::From` therefore returns a garbage pointer (the release-build `DCHECK`s are compiled out), and the subsequent virtual call `context->UkmRecorder()` traps (CHECK/CFI → `EXC_BREAKPOINT`).

So any full-GC metrics event whose context id maps to the preload realm context kills the renderer. Nothing the embedding app does in JS can prevent it; heavy SW workloads (allocation pressure → full GC) make it frequent.

Downstream consequence worth noting: the dead SW gets restarted by extension event delivery, so an app can easily end up in a crash-restart loop (we saw sustained 100% CPU in `ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorker → AllocateWorkerProcess` in the browser process until force-quit).

### Suggested fix direction

Exclude non-blink (preload realm) contexts from blink's per-context V8 metrics, e.g. ensure the preload realm context's embedder data makes `ExecutionContext::From` return `nullptr` (the function already null-checks), or set `v8::Context` embedder fields such that `v8::metrics::Recorder::GetContext` cannot resolve to the realm context.

### Expected Behavior

> **Bug 排查与 Issue 撰写**：eva-cli (Electronic Video Agent)
> **排查日期**：2026-07-14
> **提交目标**：https://github.com/electron/electron/issues

`ready-to-show` fires after the page is ready, and the window becomes visible.


### Actual Behavior

`ready-to-show` **never fires**. The window is created but remains invisible forever.

`did-finish-load` fires normally, confirming the renderer process is alive and the page loaded successfully.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Root Cause Analysis

A custom Electron diagnostic tool was built to isolate the root cause by running 5 automated tests, each creating different types of `BrowserWindow` (basic, GPU-accelerated + WebGL, offscreen, WebView, `app.getGPUInfo()`).

### Diagnostic Results: 5/5 Passed (with workaround)

All 5 tests passed, but **only because each test used `did-finish-load` instead of `ready-to-show`** to determine success. This confirms the rendering pipeline is functional — the problem is specifically that the `ready-to-show` signal is never emitted.

### Two Underlying Failures Identified

**1. GPU Shader Disk Cache Initialization Failure**

Every Chromium process start triggers:

```
cache_util_win.cc: GetDiskCacheDir() → Access Denied
```

The GPU shader disk cache directory cannot be created under `%APPDATA%`, causing the GPU process to fail during initialization.

**2. Steam CEF Confirms Chromium-Level Bug**

Steam's CEF (`steamwebhelper.exe`) is also affected — CEF browser and utility processes crash-loop indefinitely (~10 second cycle). Verified via `debug.log`:

```
[0714/013847.821:INFO:crash_reporting.cc(238)] Crash reporting enabled for process: browser
[0714/013847.888:INFO:crash_reporting.cc(238)] Crash reporting enabled for process: utility
[0714/013857.970:INFO:crash_reporting.cc(238)] Crash reporting enabled for process: browser
[0714/013858.038:INFO:crash_reporting.cc(238)] Crash reporting enabled for process: utility
... (repeats indefinitely, every ~10 seconds)
```

This proves the issue is at the **Chromium level**, not Electron-specific.

## Workarounds (Verified)

| Severity | Flags | Effect |
|----------|-------|--------|
| Light | `--disable-gpu-shader-disk-cache` | Bypasses cache init failure; GPU acceleration preserved |
| Medium | `--disable-gpu --disable-gpu-sandbox --in-process-gpu` | Disables GPU entirely; confirmed working for Obsidian & Unity Hub |
| Heavy | `--no-sandbox --disable-gpu` | Last resort; removes all sandboxing |

### Applying Workarounds

For end-user Electron apps (no source access), add flags to the shortcut target:

```
"D:\soft\Obsidian\Obsidian.exe" --disable-gpu --disable-gpu-sandbox --in-process-gpu
```

For app developers, use `app.commandLine.appendSwitch()` before `app.whenReady()`:

```js
app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-gpu');
app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-gpu-sandbox');
app.commandLine.appendSwitch('in-process-gpu');
```

|-------------|------|--------|
