title: frame_converter.cc creates a new ObjectTemplate on every IPC call, causing V8 crash after days of runtime
body:
## `frame_converter.cc` creates a new ObjectTemplate on every IPC call, causing V8 crash after days of runtime

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.10.2, 40.10.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS (Darwin 24.5.0), Mac mini (Macmini7,1)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

The application should run stably for extended periods (days/weeks) without crashing, even with frequent synchronous IPC calls (e.g., from `@electron/remote`).

### Actual Behavior

After 4–6 days of continuous runtime, the main process crashes with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` inside V8's `InstantiateFunction()` when processing a synchronous IPC message. The crash occurs consistently after an idle period (~45 minutes), suggesting it is triggered by V8's idle-time Major GC (Mark-Compact with compaction).

Three independent crash reports from different app versions (40.10.2 and 40.10.3) all show the same crash path.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

#### Root Cause Analysis

The crash originates in [`shell/common/gin_converters/frame_converter.cc`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.10.3/shell/common/gin_converters/frame_converter.cc#L49-L62), where `Converter<gin_helper::AccessorValue<content::RenderFrameHost*>>::ToV8()` creates a **new `v8::ObjectTemplate` on every call**:

```cpp
v8::Local<v8::ObjectTemplate> templ = v8::ObjectTemplate::New(isolate);
templ->SetInternalFieldCount(2);
v8::Local<v8::Object> rfh_obj =
    templ->NewInstance(isolate->GetCurrentContext()).ToLocalChecked();
```

This code runs on every synchronous IPC call via the following path:

```
ipcRenderer.sendSync()
  → ElectronApiIPCHandlerImpl::MessageSync()        // electron_api_ipc_handler_impl.cc:103
    → MakeIPCEvent()                                 // electron_api_ipc_handler_impl.cc:179
      → dict.SetGetter("senderFrame", frame)
        → Converter<AccessorValue<RFH*>>::ToV8()     // frame_converter.cc:49
          → ObjectTemplate::New(isolate)              // NEW template every time
          → templ->NewInstance(context)
            → V8 InstantiateFunction()               // CRASH here
```

`v8::ObjectTemplate` and its implicit `FunctionTemplateInfo` constructor are designed to be **created once and reused**. Creating and discarding them on every IPC call is an unusual pattern that stresses a rarely-tested V8 code path. Over millions of IPC calls (especially from `@electron/remote` which uses `sendSync` extensively), this accumulates a large number of short-lived template objects in V8's old generation heap.

When the app goes idle, V8's idle-time GC performs a Major GC (Mark-Compact with compaction), and during this process, a `FunctionTemplateInfo` object's bit fields become corrupted. The next IPC call after the idle period then crashes when `InstantiateFunction()` reads the invalid bit field.

#### Fully Symbolicated Crash Stack (from Breakpad minidump + symbols)

```
Frame 0:  InstantiateFunction(Isolate*, NativeContext, FunctionTemplateInfo, Name)  [bit-field.h:80]
Frame 1:  InstantiateObject(Isolate*, ObjectTemplateInfo, JSReceiver, bool)         [api-natives.cc:54]
Frame 2:  ApiNatives::InstantiateObject(...)                                         [api-natives.cc:514]
Frame 3:  v8::ObjectTemplate::NewInstance(context)                                   [api.cc:7227]
Frame 4:  gin::Converter<AccessorValue<RenderFrameHost*>>::ToV8()                    [fr

title: dialog.showSaveDialog / dialog.showOpenDialog appears behind parent window on GNOME Wayland
body:
## Environment

- Electron version: 28.x
- OS: Linux (GNOME Wayland)
- GPU: Intel Haswell (workaround: --disable-gpu, --in-process-gpu)

## Bug Description

When calling `dialog.showSaveDialog()` or `dialog.showOpenDialog()` on Linux with GNOME Wayland, the dialog window consistently appears **behind** the parent BrowserWindow instead of on top of it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a minimal Electron app with a BrowserWindow
2. Call `dialog.showSaveDialog(mainWindow, {...})` or `dialog.showOpenDialog(mainWindow, {...})` from the main process
3. Observe that the dialog appears behind the main window

## Expected Behavior

The dialog should appear on top of / in front of the calling BrowserWindow, as it does on Windows and macOS.

## Actual Behavior

The dialog appears behind the parent window. The user must minimize the app window or Alt+Tab to reach the dialog.

## Workaround

Using `zenity` (the system GTK file picker) via `child_process.execFileSync` works correctly — the dialog appears on top. This confirms the issue is with Electron's dialog implementation on Wayland, not with the underlying toolkit.

```js
const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');
const filePath = execFileSync('zenity', ['--file-selection', '--save', ...], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 30000 }).trim();
```

## Notes

- Setting `mainWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` before opening the dialog does NOT fix the issue
- Hiding or minimizing the parent window before showing the dialog works but causes jarring UX (window disappears/reappears)
- The issue occurs with both parented (`dialog.showSaveDialog(mainWindow, options)`) and unparented (`dialog.showSaveDialog(options)`) calls
- Occurs with both XWayland and native Wayland backends

The developers there told me that the problem is probably related to electron.

After calling `tray.setImage()`, Electron saves the icon-file in the temporary files directory, and after shutdown, this icon is not deleted from this directory.

The user's temporary file directory is not cleared automatically by Windows unless it is specially configured. And over time, a large number of files may accumulate there, which in some cases may affect system performance.
I understand that the problem is not critical at all, but it would probably be better if applications cleaned up temporary files after themselves when they become no longer needed.

Considering that Chrome officially already supports XRGB/XBGR formats, adding support for these formats should not be difficult. ### Proposed Solution

Add support for xrgb and xbgr formats.

### Alternatives Considered

Render XRGB content using ARGB format directly, but most X channels are set to 0, resulting in transparent/blank window rendering.

Use Node modules to handle texture format conversion manually, which is obviously less efficient and reliable than official Electron support.

### Electron Version

43.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 (25F84)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — every version I tested reproduces (41.10.0, 41.10.2, 43.1.1); not bisected further back.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Calling `navigator.usb.requestDevice({ filters: [] })` from a window whose `webPreferences.partition` is a **named session** should reject with `NotFoundError` — exactly as it does with the default session — when no device is selected / no `select-usb-device` handler is registered.

### Actual Behavior

The **browser process** crashes with `SIGSEGV` (`EXC_BAD_ACCESS` on `CrBrowserMain`).

The trigger is the named session partition: with the **default** session the identical call rejects cleanly with `NotFoundError: No device selected`. `navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice()` crashes the same way. Registering a `select-usb-device` handler that cancels the request (`event.preventDefault(); callback()`) does **not** prevent the crash — the fault happens in native code before the JS handler resolves.

```
Exception Type:    EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000100
Triggered by Thread: 0  CrBrowserMain

Thread 0 Crashed:: CrBrowserMain
0  Electron Framework  v8::CppHeap::Create(...)
1  Electron Framework  node::PrincipalRealm::...
```

(Symbol names are nearest-export approximations from a release build; the fault is inside V8 / cppgc internals during device-chooser setup.)

Regarding the Chromium question above: the trigger is an Electron-specific `webPreferences.partition` (named session), which has no web-page-settable equivalent in stock Chrome, so I can't reproduce it directly there. The crash itself is in the Chromium-layer device-chooser path, so a Chromium root cause is still possible.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/boutetnico/cd2005b668f680b47abab2056b3fccc6

### Additional Information

The only difference between the crashing and non-crashing runs is a single `webPreferences.partition` value. In the gist, `main.js` calls `requestDevice()` from the main process via `webContents.executeJavaScript(code, /* userGesture */ true)` on `did-finish-load`; flipping the `USE_DEFAULT_SESSION` constant to `true` gives the non-crashing control case. No device or hardware is required — the crash happens while opening the device chooser.

Reproduced identically on:

| Electron | Chromium | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 41.10.0 | 146 | SIGSEGV |
| 41.10.2 | 146 | SIGSEGV |
| 43.1.1 | 150 | SIGSEGV |

title: [Bug]: macOS 26 (Tahoe): permanent browser-process main-thread deadlock in AppKit/FrontBoardServices scene update (_setFrameCommon:fromServer: → FBSScene _sendUpdate: → performAsyncAndWait self-wait)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Tahoe

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — single field incident so far; the deadlock is inside Apple frameworks and likely OS-version-gated rather than Electron-version-gated (details below).

### Expected Behavior

The browser process main thread survives window-server-initiated frame updates.

### Actual Behavior

The browser process main thread (`CrBrowserMain`) **permanently deadlocked** inside Apple's AppKit/FrontBoardServices scene-update machinery while handling a window frame update delivered from the window server. macOS flagged the process "Unresponsive for 1305 seconds before sampling"; two samples 3 minutes apart show the identical stack (100% of samples), CPU ~0. All child processes (GPU, renderers, network) remained healthy. The app never recovers; only SIGKILL ends it.

Full kernel-annotated spindump excerpt (single process, scrubbed): https://gist.github.com/brennanb2025/d7f6f5a64aaf4353c410315225e1006b

The deadlock chain, read from the spindump:

1. The main thread picks up a BoardServices **run-loop-source callout** — i.e. it is executing a block belonging to the FrontBoard callout queue: `__CFRunLoopDoSource0` → `BSServiceMainRunLoopSourceHandler` → `__BSSERVICEMAINRUNLOOPQUEUE_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_BLOCK__` → `-[FBSWorkspace _calloutQueue_executeCalloutFromSource:withBlock:]`. While this runs, the underlying `BSServiceDispatchQueue`'s dispatch ownership is in a **transient state**.
2. The scene-settings update runs `-[NSWindow _setFrameCommon:display:fromServer:]`, which triggers AppKit autolayout (`-[NSView layoutSubtreeIfNeeded]` → `NSViewActuallyUpdateFrameFromLayoutEngine` → `-[NSView setFrame:]`), which posts `NSViewFrameDidChangeNotification`, whose (AppKit-internal) observer **re-enters** `_setFrameCommon:display:fromServer:` — the two nested `_setFrameCommon` frames are visible in the stack.
3. The nested frame change posts another notification, whose AppKit-internal observer sends a scene update back: `-[FBSScene _updateClientSettings:]` → `-[FBSScene _sendUpdate:]` → `-[BSServiceDispatchQueue performAsyncAndWait:]` — **on the same queue from step 1** → `_dispatch_async_and_wait_f_slow` → `__DISPATCH_WAIT_FOR_QUEUE__` → `kevent_id`, kernel-annotated **"(blocked by queue in a transient state)"**. The wait can never be satisfied.

Every frame between the run loop and the deadlock is Apple code (FrontBoardServices, AppKit, CoreFoundation, BoardServices). No Electron/Chromium frames participate. This machinery (scene-backed AppKit windows) is new in macOS 26, so the deadlock cannot occur on earlier macOS.

Corroboration from another app: openai/codex#23695 shows the same terminal signature (`FBSScene _sendUpdate:` → `performAsyncAndWait` → `__DISPATCH_WAIT_FOR_QUEUE__`, low CPU, permanent) entered via the `NSStatusItem` scene path instead of a window frame update — same self-deadlock, different door.

Repro attempts: a stress harness (bare Electron 43.1.0, two scene-backed windows, ~18,000 operations over 12 minutes: `setSize` re-entrantly from `show`/`restore`/`resize` handlers, hide/show/minimize/restore, occlusion churn) did **not** reproduce it on macOS 26.5.1. The trigger appears to require a genuine race with the window server (a server-delivered frame update colliding with an in-flight client scene update mid-callout), which client-side behavior alone cannot force. Filing primarily so there is a canonical tracking issue for this signature; we are also filing a Feedback Assistant report with Apple with the full spindum

title: [Bug]: Linux systemd scope registration fails for app names needing escaping (StartTransientUnit InvalidArgs) — upstream fix available for backport
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0 — but this affects all currently supported stable lines (41.x, 42.x, 43.x including latest stable 43.2.0). Already fixed on `main` via the Chromium 152 roll (see Additional Information).

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux (kernel 7.0.12-arch1-1, x86_64), Wayland session (niri). Reproduces on any systemd-based Linux session, regardless of distro or compositor.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A — this has been broken since `patches/chromium/fix_set_correct_app_id_on_linux.patch` started feeding real app/desktop names into Chromium's systemd scope registration.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes — the root cause is in Chromium code, and it is **already fixed in Chromium main** (see Additional Information). I am filing this against Electron to request picking the fix up for supported stable branches, since none of them contain it yet.

### Expected Behavior

Electron escapes the application name per `systemd.unit(5)` / `systemd-escape(1)` rules when constructing the transient scope unit name. For an app named `Open Design` the unit name should be `app-Open\x20Design-<pid>.scope`, `StartTransientUnit` succeeds, the browser process gets its systemd scope, and no error is logged.

### Actual Behavior

At every startup on a systemd-based Linux session, the browser process logs:

```
[29128:0725/174707.171989:ERROR:dbus/object_proxy.cc:572] Failed to call method: org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager.StartTransientUnit: object_path= /org/freedesktop/systemd1: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InvalidArgs: Invalid unit name or type: app-Open Design-29128.scope
```

The scope is never created: the app's processes are not placed in a dedicated cgroup, and the XDG portal app-identification this registration exists for (`SetSystemdScopeUnitNameForXdgPortal`) is defeated. This affects any app whose name contains characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9:_]` — spaces are the most common case (e.g. `productName: "Open Design"`, which also becomes the packaged executable name).

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/arseniy-gl/bb764197b773bcf5abd79cccf1225ac9

(The gist sets `"desktopName": "Open Design.desktop"` in package.json so the repro also works unpackaged / in Fiddle; watch stderr on launch. With a packaged app, a `productName` containing a space is sufficient on its own.)

### Additional Information

Root-cause chain:

1. `shell/browser/api/electron_api_app.cc` — `App::SetDesktopName()` sets the `CHROME_DESKTOP` env var (from `packageJson.desktopName` or `<executable basename>.desktop`, see `lib/browser/init.ts`).
2. `patches/chromium/fix_set_correct_app_id_on_linux.patch` makes `version_info::nix::GetAppName()` return the `CHROME_DESKTOP` basename **verbatim** (e.g. `Open Design`).
3. Chromium `components/dbus/xdg/systemd.cc` (`OnNameHasOwnerResponse`) builds the unit name with the format `app-$1-$2.scope` and substitutes the app name **without escaping**: [systemd.cc @ 146.0.7680.188 (Electron 41.3.0)](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/146.0.7680.188/components/dbus/xdg/systemd.cc#:~:text=ReplaceStringPlaceholders). systemd unit names may only contain ASCII alphanumerics, `:`, `_`, `.`, `-`; anything else must be `\xNN`-escaped, so systemd rejects the call with `InvalidArgs`.

Fixed upstream: Chromium commit [`7becfc78c4fabdffac412e894fd6ba2c92b7c804`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/7becfc78c4fabdffac412e8

title: [Bug]: Electron 43 overrides Windows file-dialog MRU when defaultPath is omitted
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a matching report.

### Electron Version

43.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10/11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.4.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No. This is in Electron's main-process `dialog` implementation.

### Expected Behavior

When `defaultPath` is omitted, Downloads may be used as the initial fallback, but subsequent dialogs should use Windows' persisted most-recently-used folder, including after restarting the application.

### Actual Behavior

Since Electron 43, every dialog without `defaultPath` opens in Downloads (or Home), overriding Windows' persisted folder.

### Steps to reproduce

```js
const { app, dialog } = require('electron')

app.whenReady().then(() =>
  dialog.showOpenDialog({ properties: ['openDirectory'] })
)
```

1. Open the dialog and select a folder outside Downloads, e.g. `D:\work`.
2. Open the dialog again, or restart the app and open it.
3. Electron 42 restores the selected folder; Electron 43 opens Downloads again.

### Additional Information

This was introduced by #49868. On Windows, Electron now resolves an omitted `defaultPath` to Downloads and calls [`IFileDialog::SetFolder`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc#L107-L158).

Microsoft documents that [`SetFolder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shobjidl_core/nf-shobjidl_core-ifiledialog-setfolder) overrides the most recently used folder regardless of previous user action, and recommends [`SetDefaultFolder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shobjidl_core/nf-shobjidl_core-ifiledialog-setdefaultfolder), which is used only when no recent folder exists.

Changing the helper to call `dialog->SetDefaultFolder(folder_item)` should preserve the intended Downloads fallback without disabling native MRU persistence.

title: [Bug]: setIgnoreMouseEvents no longer makes transparent windows click-through on Linux/X11 in Electron 43
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I searched the issue tracker, including #16777, #51808, and #52452, and did not find this Electron 43/X11 regression.

### Electron Version

43.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, GNOME, X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.7.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Not directly testable: `BrowserWindow.setIgnoreMouseEvents()` is an Electron API.

### Expected Behavior

Calling `win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` on a transparent, frameless, always-on-top window should restrict the native X11 input region so mouse clicks pass through to applications beneath the overlay.

With the minimal reproduction below on Electron 42.7.0, `XShapeGetRectangles(..., ShapeInput, ...)` reports:

```
input rectangles: 1
0: 1x1+0+0
```

Clicks pass through as expected.

### Actual Behavior

On Electron 43.2.0, the same window retains a full-window X11 input region:

```
input rectangles: 1
0: 400x400+0+0
```

For a full-screen overlay the reported region is the complete display (for example, `1919x1056`), so the transparent overlay blocks clicks to its own configuration window and every other application underneath it.

The result is unchanged when:

- Omitting the unsupported-on-Linux `{ forward: true }` option.
- Reapplying `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` after `did-finish-load`.
- Setting `focusable` to either `true` or `false`.
- Setting `roundedCorners: false` (to rule out the Electron 43 Linux frameless-window change from #52111).
- Launching explicitly with `--ozone-platform=x11`.

Electron's `NativeWindowViews::SetIgnoreMouseEvents` X11 implementation appears source-identical between the 42 and 43 tags, so this may be a regression in the Chromium 148 to Chromium 150 platform/build stack.

### Testcase

Save as `main.cjs`, install the Electron version being tested, and run it with `npx electron main.cjs`. Try clicking a window beneath the red overlay.

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({
    title: 'clickthrough-probe',
    width: 400,
    height: 400,
    x: 100,
    y: 100,
    transparent: true,
    frame: false,
    alwaysOnTop: true,
    focusable: false,
    roundedCorners: false,
  });

  win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true);
  win.webContents.on('did-finish-load', () => {
    win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true);
  });
  win.loadURL(
    'data:text/html,<body style="background:rgba(255,0,0,.2)"></body>',
  );
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => {});
```

Version comparison:

```sh
npm install --save-dev electron@42.7.0
npx electron main.cjs  # click-through works

npm install --save-dev electron@43.2.0
npx electron main.cjs  # overlay blocks clicks
```

### Additional Information

This was found in a multi-display desktop overlay. The application-level workaround is to pin Electron 42.7.0:

https://github.com/Netroforge/hronomancer/commit/007bf6fc72cbc55863a0f6e033a7516dba62aff7

Related but distinct:

- #16777 tracks support for the `forward` option on Linux. This reproduces without using `forward`.
- #51808 concerns native Wayland/Mutter; this reproduction is X11.
- #52452 is another Electron 43 Linux frameless-window regression. Disabling rounded corners does not fix this issue.

title: Environment variables
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The vast majority of developers do not think about the quality of the applications they develop using electron.

I need to disable GPU acceleration for all applications in order for them to work correctly, а от некоторых вовсе приходится отказываться, так как отключение GPU ускорения в них не предусмотрено.
I think a lot of users are facing the same problem.

I suggest two:

**ELECTRON_DISABLE_GPU**=1 - default disable GPU.
**ELECTRON_ENABLE_GPU**=1 - default enable GPU.

And configure electron so that the default behavior takes into account environment variables if developers do not care about the GPU in any way.

### Alternatives Considered

There are no alternatives for the user in electron.

title: WebHID chooser exposes devices that are discarded after recursive filtering
body:
After CL [7987617](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7987617), a HID device may be presented by the chooser but subsequently removed by `HidService::FinishRequestDevice`. Consequently, selecting a listed device can make `navigator.hid.requestDevice` resolve with an empty array.

https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52448 addresses the test regression by calling `navigator.hid.getDevices` early which would warmup the HID service connection and prepare the devices list with relevant filtering applied. However this seems to break the API contract, followup upstream if the recursive filtering should be applied as part of the chooser so the same device list view is maintained when calling `select-hid-device` and after the event.

title: install.js: unrecoverable failure and misleading error when the bundled extract-zip native binding cannot be dlopen'd (Windows Smart App Control)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0 (and any version using `@electron-internal/extract-zip`)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 26200, with Smart App Control **enforced** (`HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy` → `VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState = 1`, `Win32_DeviceGuard.CodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus = 2`)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Two things:

1. When the bundled native extractor cannot be loaded, `install.js` should still be able to short-circuit via `isInstalled()` or `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` — i.e. the `require()` of the extractor should be lazy, so that users who already have a dist are not blocked by an extractor they never need.
2. When the native binding fails to load, the underlying error should be surfaced rather than replaced by an unrelated explanation.

### Actual Behavior

On a machine with Smart App Control enforced, the OS refuses to `dlopen` the bundled, unsigned `index.win32-x64-msvc.node`, so `npm install` never produces `dist/` or `path.txt`. Downstream this surfaces as e.g. electron-vite's `Error: Electron uninstall`.

**1. The failure is unrecoverable because the `require` is unconditional.**

```js
// node_modules/electron/install.js
5:  const { extract } = require('@electron-internal/extract-zip');   // <-- dies here
16: if (isInstalled()) { process.exit(0); }
73:   const electronPath = process.env.ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH || path.join(__dirname, 'dist', platformPath);
```

The module-level `require` on line 5 runs before `isInstalled()` (line 16) and before `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` is consulted (line 73). Per #52029, pointing `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` at an existing dist is supposed to make `install.js` bail early — but it cannot, because the process has already exited by then. There is no way to opt out of extraction.

**2. The reported cause is misleading.**

```
Error: Cannot find native binding. npm has a bug related to optional dependencies
(https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828). Please try `npm i` again after removing
both package-lock.json and node_modules directory.
  [cause]: Error: prebuild for this platform is not bundled
           (and @electron-internal/extract-zip-win32-x64-msvc is intentionally not published)
    cause: Error: An Application Control policy has blocked this file.
           \\?\...\@electron-internal\extract-zip\index.win32-x64-msvc.node
      code: 'ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED'
```

Only the innermost `cause` is the real reason. The top-level message is wrong in two ways:

- Following it (delete `node_modules` + `package-lock.json`, reinstall) does not change anything, and destroys the evidence.
- `@electron-internal/extract-zip` ships the `.node` files in the tarball (`files: ["index.*.node"]`) instead of using optional dependencies, so npm/cli#4828 cannot be the cause here. The file **is** present on disk (867,328 bytes) while the message claims the prebuild is "not bundled".

**3. It presents as a flaky install.** Smart App Control judges by reputation as well as signature, so this is not necessarily permanent. On the same machine, with SAC left enforced the whole time:

| local time | `process.dlopen` of that file |
|---|---|
| ~08:00 | blocked (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`) |
| ~08:45 | loads fine |

So an affected user may see the install fail, retry later, succeed, and conclude the "remove `node_modules` and reins

title: webRequest listener callbacks silently drop headers when the returned headers object is invalid
protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged accepts invalid scheme names
body:
### Description

`protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged()` does no validation of `customScheme.scheme` before registering it and forwarding it to child processes. Scheme names are joined with commas into the `--*-schemes` switches and split on commas on the renderer side, so a scheme string that isn't a valid RFC 3986 scheme (e.g. one containing a comma) is silently reinterpreted as multiple schemes in the renderer.

Relevant code: `RegisterSchemesAsPrivileged` in `shell/browser/api/electron_api_protocol.cc` pushes `custom_scheme.scheme` straight into the `url::Add*Scheme` calls and `AppendSchemesToCmdLine` without checking it; we already have `Browser::IsValidProtocolScheme` for exactly this.

### Expected behavior

Registering a scheme that isn't a valid scheme name throws, the same way `protocol.handle` does for invalid schemes.

### Actual behavior

The string is accepted; a comma-containing name shows up as two entries in the renderer's scheme lists.

### Testcase

```js
protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged([
  { scheme: 'foo,bar', privileges: { standard: true } }
]);
```

No error is thrown; in a renderer both `foo` and `bar` are registered as standard schemes.

title: [Docs]: corsEnabled has no documented meaning, and the GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw workaround describes it as doing the opposite
body:
### Preamble

**This is a documentation issue, not a vulnerability report.** The behaviour described below is
intended and covered by Electron's own tests — I confirmed that before opening this. The problem is
that the flag's meaning is undocumented, and the workaround text in a recently published advisory
describes it as doing the opposite of what it does.

### What's missing

`docs/api/structures/custom-scheme.md` lists every privilege with a description except `corsEnabled`:

```
* `corsEnabled` boolean (optional) - Default false.
```

There is nothing stating what it does. Given the name, a reader can reasonably assume "CORS is
enforced for this scheme". The actual behaviour is closer to the opposite: it **permits** cross-origin
fetches of the scheme, and no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` validation is performed on the response.

That reading is not a guess — it is what the test suite asserts (`spec/api-protocol-spec.ts`):

```js
it('does not affect cross-origin fetch to a corsEnabled scheme', async () => {
  protocol.handle('cors', () => new Response('ok'));   // no Access-Control-Allow-Origin
  await w.loadURL(remoteUrl);                          // a remote origin
  const body = await w.webContents.executeJavaScript("fetch('cors://host/').then(r => r.text())");
  expect(body).to.equal('ok');
});
```

plus `it('allows CORS requests by default')`, which expects `200` for the same scheme.

### Why it matters right now

The workaround section of [GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw](https://github.com/electron/electron/security/advisories/GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw)
(published 2026-07-27) says:

> Set `corsEnabled: true` on schemes that must enforce CORS

Read alongside the tests above, that advice points developers toward a configuration in which the
response body remains readable cross-origin. An app that serves sensitive data from a custom scheme
and follows the workaround may believe it has restricted reads when it has not.

The same section also suggests:

> validate the request `Origin` in your protocol handler before returning sensitive data

That one does not appear to be implementable on this path: the `protocol.handle` callback receives
`Origin: null` for these requests, so there is no origin available to validate. Logged from a handler
on 42.0.1:

```
[handler corson] request Origin header = null
```

### Reproduction

Measured on **42.0.1** (which contains the advisory's fix). A page on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`
fetching a custom scheme whose handler returns a secret, varying only the ACAO header:

```
scheme registered { standard, secure, supportFetchAPI }              -> BLOCKED (expected, post-fix)
scheme registered { standard, secure, supportFetchAPI, corsEnabled } :
    no Access-Control-Allow-Origin                                   -> body readable, response.type "basic"
    Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://not-the-origin.example       -> body readable
    Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *                                    -> body readable
```

The mismatched-ACAO row is the informative one: the response is readable whether the header is
absent, wildcard, or names a different origin, so no validation is taking place. `response.type` is
`basic` rather than `cors`. Behaviour is the same on **41.3.0** (before the fix), so this is
longstanding and not a regression from it.

### Suggested changes

1. **Document `corsEnabled`.** Something like:

   > `corsEnabled` boolean (optional) - Whether cross-origin requests to this scheme are permitted.
   > When `true`, pages from other origins may `fetch()`/`XMLHttpRequest` this scheme and read the
   > response. Electron does not validate `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for custom schemes, so this
   > grants access rather than enforcing the CORS protocol. Leave `false` for schemes serving data
   > that other origins should not read. Default false.

   (Wording is a starting point, not a proposal I'm attached to — the maintainers know the intent.)

2. **Amend the `GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw` worka

title: docs: clarify D3D11 synchronization contract for Windows OffscreenSharedTexture
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the contribution documentation for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the code of conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for an issue that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

33.4.11

### Operating System

Windows 11 x64

### Description

The Windows `OffscreenSharedTexture` documentation describes `sharedTextureHandle` as a handle to a shared D3D11 texture and requires consumers to call `texture.release()` when finished. However, it does not describe the producer-to-consumer GPU synchronization guarantee at the time the `paint` event is emitted.

For ARGB/ABGR, Electron creates the resource with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` and deliberately does not use `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_KEYEDMUTEX`:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v33.4.11/patches/chromium/osr_shared_texture_remove_keyed_mutex_on_win_dxgi.patch

An external native consumer currently follows this sequence:

```cpp
// The HANDLE is received from the paint event.
ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> texture;
device1->OpenSharedResource1(
    sharedTextureHandle,
    IID_PPV_ARGS(&texture));

// Read the texture on an external D3D11 device, for example:
context->CopyResource(destination.Get(), texture.Get());

// After the external operation is complete:
// texture.release() in Electron.
```

The JavaScript texture payload exposes no keyed-mutex key, fence, or sync token. The Chromium patch notes that Chromium will not write to the shared texture after its copy request returns, but it is not clear what guarantees that this GPU work is complete and visible to another D3D11 device when the JavaScript `paint` event is delivered.

### Questions

1. When the `paint` event is emitted, is the Windows ARGB/ABGR shared texture guaranteed to be immediately readable by another D3D11 device after `OpenSharedResource1`?
2. What synchronization or ordering primitive provides producer-to-consumer visibility in the mutex-free path?
3. If the external consumer must wait or synchronize before reading, what is the supported procedure?
4. Is keeping the texture object alive until the external GPU operation completes, followed by `texture.release()`, sufficient?

It would be helpful to document this contract in `offscreen-shared-texture.md`, because without it external D3D11 consumers cannot distinguish a supported read sequence from one that only happens to work on a particular driver.

### Expected Behavior

The documentation states the supported synchronization sequence and the point at which an external D3D11 consumer may safely read the shared texture.

### Actual Behavior

The handle type and release requirement are documented, but GPU read-readiness and cross-device synchronization are unspecified.

### Testcase Gist URL

N/A - this is a request to clarify the synchronization contract for the existing API.

body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 42.0.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64 (M5) ### What arch are you using? arm64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — I've only tested 42.0.1. ### Expected Behavior Right-clicking a `-webkit-app-region: drag` region in a window with `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` should do nothing (or show a window menu), and certainly shouldn't terminate the app. ### Actual Behavior The main process segfaults immediately and the app dies. It's a null dereference in Chromium's views layer, reached straight from AppKit event dispatch: ``` Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000 Triggered by Thread: 0 CrBrowserMain, Dispatch Queue: com.apple.main-thread ``` Symbolicated against `electron-v42.0.1-darwin-arm64-symbols.zip` (the module UUID in the report matches the shipped framework), innermost frame first: ``` views::internal::RootView::UpdateCursor(ui::MouseEvent const&) <- crash views::internal::RootView::OnMouseReleased(ui::MouseEvent const&) views::Widget::OnMouseEvent(ui::MouseEvent*) -[BridgedContentView mouseEvent:] -[NativeWidgetMacNSWindow sendEvent:] -[ElectronNSWindow sendEvent:] -[NSApplication(NSEventRouting) sendEvent:] -[AtomApplication sendEvent:] -[NSApplication _handleEvent:] -[NSApplication run] ``` Registers at the fault: `far: 0x0`, `x8: 0x0`, `esr: 0x92000006 (Data Abort) byte read Translation fault`. `RootView::UpdateCursor` looks up a view for the event location and asks it for a cursor, so a null result from that lookup for a point in the drag region would produce exactly this. I haven't verified that specific line, though — that's inference from the stack rather than something I've confirmed. ### Testcase Gist URL Not a gist, but the whole reproduction is below. `package.json`: ```json { "name": "titlebar-rightclick-repro", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "main.js" } ``` `main.js`: ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') app.whenReady().then(() => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 500, titleBarStyle: 'hidden', trafficLightPosition: { x: 12, y: 16 }, }) win.loadURL( 'data:text/html,' + encodeURIComponent(`
right-click anywhere in this strip

right-clicking below the strip is fine

`) ) }) ``` Run it, then right-click the dark strip. The app dies instantly, every time. ### Additional Information Right-clicking anywhere in the drag region crashes it, **including directly on the traffic-light buttons**. Right-clicking outside the drag region (the page content below) does not. I tried a few variations to narrow down what's needed. Both ingredients seem to be required — a drag region, in a window with no native title bar: | Window config | `-webkit-app-region: drag` present | Right-click in that region | | --- | --- | --- | | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` | yes | **crash** | | default (framed) | yes | no crash | | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` | no | no crash | | `frame: false` | yes | **crash** | With the default framed window I also right-clicked the real macOS title bar, which was fine. Worth noting that `frame: false` is affected too, not just `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` — the crash from that variant is identical to the `'hidden'` one across the entire stack, not jus

title: [Bug]: macOS 26.4 (Tahoe): browser process never exits after quit if a BrowserWindow was ever created — infinite usleep poll loop after all teardown completes
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0 (also reproduced on 42.8.0, 43.1.0, and 44.0.0-alpha.8 — see below)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (Tahoe)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None on macOS 26.4.1 — every version tested (42.8.0, 43.1.0, 43.2.0, 44.0.0-alpha.8) hangs 5/5. The same versions exit cleanly on earlier macOS, so the regression is OS-version-gated, not Electron-version-gated.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Unknown — not systematically tested. The stall is in Electron Framework code (unsymbolicated Chromium teardown frames), so Chrome may carry a different shutdown path or a fix.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/bofeizhu/f91f42f580632ecff84b393ef939e66a (both mains, the EXIT/HANG runner, and the full `sample` output of a hanging 44.0.0-alpha.8 process)

### Expected Behavior

After `app.quit()` completes, the process exits.

### Actual Behavior

If the app **ever created a BrowserWindow** (even a single hidden one that only loaded `about:blank`), the main process never exits after quitting. The window closes, the Dock entry disappears, every JS lifecycle stage completes normally in milliseconds — `before-quit`, window close, `will-quit`, `quit`, and even Node's `process.on('exit')` — and the process then idles forever holding 100–150 MB RSS, spinning in a native usleep poll loop, at ~0% CPU.

With **no window at all**, the identical quit path exits cleanly with code 0 in ~1 s, 5/5.

Key observations:

- **Unbounded**: the process is still alive after 6.5 minutes; there is no timeout guard. Only SIGKILL ends it.
- **It is not waiting on children**: during the hang, the renderer helper exits first, then the GPU process and NetworkService utility helpers exit on their own within the first minute. After that the browser process is completely alone — no children, no windows — and still never exits.
- **Emergency exits hang identically**: calling `process.exit(0)` or `app.exit(0)` from the `quit` event produces the same stall, so the loop runs during native `exit()`/atexit/static-destructor teardown, past the last point where JS can run.
- **Stack signature**: `sample <pid>` during the hang shows 100% of samples (2612/2612 over 3 s) on the main thread in the identical stack — a chain of unsymbolicated Electron Framework frames with the leaf in `usleep` (libsystem_c). No modal/NSAlert, no dispatch-queue wait. Sample file attached.
- Reproduced 5/5 on each of Electron 42.8.0, 43.1.0, 43.2.0, and 44.0.0-alpha.8, in two independent investigation sessions on separate days.

Because the trigger is "a scene-backed NSWindow existed at some point," this looks like the macOS 26 scene-window teardown family (cf. #52437, which is a *different* signature: a runtime `performAsyncAndWait` dispatch deadlock while the app is unresponsive — here the app is responsive to the end, all teardown succeeds, and only the final process exit stalls). Also distinct from #49261 (macOS force-SIGKILLing running Electron apps). Presumably some teardown routine polls for a scene/WindowServer acknowledgment that macOS 26.4 no longer delivers.

### Steps to Reproduce

`main-hidden.js` — hangs 5/5:

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({ show: false });
  await win.loadURL('about:blank');
  setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 500);
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => app.quit());
app.on('quit', () => console.log('QUIT_EVENT_FIRED'));
```

`main-nowindow.js` — control, exits cleanly 5/5:

```js
const { app } = require('electron');

ap

title: [Bug]: Main process crashes when onBeforeRequest redirects a CORS preflight
OSR useSharedTexture: details.texture is always null on Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 40.10.6 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 22.04.5 and Ubuntu 24.04.4, X11 (kernel 6.8.0-136) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior With `webPreferences.offscreen.useSharedTexture: true`, the `paint` event should provide `details.texture` as an `OffscreenSharedTexture`, with `textureInfo.handle.nativePixmap.planes[].fd` on Linux. ### Actual Behavior `details.texture` is always `null` on Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver. The `paint` event fires normally, but every frame silently falls back to the CPU bitmap path, so the GPU-accelerated capture mode is unusable. There is no error thrown and no warning — the only way to notice is checking `details.texture` yourself. The same code returns a shared texture on Windows and macOS. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/sdkv2/94dec53fa8397ef82cd2e218dfdf9a36 ### Additional Information Reproduced on three separate machines (RTX 3060), across both Ubuntu versions, three NVIDIA driver versions (575.51.03, 575.57.08, 580.95.05), two libgbm versions (23.2.1 and 25.2.8), and three X server setups (Xvfb, hand-configured Xorg with `nvidia_drv.so`, and a full SDDM/KDE session). Result was identical in every combination. `--enable-features=Vulkan` is often suggested as the NVIDIA workaround. It did not produce a shared texture in any configuration I tried, and it additionally disabled WebGL2 entirely — for an app using OSR to capture WebGL content, that trade is not usable. Note for anyone else testing this: Xvfb provides no DRI3, so it can never work — but hardware GL still reports a real GPU renderer string under it, which makes it look like a working setup.
In-depth investigation

`details.texture` is explicitly `null` rather than `undefined` (verified by dumping the whole paint callback: `arg[0] = { texture: null, preventDefault: …, defaultPrevented: false }`), so `offscreen_use_shared_texture_` is being set correctly in C++ — viz simply never delivers a usable frame to `OnFrameCaptured`. With `--enable-logging=stderr --v=1`, ANGLE reports: ``` ERROR:ui/gl/egl_util.cc:92] EGL Driver message (Error) : Internal Vulkan error (-8): A requested feature is not supported, in third_party/angle/src/libANGLE/renderer/vulkan/linux/DmaBufImageSiblingVkLinux.cpp, initImpl:614. ``` `-8` is `VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT`. The likely cause is what the capture pool asks GBM for. `RenderableGpuMemoryBufferVideoFramePool` allocates with `requires_cpu_access = true` → `SCANOUT_CPU_READ_WRITE` → `GBM_BO_USE_LINEAR | GBM_BO_USE_SCANOUT | GBM_BO_USE_TEXTURING`, notably *without* `GBM_BO_USE_RENDERING` (`ui/gfx/linux/gbm_util.cc`). Chromium's own comment in `media/video/renderable_gpu_memory_buffer_video_frame_pool.cc` predicts this failure and names the vendor: > "On Linux, `GBM_BO_USE_LINEAR` (implied by `SCANOUT_CPU_READ_WRITE`) can prevent GPU rendering on some drivers, notably NVIDIA's GBM driver, because it disables `GBM_BO_USE_RENDERING`." So the buffer is allocated, but NVIDIA's Vulkan will not import a LINEAR/SCANOUT dma-buf as a renderable image sibling. Verified present on the failing hosts, so these are not the cause: - `nvidia-drm.modeset = Y`; `/dev/dri/card0` + `renderD128` present - X server exposes DRI2 + DRI3 - `nvidia-drm_gbm.so` GBM backend

### Electron Version

30.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

win 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should not allow Windows system DLLs or optional DLLs to be loaded from the application installation directory unless explicitly intended. DLL loading should use secure Windows DLL loading mechanisms and trusted system locations to prevent DLL side-loading.

### Actual Behavior

The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Summary:**
- We observed behavior that may indicate a DLL side-loading vulnerability in Electron 30 on Windows.

**Environment**
- Electron: 30.0.0
- Platform: Windows 11 (64-bit)
- Packaging: Electron Forge (MSI)

**Steps to Reproduce**
- Build and install an Electron application.
- Monitor the application startup using Process Monitor.
- Observe that Windows probes the application installation directory for optional system DLLs, including:
   - CRYPTSP.dll
   - dbghelp.dll
   - version.dll
   - winhttp.dll
   - userenv.dll
   - dbgcore.dll

- Create a custom DLL (proof of concept) with a payload  (for example, launching Calculator).
- Rename the DLL to match one of the DLL names observed during startup (for example, CRYPTSP.dll).
- Copy the DLL into the application's installation directory.
- Launch the application.

**Observed Behavior**
- The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

title: Browser process aborts (NOTREACHED "Unsuitable process reused for site") when an MV3 extension service worker is re-woken via startWorkerForScope
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (Chromium 150.0.7871.46)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6 (25G72), arm64 (M3 Pro)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — first observed on 43.0.0. I have not bisected.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No. Chrome loads the same extension without incident. Note that Electron runs with
`--disable-features=SpareRendererForSitePerProcess`, which Chrome does not, and this
plausibly makes process reuse more aggressive here (see Additional Information).

### Expected Behavior

Waking a stopped MV3 extension background service worker — which
`session.serviceWorkers.startWorkerForScope()` does, and which
`electron-chrome-extensions` does on every `chrome.*` event delivery — should either
start the worker or fail gracefully.

### Actual Behavior

The **browser process** aborts with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` on `CrBrowserMain`.
The whole app disappears; this is not a renderer crash and it is not catchable from
JavaScript.

The abort is a Chromium `NOTREACHED` in
`content/browser/renderer_host/render_process_host_impl.cc:5423`:

```cpp
if (render_process_host && !RenderProcessHostImpl::MayReuseAndIsSuitable(
                               render_process_host, site_instance)) {
  …
  NOTREACHED() << "Unsuitable process reused for site " << site_info;
}
```

Symbolicated stack (Breakpad symbols from the 43.0.0 release, framework UUID
`4C4C443A55553144A1ACB7F47BA94945`):

```
base::MessagePumpCFRunLoopBase::RunWorkSource
  mojo::internal::MultiplexRouter::Accept
    storage::mojom::ServiceWorkerStorageControl_FindRegistrationForScope_ForwardToCallback::Accept
      content::ServiceWorkerRegistry::DidFindRegistrationForScope
        content::ServiceWorkerContextWrapper::DidFindRegistrationForFindImpl
          content::(anonymous namespace)::FoundRegistrationForStartWorker
            content::ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorker
              content::ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorkerInternal
                content::EmbeddedWorkerInstance::Start                    (embedded_worker_instance.cc:289)
                  content::ServiceWorkerProcessManager::AllocateWorkerProcess (service_worker_process_manager.cc:145)
                    content::SiteInstanceImpl::GetOrCreateProcess            (site_instance_impl.cc:482)
                      content::RenderProcessHostImpl::GetProcessHostForSiteInstance
                        NOTREACHED()                                        (render_process_host_impl.cc:5423)
```

`FoundRegistrationForStartWorker` is referenced from exactly one function in
Chromium — `ServiceWorkerContextWrapper::StartWorkerForScope` — which is the backing
of `session.serviceWorkers.startWorkerForScope()`. So the crash is specific to that
API, not to service workers in general: a website's service worker starting through
navigation/fetch/push does not take this path.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Reproduction shape.** Load an MV3 extension with a background service worker into a
`persist:` session, then browse normally. The MV3 worker idles out after ~30s and is
re-woken on the next `chrome.*` event via `startWorkerForScope`. The crash happens on
one of those wakes. It is not deterministic per wake — many wakes succeed — but it
recurs reliably over a session. I have five crash reports with **byte-identical**
stacks (same image offsets in every frame), with uptimes from 2m22s to 2h14m.

I instrumented `session.serviceWorkers.on('running-status-changed')` to log the worker
lifecycle. The last events before one crash:

```
18:38:30.818Z stopping v0 chrome-ex

title: Electron Fuses for --no-stdio-init flag
body:
### Preflight Checklist

### Problem Description

Electron fails to start when nul devices are disabled on Windows systems. This issue has been reported in #44881 and fixed in #47870.

But the current fix is ​​to start electron with the `--no-stdio-init` flag, but there is no way to always enable this flag. Because NodeJS has not been initialized, `app.relaunch` cannot work.

We could probably provide a fuse to always enable it.

### Proposed Solution

Provide a fuse to always enable the `--no-stdio-init` flag

### Alternatives Considered

Use an external program to check if the NUL device is available and then start electron using the `--no-stdio-init` flag, but this requires introducing an additional build process.

title: Windows MSIX/AppX: Chromium GPU process can be killed when Code Integrity rejects vk_swiftshader.dll
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

An Electron/Chromium application packaged as MSIX/AppX should be able to initialize its GPU process without Windows terminating the process because a bundled Chromium runtime DLL does not satisfy the effective binary-signature policy.

If SwiftShader cannot be loaded under the GPU process's Code Integrity policy, Chromium should fall back gracefully rather than causing the GPU process — and potentially the entire packaged application — to terminate.

### Actual Behavior

There are now independent reports from multiple packaged Chromium/Electron desktop applications where the Chromium GPU process attempts to load:

```text
vk_swiftshader.dll
```

and Windows records Code Integrity Event ID 3033:

```text
Code Integrity determined that a process (...) attempted to load
...\vk_swiftshader.dll
that did not meet the Microsoft signing level requirements.
```

This is followed by the GPU process terminating and, in several reproductions, failing to relaunch.

Typical Chromium logs include:

```text
GPU process exited unexpectedly
GPU process launch failed
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

On affected MSIX installations, the package can additionally transition to:

```text
Modified, NeedsRemediation
```

after which the application may no longer launch until repaired/reinstalled.

### Evidence that MSIX/AppX execution is relevant

One OpenAI Codex reproduction copied the exact same application payload out of:

```text
C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...
```

and executed it from an ordinary directory.

Results:

```text
Packaged MSIX:
Code Integrity 3033 on vk_swiftshader.dll
application terminated

Same files executed unpackaged:
normal GPU path works
no Code Integrity block
application remains running
```

This suggests that the packaged execution environment / GPU child-process signing policy is material to the failure.

A separate Claude Desktop report reproduced the problem 15/15 times using the MSIX build while the same-version non-MSIX build worked.

WinDbg on the Claude GPU child showed:

```text
ntdll!LdrAppxHandleIntegrityFailure
```

with Code Integrity simultaneously rejecting `vk_swiftshader.dll`.

### Code Integrity details

Another independent Codex reproduction recorded:

```text
Event ID: 3033
DLL: vk_swiftshader.dll
Status: 0xC0000428
RequestedPolicy: 8
ValidatedPolicy: 1
```

and observed the GPU child with:

```text
MicrosoftSignedOnly = ON
AllowStoreSignedBinaries = OFF
```

The Code Integrity event was immediately followed by the Chromium GPU process crashing and its relaunch failing.

title: Windows: dialog.showMessageBox auto-closes and returns a fabricated button index (420) for a button that was never created
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.3.0 (Also verified on 42.8.1 and 36.9.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 26200.8973, Windows 10 

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None. The affected code is unchanged in v20.3.12, v25.9.8, v30.5.1, v36.9.1 and v43.3.0, so this appears to have been present since custom buttons were introduced.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a message box is closed by a button id that Electron did not create, the
returned `response` should not be a valid-looking index into `buttons`. Returning
`cancelId` (the existing fallback for unknown ids below `kIDStart`) would be
consistent and safe.

### Actual Behavior

> **Scope, up front:** the dialog is closed by comctl32 before
> `TaskDialogIndirect` returns, so Electron cannot prevent the dismissal and this
> issue does not ask it to. The bug being reported is the **`response` value**:
> Electron fabricates a valid-looking button index from an id it never created,
> which is what makes the failure silent and undiagnosable in application code.

`showMessageBox` / `showMessageBoxSync` return `response: 420` for a message box
that has two buttons. Application code that branches on `response === 0` takes the
"no" path with no indication that anything unusual happened, and nothing is logged.

The cause is an unbounded range check in
[`shell/browser/ui/message_box_win.cc`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.3.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_win.cc#L259):

```cpp
int id = 0;
BOOL verification_flag_checked = FALSE;
TaskDialogIndirect(&config, &id, nullptr, &verification_flag_checked);

int button_id;
if (id_map.contains(id))  // common button.
  button_id = id_map[id];
else if (id >= kIDStart)  // custom button.
  button_id = id - kIDStart;      // <-- no upper bound
else
  button_id = cancel_id;
```

Any `id >= kIDStart` (100) is treated as a custom button, so an id of 520 becomes
`response: 420` even when only two buttons were configured. The check never
compares against `dialog_buttons.size()`.

### Suggested fix

```cpp
else if (id >= kIDStart && id - kIDStart < static_cast<int>(buttons.size()))
  button_id = id - kIDStart;
else
  button_id = cancel_id;
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/itsjithinv/16e9fde9bb666a4d0e25244a5db52ca3

### Additional Information

### Why an id we never created arrives at all

`0x0466` is `TDM_CLICK_BUTTON` for a TaskDialog and `CDM_GETFOLDERPATH` for a
common file dialog — the same message number, and both dialog types use window
class `#32770`. Software that reads the current folder out of file dialogs (file
dialog enhancers, DLP and endpoint agents) enumerates `#32770` windows and sends
`0x0466` with `wParam` = buffer size and `lParam` = buffer pointer. On a file
dialog that is a legitimate query and the dialog stays open. On an Electron
message box, comctl32 interprets `wParam` as a button id and ends the dialog.

`wParam` is typically `0x208` = 520 = `MAX_PATH` in bytes, which is why the
fabricated index is consistently 420.

### Scope of the request

comctl32 closes the dialog before `TaskDialogIndirect` returns, so Electron cannot
prevent the dismissal — that part is not what this issue asks for. The request is
only that Electron not fabricate a plausible button index from an id it never
created. With the fix, an app receives `cancelId` and behaves as though the use

I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior For an offscreen-rendered page, a reversed wheel packet should be retargeted to the scrollable element under the pointer after the preceding direction was unconsumed at a scroll boundary. ### Actual Behavior After an unconsumed wheel packet at the top boundary, reversing the direction does not scroll the nested container under the pointer. The nested container remains at its top boundary. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/eric8810/3c54f310f196ea987a7ebcbf42ce2bd5 ### Additional Information The issue reproduces with ordinary `offscreen: true`; shared-texture output is not required. A proposed fix and regression spec are in #52776.
In-depth investigation

`OffScreenRenderWidgetHostView::SendMouseWheelEvent()` lets `MouseWheelPhaseHandler` update a mutable copy of the event but forwards the original event. The view also does not feed gesture acknowledgements back into the phase handler. Forwarding the adjusted event and handling `GestureEventAck()` allows the reversed packet to begin a new sequence at the point under the pointer.

### Electron Version

42.7.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 PRO 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron's embedded Node.js DNS resolver should use the DNS servers configured in the Windows network stack. When the native Windows resolver can resolve a public SRV record, dns.getServers() should expose the effective non-loopback DNS server(s), and dns.promises.resolveSrv() should return the SRV records.

### Actual Behavior

On an affected Windows x64 machine, Electron 42.7.0 (Node.js 24.18.0, c-ares 1.34.6) returns only [ '127.0.0.1' ] from dns.getServers(), even though Windows has a working non-loopback DNS server and nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:53.

dns.promises.resolveSrv() then fails with:

~~~text
Error: querySrv ECONNREFUSED _incallapp_sip._tcp.redt.com.br
~~~

The native Windows resolver resolves the same public SRV record successfully. This prevents a production Electron application from discovering its service endpoint and blocks login.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Minimal main-process reproduction

~~~js
const { app } = require('electron');
const dns = require('node:dns');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  console.log('versions:', process.versions);
  console.log('servers:', dns.getServers());

  try {
    const records = await dns.promises.resolveSrv(
      '_incallapp_sip._tcp.redt.com.br'
    );
    console.log('records:', records);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
  } finally {
    app.quit();
  }
});
~~~

### Steps

1. Install Electron 42.7.0 in a minimal application with the snippet above as main.js.
2. On a Windows machine showing the affected DNS configuration, run the native query below.
3. Run the application with npx electron . and compare the results.

On the affected machine, the native resolver succeeds:

~~~powershell
Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _incallapp_sip._tcp.redt.com.br
~~~

It returns target redt-cloud.pbx.redt.com.br on port 5022. Running the Electron snippet on the same machine prints [ '127.0.0.1' ] and throws ECONNREFUSED. The system-installed Node.js is not involved; the failure occurs in Electron's main process using its embedded runtime.

The condition is machine-dependent, but it matches multiple independent Windows reports in the upstream Node.js issue.

### Upstream root cause and fix

This matches nodejs/node#62347:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62347

The bug is in the Windows c-ares system configuration code. An empty Registry wide string is checked using size == 1 instead of size == sizeof(WCHAR), which can cause the Windows DNS configuration to be discarded and c-ares to fall back to loopback.

The fix was merged in nodejs/node#64110:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/64110

It is included in Node.js 24.19.0:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/doc/changelogs/CHANGELOG_V24.md#2026-08-03-version-24190-krypton-lts-aduh95

Electron 42.9.0 still embeds Node.js 24.18.1, whose c-ares source retains the faulty check:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.9.0/DEPS#L3-L8

### Why this needs tracking in Electron

Electron applications cannot replace the embedded Node.js runtime with the system-installed Node.js. Therefore, even though the upstream defect is fixed, applications on supported Electron releases remain affected until Electro

### Expected Behavior

## Environment

* **Electron:** 35.0.0
* **Electron Forge:** 7.4.0
* **Platform:** macOS

## Background

We are building a reusable Electron framework that is used to generate customer applications.

During a security assessment, we noticed that the generated macOS `Info.plist` contains the following configuration:

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
```

We did not explicitly configure this setting in our application.

We traced it back to Electron's macOS `Info.plist` template:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v30.0.0/shell/browser/resources/mac/Info.plist

Since `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true` disables ATS restrictions for applicable network requests, this setting was flagged during our security assessment.

## Testing

We tested the behavior with Electron 35.0.0 using both configurations.

### Test 1 — `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: true`

Request:

```text
http://httpbin.org/get
```

### Test 2 — `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: false`

Request:

```text
http://httpbin.org/get
```

We tested the request using `net.fetch()`.

In both cases, the HTTP request showed the same behavior. Setting `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` to `false` did not appear to prevent the HTTP request.

Because of this, we are unclear about which Electron networking APIs or request paths are actually affected by macOS App Transport Security (ATS).

## Current Workaround

We are currently overriding Electron's default configuration through our packaging configuration:

```javascript
extendInfo: {
    NSAppTransportSecurity: {
        NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: false,
    },
},
```

So far, we have not observed any functional issues with this configuration.

## Questions

We would appreciate clarification on the following:

1. Why does Electron set `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true` by default in the macOS `Info.plist`?

2. Is this setting required for any specific Electron functionality?

3. Which Electron networking APIs are actually affected by macOS ATS?
   For example:

   * `net.fetch()`
   * `net.request()`
   * Chromium renderer requests (`fetch`, XHR, etc.)
   * `<webview>` or navigation requests
   * any other Electron networking paths

4. Is it expected that `net.fetch()` can access an HTTP endpoint even when `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=false`?

5. Is overriding `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` to `false` fully supported and safe for Electron applications that do not require arbitrary HTTP access?

6. Are there any known Electron features or networking scenarios that could stop working when this value is changed to `false`?

Our goal is to keep the more restrictive ATS configuration for security compliance while ensuring that we do not unintentionally break any Electron functionality.

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>

</dict>
```

even when the application does not explicitly configure this property.

title: Expose destructive buttons in macOS message boxes
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron applications cannot currently identify a `dialog.showMessageBox()` button as destructive on macOS.

AppKit provides [`NSButton.hasDestructiveAction`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsbutton/hasdestructiveaction) for this purpose. Apple recommends setting it for actions that can irretrievably discard user data, allowing the system to apply an appropriate appearance and safeguards against accidental presses.

This came up in [microsoft/vscode#325273](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325273), where a native three-button `Save` / `Don't Save` / `Cancel` prompt could initially give `Don't Save` keyboard focus when macOS Keyboard Navigation was enabled. Space would then discard unsaved work.

VS Code has since mitigated that immediate problem by changing its button ordering, but Electron still cannot express the underlying semantic: “this button performs a destructive action.” Application code must instead rely on button order, labels, or a custom non-native dialog.

### Proposed Solution

Add an optional macOS-only destructive button index to `MessageBoxOptions`, analogous to `defaultId` and `cancelId`:

```js
dialog.showMessageBox(window, {
  buttons: ['Save', "Don't Save", 'Cancel'],
  defaultId: 0,
  destructiveId: 1,
  cancelId: 2,
  message: 'Do you want to save your changes?'
})
```

On macOS, Electron would set `hasDestructiveAction = YES` on the corresponding `NSButton` in the native `NSAlert`. Existing button indices, response values, default-button behavior, and cancel behavior would remain unchanged. Other platforms could ignore the macOS-only option.

The main question I would like maintainer feedback on is whether this is an appropriate Electron API and whether a singular `destructiveId` is the right minimal shape.

### Alternatives Considered

- Applications can reorder their buttons to influence which button receives initial keyboard focus. This can mitigate a particular accidental-input path, as VS Code has done, but it does not identify the action as destructive or allow AppKit to apply its destructive-action behavior.
- Applications can use custom HTML dialogs. That provides complete control but gives up the native dialog and its platform behavior.
- Electron could infer destructive actions from labels such as `Delete` or `Don't Save`. That would be unreliable, difficult to localize, and surprising compared with an explicit option.

### Additional Information

I created an AI-assisted prototype to test the API shape and observable AppKit behavior before proposing a production PR:

- [Prototype branch](https://github.com/joshka/electron/tree/joshka/destructive-message-box)
- [Electron implementation commit](https://github.com/joshka/electron/commit/d175f19e821f)
- [Manual Electron and native AppKit probes](https://github.com/joshka/electron/commit/323feb78f018)

The implementation commit passes the option through Electron's existing message-box conversion path, applies `hasDestructiveAction` in the macOS `NSAlert` implementation, documents the option, and adds automated coverage. The second commit deliberately keeps the manual probes separate.

In testing on macOS Sequoia 15.7.7 with Keyboard Navigation enabled, setting `hasDestructiveAction` on `Don't Save` changed the initial keyboard focus from `Don't Save` to `Cancel` for the button insertion order involved in the VS Code report. That observation motivates the proposal, but AppKit behavior can vary by macOS version and context; Electron should
