title: [Bug]: createReadStream fails for ASAR entry after extracted temp file is deleted
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.4.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.6 (25G72) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No. This is specific to Electron's ASAR filesystem integration. ### Expected Behavior After a temporary copy of a packed ASAR entry is removed while Electron remains running, a later `fs.createReadStream()` call for that ASAR entry should recreate the temporary copy or otherwise read the packed bytes successfully. ### Actual Behavior The first `fs.createReadStream()` succeeds. If its extracted temporary file is then deleted while Electron remains running, every later `fs.createReadStream()` for the same ASAR entry fails with `ENOENT` for the deleted temporary pathname. A buffered `fs.readFileSync()` of the same packed entry continues to succeed. Example output from the testcase: ```text Extracted copy: /var/folders/.../T/.com.github.Electron.ul88vz Deleted the extracted copy while Electron remains running. readFileSync after deletion: "electron-asar-stale-cache-repro-7e8fa4f9\n" REPRODUCED: ENOENT opening cached path /var/folders/.../T/.com.github.Electron.ul88vz ``` ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/0xdevalias/b28e27ea290913bbe4510eeaad7edaf3 Run with: ```sh git clone https://gist.github.com/b28e27ea290913bbe4510eeaad7edaf3.git cd b28e27ea290913bbe4510eeaad7edaf3 npm install npm start ``` ### Additional Information This was first encountered in openai/codex#37551, where a long-running Electron process could no longer open Codex windows after its extracted `.com.openai.codex.*` ASAR files disappeared. The original packed entries remained readable, and recreating the expected temporary files restored the running application. The validated diagnosis and workaround are documented in openai/codex#37551 (especially [this investigation comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37551#issuecomment-5278987637) and [the upstream-context follow-up](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37551#issuecomment-5279309264)). This report is specifically about recovery from a missing cached extraction file, rather than whether temporary files should be cleaned up at process exit. Related prior reports: - #30911 reports the same temporary-file lifetime problem for an ASAR-backed tray icon after the temp directory is cleared. It was closed for inactivity rather than by a generic cache fix. - #22500 notes that the OS may clean files from the temporary directory while the application is alive. - #29293 made the ASAR archive cache process-wide. That fixed #29292, but also makes the archive's extracted-path cache long-lived. - #52424 recently avoided `CopyFileOut()` for one packed-ICO call site, but did not change generic missing-file recovery.
In-depth investigation

`Archive::CopyFileOut()` retains extracted files in `external_files_`. Its cache-hit branch returns the stored pathname without checking whether it still exists: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/common/asar/archive.cc#L354-L390 Electron's Node filesystem wrapper calls `archive.copyFileOut()` from its `fs.open()` override. `fs.createReadStream()` reaches that wrapper, so a later stream open receives the stale pathname and the underlying OS open fails with `ENOENT`: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/node/asar-fs-wrapper.ts#L179-L237

title: GPU process crash (AVX2 gather out-of-bounds read) in hsw::lowp::gather_8888 when software-compositing after Electron 22.3.6 → 34.5.8 upgrade
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

34.5.8

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10.0.22631 (build 6060/26100-series)

### What arch are you using?

ia32

### Last Known Working Electron version

22.3.26

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The GPU process does not crash frequently.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrading our Electron app from 22.3.6 to 34.5.8, we started seeing frequent GPU process crashes, even with --disable-gpu set. The crash occurs in Skia's SIMD raster pipeline (hsw::lowp::gather_8888, using the AVX2 vpgatherdd instruction), triggered through Chromium's software compositing fallback path (viz::SoftwareRenderer), not the hardware GPU path. Since --disable-gpu forces Chromium into this CPU/Skia compositing path, the flag does not avoid the crash — it routes all rendering into the exact code path that's crashing.

Crash details
Exception: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ (0xC0000005), read from 0x46cc913c
Faulting function: hsw::lowp::gather_8888 / hsw::lowp::gather (vpgatherdd ymm4, dword ptr [eax+ymm1*4], ymm3)
OS: Windows 10.0.22631 (build 6060/26100-series)
CPU: Intel family 6, model 186 (0xBA) — 13th Gen "Raptor Lake" (mobile, e.g. i7-1360P class), 16 logical CPUs, fully AVX2-capable, not a legacy/edge-case CPU
GPU: unknown (crash happens in the software renderer, independent of GPU vendor/driver)

Call stack (top frames)
hsw::lowp::gather (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:5883)
hsw::lowp::gather_8888_k (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:6032)
hsw::lowp::gather_8888 (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:6029)
hsw::lowp::seed_shader (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:5580)
hsw::lowp::start_pipeline (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:5160)
SkRasterPipelineBlitter::blitRectWithTrace (SkRasterPipelineBlitter.cpp:431)
SkRasterPipelineBlitter::blitRect (SkRasterPipelineBlitter.cpp:394)
SkScan::FillIRect (SkScan.cpp:45)
SkScan::FillRect (SkScan.cpp:108)
SkDrawBase::drawRect (SkDrawBase.cpp:230)
SkBitmapDevice::drawRect (SkBitmapDevice.cpp:354)
SkBitmapDevice::drawImageRect (SkBitmapDevice.cpp:530)
SkCanvas::onDrawImageRect2 (SkCanvas.cpp:2328)
viz::SoftwareRenderer::DrawTileQuad (software_renderer.cc:524)
viz::SoftwareRenderer::DoDrawQuad (software_renderer.cc:360)
viz::DirectRenderer::DrawRenderPass (direct_renderer.cc:838)
viz::DirectRenderer::DrawFrame (direct_renderer.cc:435)
viz::Display::DrawAndSwap (display.cc:1034)
viz::DisplayScheduler::DrawAndSwap (display_scheduler.cc:269)

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

claude analyze below:

Root cause (hypothesis)

gather_8888 uses the AVX2 vpgatherdd instruction to batch-load 8 pixels at once from a source tile bitmap during compositing. This appears to be an out-of-bounds read near the edge of a scaled/clipped source image — a known recurring class of bug in Skia's SIMD raster pipeline (e.g. Mozilla bug [1568858](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1568858), [CVE-2021-29968](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1712047)), which historically manifests in the CPU/software-compositing path. When the source buffer's last valid bytes happen to sit at a page boundary, the over-read crosses into unmapped memory and triggers the access violation.

Why --disable-gpu doesn't help

--disable-gpu forces Chromium into viz::SoftwareRenderer, which performs compositing via Skia's CPU raster pipeline — including the AVX2 hsw::lowp code path that's crashing. Disabling the GPU therefore increases exposure to this bu

title: [Bug]: ElectronMain abort()s in _RegisterApplication when launchservicesd is unreachable (macOS 26)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6 (25G70), Apple Silicon (M1 Max)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown. This is not a regression I can pin to a version: `ElectronMain` always creates `NSApplication`, and HIServices `abort()`s when Launch Services cannot assign an identity. Older reports of the same `launchservicesd` ASN failure: #16919, #36671 (MAS / "unable to get application ASN").

This is a **different** abort from #51871 (UTF-8 `node::Utf8Value` / `SIGTRAP` on 42.3.1–42.3.2).

### Expected Behavior

If the process cannot register with Launch Services / the window server, Electron should print a clear error and exit with a non-zero status. It should not call `abort()`.

`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` already survives the same sandbox (it never creates `NSApplication`). A GUI launch that cannot register should fail the same way: an error, not a crash.

### Actual Behavior

Stock Electron 43.1.0 dies with `SIGABRT` / `abort()` in `+[NSApplication sharedApplication]` → `_RegisterApplication` **before any JavaScript runs**.

```
abort
___RegisterApplication_block_invoke
_RegisterApplication
GetCurrentProcess
-[NSApplication init]
+[NSApplication sharedApplication]
ElectronMain
```

Exit status is 134. No Electron/Chromium log line. macOS writes an `.ips` with `Application Specific Information: abort() called`.

In a real app (Orca 1.4.177, same Electron 43.1.0) this produced a 10-crash loop in 11 minutes: each `orca serve` / exec of `Contents/MacOS/App` spawned a new main process, each died before the JS single-instance lock, the caller retried.

`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` under the same sandbox does **not** abort (it does print `task_name_for_pid: (os/kern) failure (5)` from `codesign_util.cc` and then runs).

### Testcase Gist URL

Inline repro, no gist required. From a checkout that has `electron@43.1.0`:

```bash
cat > /tmp/deny-ls.sb << 'SB'
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read*)
(allow file-write* (subpath "/tmp") (subpath "/private/tmp") (subpath "/var/folders"))
(allow process-exec)
(allow process-fork)
(allow sysctl-read)
(allow mach-lookup)
(deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.lsd.modify"))
(deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.lsd.mapdb"))
(deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.launchservicesd"))
(deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd"))
SB

sandbox-exec -f /tmp/deny-ls.sb \
  node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron
# → exit 134, SIGABRT in _RegisterApplication

sandbox-exec -f /tmp/deny-ls.sb \
  env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 \
  node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron -e 'console.log("ok")'
# → prints ok, exit 0
```

Verified on macOS 26.6 arm64 with the Electron 43.1.0 binary shipped by npm (`com.github.Electron`). Crash report incident `9D39640F-1153-484A-9BB9-9EFCB8DE4F9`, parent `zsh`, role Unspecified.

The same profile against a packaged Electron app (`Orca.app/Contents/MacOS/Orca`) produces the identical stack.

`open -a App` from the same sandbox fails with `_LSOpenURLsWithCompletionHandler error -54` instead of aborting — still no window, but no crash.

### Additional Information

This hits any Electron app whose CLI or agents exec the inner `Contents/MacOS/*` binary from a seatbelt/sandbox that cannot talk to `launchservicesd`. That is now a common agent environment (Codex/Claude/Grok sandboxes, CI, SSH without Aqua).

JS cannot catch it: the abort is inside `ElectronMain` before

title: Web Bluetooth `GATT Error: Not paired.` instead of triggering automatic pairing using the pairing handler.
body:

### Electron Version

43.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 24H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Once subscribing to a protected characteristic, the pairing handler should trigger in the electron main process (which has been set using `ses.setBluetoothPairingHandler((details, callback) => { ... })`), allowing to confirm the pairing and read/write/subscribe to the protected characteristic.

### Actual Behavior

**First**: Initial pairing works fine.
After connecting, once I try to subscribe to a characteristic that is protected, the electron pairing handler is called in the main process and allows me to confirm the pairing.

But this behaviour differs, once the central (windows) forgets the bond information (e.g. user deleted it) and the peripheral still has the bond information stored.

In this asymmetric state subscribing to the characteristic fails with `GATT Error: Not paired.` It does not trigger the pairing handler, which it should.

Interestingly this does not happen, when I try to connect using Windows System Settings. Here connecting works fine, a new pairing is automatically initiated. It also does not happend on my Android phone (not via Web BLE). So this must be some specific error of the chromium/electron stack.

title: Flaky test: nn-test — short tls/https Node tests die with a silent SIGABRT (exitcode -6)
body:
Random tests in the Node.js suite (`linux-x64 / nn-test / Run Node.js Tests`) die with a silent SIGABRT — no stderr, no stack — and pass 9/9 on the `--measure-flakiness` rerun, which still fails the job. The victim is a different test each time but always one that loads `tls`/`https` and exits quickly.

**Test:** any short `parallel/test-tls-*` / `parallel/test-https-*` (seen: `test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra`, `test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra-empty`, `test-https-argument-of-creating`)
**Job:** `linux-x64 / nn-test / Run Node.js Tests` (`script/node-spec-runner.js`)
**Platform:** linux x64 (the bug is cross-platform, this is just where we run the suite)
**Frequency:** 3 of the last 34 completed nn-test jobs (2026-08-14 → 08-16), all on unrelated PR branches, each `failed 1 out of 10` on rerun. Locally ~1 in 30k test processes at `-j128`; `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 electron -e "require('tls')"` hits it ~1 in 700.
**Error / signal:** `severity: crashed` / `exitcode: -6`, or from `test/common/child_process.js`: `status = null, signal = SIGABRT` with empty `--- stderr ---` / `--- stdout ---`.

**Failing runs:**
- https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/31939048118/job/95146708674 (`test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra`)
- https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/31934729186/job/95136834082 (`test-https-argument-of-creating`)
- https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/31909127762/job/95072968384 (`test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra-empty`)

**Cause:** since Node 24.9 (nodejs/node#59856) `require('tls')` starts a `uv_thread` that loads the CA certificates and then takes `per_process::cli_options_mutex`. Node joins it in `node::TearDownOncePerProcess()`, which we never call, so if the process exits first the static mutex is destroyed by `exit()` under the thread and libuv's `uv_mutex_lock` `abort()`s. Core from a local repro:

```
main thread:                          crashing thread:
  exit() → _dl_fini (static dtors)      abort()
  __libc_start_main                     uv_mutex_lock()               deps/uv/src/unix/thread.c:366
                                        node::crypto::LoadCACertificates()  src/crypto/crypto_context.cc:934
```

Not limited to `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`: `require('node:tls'); app.exit()` before `ready` in the browser process aborts ~1 in 5. All of 41–44-x-y ship Node 24.18 and are affected.

title: Opaque frameless windows visually jitter during interactive resize on Linux/X11 since 43.0.0-alpha.4
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.4.0 (also reproduced on 44.0.0-beta.4 and current `main`) ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, GNOME Shell 42.9, X11, Linux 6.16.7, Mesa 23.2.1 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 43.0.0-alpha.3 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior An opaque frameless X11 window should resize with a stable presentation. Its content and apparent top edge should follow the native window bounds without jumping. ### Actual Behavior Quickly resizing an opaque `BrowserWindow` with `frame: false` vertically or diagonally causes its content and apparent top edge to jump and lag behind the native bounds. Electron continues to report a constant window origin while the visual artifact occurs. The regression begins at 43.0.0-alpha.4. Alpha.3 is smooth. It also reproduces on current `main` combined with PR #52740. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/otanim/12c2cece789b68d04c271b96bfc41b68 ### Additional Information Confirmed on Intel Meteor Lake-P / Intel Arc Graphics using the i915 driver. Native edge and corner resizing remain functional when using the proposed opaque-X11 policy together with PR #52740.
In-depth investigation

The first bad source change is `b36120f48` (43-x-y backport `accc847eb`), which replaced `OpaqueFrameView` with `ElectronFrameViewLinux` and began forcing every Linux frameless widget to `WindowOpacity::kTranslucent`. The unpatched opaque window is an X11 depth-32 ARGB window. The artifact remains with `hasShadow: false`, remains with PR #52740's transparent/internal-resize path, and remains after removing `_NET_WM_SYNC_REQUEST` and its counter. Disabling GPU compositing removes it. A preview of the proposed change keeps opaque frameless X11 windows on the system visual, producing a depth-24 window with a full opaque region. Repeated fast vertical and diagonal resizing is then smooth. Under the same preview, `transparent: true` remains a depth-32 ARGB window. The proposed implementation restores the pre-43 opaque surface policy for opaque frameless X11 windows, disables alpha-dependent client-frame shadow insets on that path, and relies on PR #52740's internal resize band. Genuine transparent windows and Wayland CSD windows remain translucent.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, bisect, reproduction, and drafting. I manually performed the visual A/B validation, reviewed the findings and proposed source change, and take responsibility for this report.

title: [Bug]: Window capture crashes when the captured window is continuously resized on some Windows 10 systems
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.8.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.5854

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

After capturing an individual application window, resizing the captured window should not terminate the Electron application. Capture should continue using the new window dimensions.


### Actual Behavior

Window capture starts successfully and frames are produced normally.

When the user continuously resizes the captured application window, total CPU usage rises to approximately 100%. After several seconds, the entire Electron browser process terminates without a JavaScript exception.

The problem is reproducible on the affected Windows 10 computer, but not on most newer computers.


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/307914070/14a2fd13dd155037f8a36ceb39819149

### Additional Information

### Reproduction steps

1. Open an external application such as Notepad.
2. Start capturing that individual application window.
3. Continuously drag an edge of the captured window to change its width and height.
4. Total CPU usage reaches approximately 100%, followed by a native crash after several seconds.

This uses direct individual-window capture through `desktopCapturer` / `chromeMediaSource`. It is not full-screen capture followed by region cropping.

### Affected machine

- Intel Core i5-3470
- 8 GB RAM
- 1920 × 1080 display
- Microsoft Basic Display Adapter, driver 10.0.19041.3636
- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.5854

The failure mainly appears on a small number of older Windows 10 integrated-graphics systems. Reducing capture resolution, frame rate, and encoder bitrate did not prevent the crash.

### Related issues

- #47450 reports a crash while refreshing the `desktopCapturer.getSources()` list; this report crashes during an active window-capture session while resizing the source window.
- #51910 concerns WGC thumbnail capture errors in a different Electron version; this report concerns active individual-window capture.

<details>
<summary>Native crash evidence</summary>

A minidump from an affected run showed native C++ exception code `0xE06D7363`. Loaded graphics modules included `GraphicsCapture.dll`, `d3d11.dll`, `dxgi.dll`, and `d3d10warp.dll`.

WGC responds to source-window size changes by recreating capture-frame-pool and texture resources. The presence of `d3d10warp.dll` together with Microsoft Basic Display Adapter suggests that this machine may be entering a software-rendering path when those resources are repeatedly recreated.

</details>

title: Support non-activating, keyboard-focusable panels for immersive, Spotlight-like AI chat input
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron does not provide a supported macOS window mode for an immersive, Spotlight-like AI chat input panel that can receive keyboard input without activating the Electron application or becoming the main window.

The desired interaction is an immersive AI chat input surface: the panel appears above the user's current application, accepts a question immediately, and leaves the current application visually and semantically active. The currently exposed concepts do not express this combination. win.showInactive() can show a window without focusing it, but it does not provide a path for the window to later receive keyboard input while remaining non-activating. Conversely, a regular focused window takes application focus, while win.setFocusable(false) prevents the window from becoming a key window and therefore prevents keyboard interaction.

This leaves applications without a reliable way to create an input-capable, non-activating surface on macOS.



### Proposed Solution

Proposed API

One possible macOS-only API is an activable panel option and matching runtime setter:

Plain Text


const panel = new BrowserWindow({
  type: 'panel',
  activable: false,
});

panel.setActivable(false);



With activable: false, the panel would remain eligible to become a key window when focusable is true, but it would not become the main window. This keeps main-window activation separate from keyboard focus.

See PR https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52914



### Alternatives Considered

title: Adapt to upstream heap profiling changes
body:
Heads-up to WG Upgrades:

Chromium is changing how heap profiling works upstream: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8258807

They’re adding it as a Perfetto data source and deleting the memlog infrastructure that Electron has been using for heap profiling so far.

When upgrading Chromium, this will probably require breaking API changes on Electron’s side:

1. Thoughts on the preferred API shape:
    - Drop the dedicated `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()`
    - Probably just roll it into `contentTracing.startRecording()` as described in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51184
2. How to find the code to delete:
    - Start with https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50826
    - Delete any code added back then that is no longer necessary
3. Reference for how the integration can work:
    - Chromium's own usage of the API: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8263276/7

title: [Bug] `webContents.sendInputEvent` mouse coordinates are mis-scaled by `devicePixelRatio` under fractional-DPR (Linux/Wayland) → clicks land off-target
body:
# [Bug] `webContents.sendInputEvent` mouse coordinates are mis-scaled by `devicePixelRatio` under fractional-DPR on Linux/Wayland

## Environment
- **OS:** CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.1.8-1-cachyos
- **DE/Session:** KDE Plasma on **Wayland** (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland)
- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
- **Electron:** 40.10.2
- **Display:** 4K (3840×2160), monitor reports scale `1` (kscreen-doctor: `Scale: 1`), but `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.2559…**

## Summary
`webContents.sendInputEvent()` mouse events (`mouseMove`/`mouseDown`/`mouseUp`) are
dispatched to the page at coordinates that are **divided by the window's
`devicePixelRatio`**. A click sent to `(x, y)` arrives in the page at
`(x/DPR, y/DPR)`, so on a fractional-DPR display every synthetic click lands
~20% short of where it was aimed. Links/nav elements miss, so programmatic
clicking does not work.

## Reproduction (minimal, no app)
```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')
app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 900, height: 600, show: false })
  await win.loadURL('https://example.com/')
  console.log('DPR', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('window.devicePixelRatio'))
  await win.webContents.executeJavaScript(`
    window.addEventListener('mousedown', e=>window.__m=[e.clientX,e.clientY], true);
    'ok'`)
  win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseMove', x:200, y:150 })
  win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseDown', x:200, y:150, button:'left', clickCount:1 })
  win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseUp',   x:200, y:150, button:'left', clickCount:1 })
  await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,300))
  console.log('received at', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('window.__m'))
  app.exit(0)
})
```

## Observed (this machine)
`devicePixelRatio` = 1.2559. Clicks sent to known points are received at ~0.795× (≈ 1/1.256):

| Sent | Page received |
|------|--------------|
| (50,50)   | (39,39)     |
| (100,100) | (79,79)     |
| (200,150) | (159,119)   |
| (400,300) | (318,239)   |

The received coordinates track `sent / devicePixelRatio`. On this fractional-DPR
display the offset is large enough that clicking a normal-sized link hits empty
space, so nothing navigates.

## Additional observations
- Events still arrive as `trusted: true` — the input is genuine, just mis-positioned.
- `pointermove` receives a slightly different coordinate than `mousemove`
  (`149,149` vs `148,148` in one probe), consistent with a DIP↔CSS translation
  happening inside the input pipeline.
- Not related to window zoom: reproduced identically at zoom levels 100% / 90% / 125%.
- **The fractional DPR is triggered by the page itself, not the display config.**
  On this system the compositor reports `Scale: 1` and there is NO global/fractional
  scaling configured (kwinrc `Scale=1`, `Xft.dpi=96`, no `GDK_SCALE`/`QT_SCALE_FACTOR`).
  Yet:
  - `about:blank`  → `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.0** (clean)
  - `example.com`  → `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.2559** (anomalous)
  Same window, same display. The DPR jumps to the fractional value only when a real
  web page is navigated to. This points at a buffer/scale negotiation that happens
  on page load (Wayland fractional-scaling path), not a user display setting.
- Suspected to be specific to this Linux/Wayland + NVIDIA + fractional-scale path,
  where `scaleFactor` (1) and `devicePixelRatio` (1.256) diverge.

## Expected
A `sendInputEvent` click at `(x, y)` should be received by the page at `(x, y)`.

## Notes for maintainers
Likely the coordinate translation in the renderer input path isn't accounting for
the page's `devicePixelRatio` (the window is scaled to DPR 1.256 while coordinates
are passed in CSS pixels). A workaround on the caller's side is to multiply the
coordinates by `webContents.getZoomFactor()`-adjacent DPR before sending, but the
correct fix is in Electron's input dispatch so `sendInputEvent` coordinates match
the page coordinate space.

title: [Bug]: Tray StatusNotifierItem answers property reads on its well-known name but errors on its unique name, breaking GNOME AppIndicator
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, GNOME 46, Wayland session, aarch64

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — not bisected. Reported by a user upgrading an app from Electron 28.3.3 to 43.4.0.

### Expected Behavior

A `Tray`'s StatusNotifierItem should answer `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get` / `GetAll` regardless of whether the request is addressed to its well-known name (`org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1`) or to that name's unique connection name (`:1.NNN`). They are the same connection, so both destinations must resolve to the same object and return the same properties.

This matters because GNOME's `ubuntu-appindicators` / `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` resolves the service to its unique name before reading properties, so the unique-name path is the only one it ever uses.

### Actual Behavior

Property reads succeed on the well-known name and fail on the unique name, for both `Get` and `GetAll`:

```
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 \
    --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
(<'..._status_icon_1'>,)

$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.558 \
    --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get

$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 ... GetAll
(full property dict)

$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.558 ... GetAll
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get
```

`:1.558` is the unique owner of that well-known name, obtained via `GetNameOwner`.

**Control.** A non-Electron indicator on the same session answers the same call shape on its unique name:

```
$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.115 \
    --object-path /org/ayatana/NotificationItem/livepatch \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
(<'livepatch'>,)
```

**Downstream effect.** `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` resolves to the unique name (`statusNotifierWatcher.js` → `Util.getUniqueBusName`) and then requires `['Id', 'Menu']` in `appIndicator.js:_checkNeededProperties`. It therefore always takes the failing path and throws:

```
While initalizing proxy for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1:
Gio.DBusError: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get
  getProperty@.../dbusProxy.js:89:33
  refreshProperty@.../appIndicator.js:306:48
  _checkNeededProperties@.../appIndicator.js:505:66
  _registerItem@.../statusNotifierWatcher.js:95:31
  RegisterStatusNotifierItemAsync@.../statusNotifierWatcher.js:205:24
```

Visible outcomes varied between runs of the same build:

- the item never registers with the watcher and no icon appears at all;
- the item registers but has no readable properties, and the panel draws a generic missing-image placeholder;
- **in one run the exception left the extension INACTIVE for the remainder of the session, removing the tray for every other app too.**

Because `Menu` is one of the properties that cannot be read, `setContextMenu()` is also unreachable — so the item ends up with no icon, no working activation, and no context menu.

Not investigated: whether other SNI hosts are affected. KDE Plasma has a native host and may address items by wel

title: macOS 15+ CJK garbling in Electron via system PingFang font (upstream Chromium hvgl)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker without success

### Electron Version

22.3.27 (also seen on 19.1.9)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.x and Tahoe 26.4.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not tied to Electron version - triggered by macOS 15+ font subsystem behavior.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Chinese text like "工作辛苦了" renders correctly in Electron app windows.

### Actual Behavior

On some macOS 15+ machines, CJK characters render as unrelated glyphs. Real-world user screenshots show a stable per-character mapping:

```
工 → ┥
作 → ﬄ
辛 → 扳
苦 → 梧
了 → Y
```

The corruption is intermittent - triggered by macOS font subsystem state (both PingFangUI.ttc and AssetsV2 PingFang.ttc present). Restarting the Electron app usually recovers.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Root cause is upstream in Chromium/Skia, not Electron-specific. Chromium already has partial handling in `printing/common/metafile_utils.cc:490` (see [chromium/455517173 comment4](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173) and fix [8007770](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8007770)). The rendering path in main Chromium is still affected.

Filing here for visibility and to check if Electron would consider a backport/workaround for supported branches. If out of scope for Electron, please redirect.

<details><summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

macOS 15 introduced the private `hvgl` outline table used exclusively by PingFangUI.ttc. `CGFontCreateWithDataProvider()` returns nil on the raw hvgl bytes. When Chromium/Skia falls back to `MakeFromName("PingFang SC")` for cross-process rasterization, it can resolve to AssetsV2's PingFang.ttc (CFF format), whose glyph table layout differs entirely from PingFangUI's. The result: text shape produces glyph IDs from PingFangUI's cmap (e.g., 工 → gid 695), which are then rendered against AssetsV2's glyph table (where gid 695 corresponds to ┥).

Minimal API-level reproducer (any macOS 15+):

```swift
import Foundation
import CoreText
let path = "/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Versions/A/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc"
let data = NSData(contentsOfFile: path)!
let provider = CGDataProvider(data: data as CFData)!
print(CGFont(provider) as Any)  // nil
print(CTFontManagerCreateFontDescriptorsFromData(data as CFData) as Any)  // 0 descriptors
```

Related upstream references:
- Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/380313555, https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173
- HarfBuzz: https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/4891
- FreeType: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/freetype/freetype/-/issues/1281
- Fonttools: https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/issues/3639
- Apple HVF docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hvf

Other applications hitting the same underlying macOS font issue via different code paths: mpv, Servo, Godot, Jellyfin Swiftfin, Parley/Blitz.

</details>

title: Guidance / workaround request: macOS 15+ CJK font rendering corruption (upstream Chromium hvgl)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker without success

### Problem Description

Electron apps rendering Chinese text on macOS 15+ (Sequoia / Tahoe) can hit CJK glyph corruption when the system font subsystem is in certain states. The root cause is upstream: macOS 15 introduced the private `hvgl` outline format used exclusively by PingFangUI.ttc, and `CGFontCreateWithDataProvider()` returns nil for hvgl bytes. Skia's cross-process typeface reconstruction falls back to family-name lookup, which can pick a different PingFang variant than the one used for shaping, producing a stable per-character CID mismatch (e.g. 工 → ┥, 作 → ﬄ, 辛 → 扳, 苦 → 梧, 了 → Y).

This has been observed across Electron 19 (Chromium 102), Electron 22 (Chromium 108), and Electron 38 (Chromium ~130). Chromium has a partial fix in `printing/common/metafile_utils.cc:490` (see [455517173 comment 4](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173) and fix [8007770](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8007770)) but this only covers the printing path; the on-screen rendering path is still affected on current Chromium.

For enterprise clients with large Chinese-mainland user bases (banking, IM, VPN, remote work tools), this manifests as intermittent garbled UI text that requires restarting the app to recover. There is no way to fix this from Chromium side without an upstream Apple fix (public hvgl spec or API), which has not been forthcoming since macOS 15 released in Sept 2024.

### Proposed Solution

Any of the following would help downstream apps:

1. **Documentation**: Add a note to Electron macOS docs about the recommended CJK-safe `font-family` stack pattern (put `"PingFang SC"` before `-apple-system` to force run-level match and avoid the Blink char-level fallback path that triggers the mismatch). This is the simplest and confirmed effective workaround.

2. **Cherry-pick evaluation**: Consider evaluating whether the Chromium `metafile_utils.cc:490` fix (or similar rendering-path workaround if/when Chromium lands one) should be backported to Electron LTS branches.

3. **Optional runtime flag**: A CLI flag like `--force-native-cjk-render` that routes CJK glyph rasterization through CoreText's high-level APIs (which handle hvgl natively) instead of the byte-stream serialization path.

Option 1 is the lowest-cost and would help many downstream apps immediately.

### Alternatives Considered

- **CSS-only fix in each app**: Put `PingFang SC` first in the `font-family` stack. Confirmed effective across all affected Electron versions. Requires every affected app to figure this out independently.
- **Wait for Apple to publish hvgl spec**: HarfBuzz maintainers have been waiting since 2024. No public timeline.
- **Embed a fallback font (e.g. Noto Sans SC)** and activate via probe-based auto-heal. Works but adds several MB to the app bundle and requires runtime detection logic. Not scalable to every Electron app.

### Additional Information

<details><summary>Minimal API-level reproducer (macOS 15+ only)</summary>

```swift
import Foundation
import CoreText
let path = "/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Versions/A/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc"
let data = NSData(contentsOfFile: path)!
let provider = CGDataProvider(data: data as CFData)!
print(CGFont(provider) as Any)  // nil on macOS 15+
print(CTFontManagerCreateFontDescriptorsFromData(data as CFData) as Any)  // 0 descriptors
```

Related upstream references:
- Chromium: [#380313555](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/380313555), [#455517173](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173)
- HarfBuzz: [#4891](https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/4891)
- FreeType: [#1281](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/freetype/freetype/-/issues/1281)
- fonttools: [#3639](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/issues/3639)
- Apple HVF partial docs: https://developer.apple.com/d

title: Send preedit rectangle (not just cursor rectangle) to support stable IME popup positioning
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Hi,

On Wayland, CJK input methods currently only get a cursor rectangle from the app. Because the cursor moves while typing Pinyin, the candidate popup jumps around constantly.

The proposed fix in wayland-protocols is to let apps also send a preedit rectangle, so the input method can anchor the popup to the start of the preedit instead of the moving cursor. See the discussion here:
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/517
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/521

title: Tray icon missing on GNOME (Wayland) in 44.0.0 / 43.4.1+: StatusNotifierItem registration is rejected
body:
### Electron Version

44.0.0 (also 44.0.0-beta.6, 43.4.1, 43.4.2)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME with the default ubuntu-appindicators extension, Wayland and Xorg sessions

### What arch are you using?

x64, arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

44.0.0-beta.5 / 43.4.0 (icon registers; see #52674 for the separate menu problem those had), 42.x fully working

### Expected Behavior

`new Tray(image)` registers a StatusNotifierItem with `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` and the icon shows in the GNOME top bar.

### Actual Behavior

Nothing is registered with the watcher (`busctl --user get-property org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher /StatusNotifierWatcher org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` never lists the app). On Wayland there is no tray icon at all; on Xorg the legacy XEmbed fallback icon appears instead.

The item calls `RegisterStatusNotifierItem("org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1")`, i.e. the well-known name with the object path appended. GNOME's watcher treats an argument that does not start with `/` as a bus name, `GetNameOwner` fails on that string, and the registration is refused, after which the SNI implementation is torn down. This came in with the cherry-pick of https://crrev.com/c/8250459 in #52951 (44-x-y) and #52952 (43-x-y); upstream fixed it a week later in https://crrev.com/c/8272040 (in Chromium 154.0.8016.0, so `main` already has it), which registers the plain well-known name and exports the item at `/StatusNotifierItem` again.

### Testcase Gist URL

```js
const { app, Tray, Menu, nativeImage } = require('electron');
app.on('ready', () => {
  const t = new Tray(nativeImage.createFromPath('icon.png'));
  t.setContextMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate([{ label: 'Quit', role: 'quit' }]));
});
```

Per-version result against a watcher that resolves items the way the GNOME extension does:

| version | RegisterStatusNotifierItem argument | result |
|---|---|---|
| 42.10.0 | `:1.1` | ok |
| 43.4.0, 44.0.0-beta.5 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` | registered (menu issue is #52674) |
| 43.4.1, 44.0.0-beta.6, 44.0.0 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1` | `NameHasNoOwner`, registration refused |

title: [Bug]: electron --version on Linux crashes with SIGTRAP inside a seccomp sandbox
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.4.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Omarchy 4.0.0 (Arch-based), Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3, Wayland (Hyprland) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior `electron --version` prints the version string and exits 0, including when the process is started from a Linux command sandbox that returns `EPERM` for `shutdown(2)`. ### Actual Behavior Official Electron 43.4.0 (`electron-v43.4.0-linux-x64.zip`) and Slack Desktop 4.51.191 (Electron 43.4.0 / Chrome 150.0.7871.224) both abort on `--version` with SIGTRAP: ``` [2:0827/123407.303066:FATAL:content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc:41] Check failed: . shutdown: Operation not permitted (1) Trace/breakpoint trap (core dumped) ``` Exit status is 133 (128+SIGTRAP). Google Chrome 151.0.7922.173 in the **same** sandbox does not abort: `google-chrome-stable --version` prints the version, and `--headless=new --dump-dom about:blank` exits 0. Outside the sandbox, `electron --version` prints `v43.4.0` and exits 0. ### Testcase Gist URL No app code is required. Reproduction with the official binary: ```bash curl -fsSL -o electron.zip \ https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v43.4.0/electron-v43.4.0-linux-x64.zip unzip -q electron.zip ./electron --version # v43.4.0 # Codex (or any Linux sandbox that makes shutdown(2) return EPERM): codex sandbox -- ./electron --version # FATAL:content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc:41 Check failed: . shutdown: Operation not permitted (1) ``` A direct check that the sandbox returns EPERM for `shutdown`: ```bash codex sandbox -- python3 -c 'import socket,ctypes,ctypes.util a,b=socket.socketpair(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_SEQPACKET) libc=ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("c"), use_errno=True) r=libc.shutdown(a.fileno(), 0); print("ret", r, "errno", ctypes.get_errno())' # ret -1 errno 1 ``` ### Additional Information This showed up first as a Slack Desktop 4.51.191 coredump after `slack --version` was run from a Codex bubblewrap jail (`tmux-spawn` scope, root mounted `ro,nosuid,nodev`, `/tmp/.codex` present). Slack has no public desktop issue tracker, so this is filed against Electron. Vanilla Electron 43.4.0 reproduces it. `chrome-sandbox` on the Slack package is correctly `rwsr-xr-x` root. This is not the SUID-helper-misconfigured abort.
In-depth investigation

Chromium `content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc` `SandboxHostLinux::Init()` does: ```cpp CHECK(socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0, fds) == 0); PCHECK(0 == shutdown(child_socket_, SHUT_RD)) << "shutdown"; ``` The outer sandbox's seccomp filter returns `EPERM` for `shutdown(2)` (`man shutdown` does not list EPERM as a normal error). Chromium treats that as fatal and calls `ImmediateCrash()` (`int3; ud2`), which the kernel delivers as SIGTRAP. systemd-coredump for Slack PID 24324: signal 5 (TRAP), `si_code: SI_KERNEL`, command `/usr/lib/slack/slack --version`. RIP was `int3` / `ud2`. The core contained the FATAL line above. One main thread; died during Chromium sandbox-host init. Chrome 151 in the same Codex sandbox logs `setsockopt: Operation not permitted` from crashpad and continues. Electron 43.4.0 / Chromium 150 still takes the fatal PCHECK path on `--version`.

title: setZoomLevel() / setZoomFactor() is silently ignored before the first navigation in the isolated and manual zoom modes
body:
### Electron Version

45.0.0-nightly.20260826 (current `main`, local build)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS 26 (arm64) – the code path is platform-independent browser-process logic

### Expected Behavior

A zoom level set before the first navigation commits is applied once the page loads, in the zoom
modes that are meant to persist (`isolated` and `manual`) – the same way
`webPreferences: { zoomMode: 'isolated', zoomFactor: 1.5 }` already behaves.

### Actual Behavior

The call is silently dropped – no error, no return value, and `getZoomFactor()` stays at `1`:

```js
const w = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { zoomMode: 'isolated' } })
w.webContents.setZoomFactor(1.5)        // silently dropped
await w.loadURL('https://example.com')
w.webContents.getZoomFactor()           // 1 (expected 1.5)
```

`WebContentsZoomController::SetZoomLevel()` bails out on `!IsRenderFrameLive()` (no frame is live
before the first navigation commits), and the JS binding discards its `bool` result, so nothing
surfaces to the app. Expressing the same intent through web preferences does work, so the two
spellings of one intent disagree.

Workaround: pass the initial factor via `webPreferences: { zoomFactor }` instead of calling the
setter before load.

I have a fix with regression specs ready, built and tested against `main` – PR to follow.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_ (the snippet above is the complete reproduction)

### Electron Version

44.0.0 (also reproduced on 42.3.3)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

CachyOS (Arch), kernel 7.1.3-1-cachyos, x86_64. KDE Plasma 6 / kwin_wayland, and separately a bare Xorg session on a spare VT.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

none on Linux (useSharedTexture working great on MacOS and Windows)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

With `webPreferences.offscreen.useSharedTexture: true`, the dma-buf referenced by
`textureInfo.handle.nativePixmap` should contain the rendered page.

### Actual Behavior

The `paint` event fires, `textureInfo` is fully populated and plausible, and the dma-buf is a real,
importable allocation of exactly the expected size — but every byte of it is zero.

This is **not** #49247. There, `paint` never fires with a texture. Here the handle arrives and is
structurally correct; only its contents are missing. It also reproduces where
`supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport` is `true`, which is the configuration #49247 treats as working.

The clearest way to see it uses only Electron's own APIs — `sharedTexture.importSharedTexture`,
`sendSharedTexture`, and `VideoFrame.copyTo`. No native addon, no external consumer:

Under KDE Plasma / Wayland:

```
paint#5  supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport=false  modifier=0  stride=5120
imported textureId=578d48a9-...
VideoFrame 1280x720 format=BGRA bytes=3686400
nonzeroPixels=0/921600  firstPixel=[0,0,0,0]
```

And on a bare Xorg session on a spare VT, where the flag is `true` — the configuration #49247
treats as working — the same script, unchanged:

```
session: tty  DISPLAY=:1  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=unset
paint#5  supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport=true  modifier=0  stride=5120
imported textureId=14f9f92c-186a-4e2d-ac3a-07d73971ff53
VideoFrame 1280x720 format=BGRA bytes=3686400
nonzeroPixels=0/921600  firstPixel=[0,0,0,0]
```

The page under test is a solid, continuously animating background, so a correct buffer cannot be
zero. The A/B against Chromium's other output path, same URL, same switches, same machine, differing
only in `useSharedTexture`:

| offscreen mode | non-zero pixels |
| --- | --- |
| `useSharedTexture: false` (CPU bitmap) | 921600 / 921600 |
| `useSharedTexture: true` (dma-buf) | 0 / 921600 |

Chromium renders the page; only the shared-texture export is empty.

#### What has been ruled out

Four independent readers agree the memory is zero — Electron's own import + WebCodecs readback; a
`VK_EXT_image_drm_format_modifier` import plus GPU copy; a CPU `mmap` with `DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC`; and
a third-party Vulkan consumer. The CPU mapping shares none of the Vulkan importers' assumptions
about modifier, stride, memory type or layout, and still reads zero. Zeros rather than garbage
argues the memory is genuinely zero rather than correct bytes read through a wrong layout.

Also ruled out:

- **Timing.** Reading 3 seconds after the paint, while still holding the lease, is unchanged.
- **Warm-up.** The 25th paint of a continuously animating page is unchanged.
- **First-frame effects.** Same at paint 1, 5, 10 and 25.
- **Content.** Same for a `data:` URL, a local app, and a fully loaded `https://youtube.com`.
- **Format.** Same for `argb` (stride 5120) and `rgbaf16` (stride 10240).
- **Electron version.** Same on 42.3.3 and 44.0.0.
- **Session type.** Same under Wayland and under a real Xorg session (not XWayland).

In chromium 150.0.7833.0, the logic for IsFilePickerAllowedForCrossOriginSubframe changed, see this [pr](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/3fd5e2cb1ef275dfe83f63d84d604ededba6ccb1).
Additional note: With electron 43.0.0-alpha.2 the save dialog will open, but if the dialog gets closed via cancel or x button, the electron window cannot be closed and the process has to be killed.

title: [Bug]: linux-arm64 builds published since 2026-08-24 expose x86-64 fcntl constants (O_DIRECTORY / O_NOFOLLOW / O_DIRECT)
body:
## Preflight checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Electron version

44.0.0 (also 42.10.0, 42.10.1)

## What operating system(s) are you using?

Debian (forky/sid), aarch64

## Operating System Version

Linux aarch64, ext4

## What arch are you using?

arm64

## Last Known Working Electron version

43.4.1 (published 2026-08-19)

## Expected Behavior

On aarch64 Linux, `fs.constants` should carry the arm64 values defined in
`arch/arm64/include/uapi/asm/fcntl.h`:

| constant | aarch64 | generic / x86-64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `O_DIRECTORY` | 16384 (`040000`) | 65536 (`0200000`) |
| `O_NOFOLLOW` | 32768 (`0100000`) | 131072 (`0400000`) |
| `O_DIRECT` | 65536 (`0200000`) | 16384 (`040000`) |

arm64 is one of the architectures that override the `asm-generic` defaults, and it
swaps exactly these two pairs.

## Actual Behavior

Affected linux-arm64 builds report the **generic/x86-64** values. On arm64 those bit
patterns mean `O_DIRECT | O_LARGEFILE`, so any `open()` that asks for
`O_DIRECTORY` actually asks for `O_DIRECT`, and opening a directory with `O_DIRECT`
returns `EINVAL`.

```
$ unzip -q electron-v44.0.0-linux-arm64.zip -d x
$ cd x && ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 ./electron ../repro.js
arch            : arm64
electron        : 44.0.0
node            : 24.18.1
O_DIRECTORY     : 65536 (aarch64 expects 16384)
O_NOFOLLOW      : 131072 (aarch64 expects 32768)
O_DIRECT        : 16384 (aarch64 expects 65536)
open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : EINVAL   <-- the bug

$ node ../repro.js          # system Node, same machine, same kernel
arch            : arm64
electron        : undefined
node            : 24.20.0
O_DIRECTORY     : 16384 (aarch64 expects 16384)
O_NOFOLLOW      : 32768 (aarch64 expects 32768)
O_DIRECT        : 65536 (aarch64 expects 65536)
open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK
```

## Testcase Gist URL / repro.js

```js
const fs = require('fs');
const c = fs.constants;
console.log('arch            :', process.arch);
console.log('electron        :', process.versions.electron);
console.log('node            :', process.versions.node);
console.log('O_DIRECTORY     :', c.O_DIRECTORY, '(aarch64 expects 16384)');
console.log('O_NOFOLLOW      :', c.O_NOFOLLOW, '(aarch64 expects 32768)');
console.log('O_DIRECT        :', c.O_DIRECT, '(aarch64 expects 65536)');
try {
  fs.closeSync(fs.openSync('/tmp', c.O_RDONLY | c.O_DIRECTORY | c.O_NOFOLLOW));
  console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK');
} catch (e) {
  console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) :', e.code, '<-- the bug');
}
```

## Additional Information

### This tracks the build date, not the branch or the Node version

I probed the official `electron-v<version>-linux-arm64.zip` release assets, one by one,
on the same aarch64 machine:

| published | version | `O_DIRECTORY` | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-06-30 | 43.0.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-07-21 | 43.2.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-04 | 42.8.1 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-04 | 43.3.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-11 | 42.9.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-11 | 43.4.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-15 | 42.9.1 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-16 | 42.9.2 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-18 | 42.9.3 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-19 | 43.4.1 | 16384 | correct — **last good** |
| 2026-08-24 | 42.10.0 | 65536 | **broken — first bad** |
| 2026-08-25 | 42.10.1 | 65536 | **broken** |
| 2026-08-25 | 44.0.0 | 65536 | **broken** |

Two points worth stressing:

1. The break spans **three different release branches** (`42-x-y` and `main`). The only
   thing the bad builds share is that they were produced after 2026-08-19.
2. **42.9.3 (good) and 42.10.0 (bad) ship th

title: Expose window reference handles (from xdg_foreign, XID, etc)
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Windowing systems allow to reference windows of other apps using some kind of platform specific tokens. For example wayland has the `xdg_foreign` protocol, X11 uses XIDs. I am not familiar with Windows or MacOS APIs, but i am sure they have something similar. Currently Electron has no way to get these for own windows, so they cannot be exported to other applications.

An example (and the motivation for this issue) are XDG Desktop portals. They describe the reasoning here: https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/window-identifiers.html. As of now, using portals from within an Electron application requires passing an empty string as the window identifier, so dialogs do not get placed correctly.

Internally, they are already detected and used by chromium and electron (via [`ExportWindowHandle`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/4ae8411d3e994ca1445c358a858f16fc9bdf40e2/ui/linux/linux_ui_delegate.h#L44)), so it shoud merely be a case of exposing them on a public API.

### Proposed Solution

Add a method to `BaseWindow` that returns the platform dependent window identifier handle.

### Alternatives Considered

Use `getNativeWindowHandle`, and write platform specific code that somehow talks witht the compositor itself.

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: [Bug] Native addons deriving from `node::ObjectWrap` abort during GC on Node 24.19.0 / 24.20.0
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.11.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.3.1 

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.10.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A native addon deriving from `node::ObjectWrap` should not abort the process when its wrapped JS object is garbage collected.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrading to 42.11.0 the main process aborts with SIGABRT from inside a V8 first-pass weak callback. The crash happens on a `worker_threads` thread of the main process. Symbolized frames from the minidump:

```
libsystem_kernel      __pthread_kill
libsystem_c           abort
Electron Framework    node::Assert(node::AssertionInfo const&)                        node_errors.cc
Electron Framework    node::RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(v8::Isolate*, void (*)(void*), void*) + 220
better_sqlite3.node   Statement::~Statement() + 312
better_sqlite3.node   Statement::~Statement() + 12
Electron Framework    v8::internal::GlobalHandles::InvokeFirstPassWeakCallbacks()
Electron Framework    v8::internal::Heap::CollectGarbage(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::HeapAllocator::CollectGarbageAndRetryAllocation(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::HeapAllocator::AllocateRawSlowPath(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration(...)
                      [JS frames]
Electron Framework    node::worker::MessagePort::OnMessage(...)
Electron Framework    node::worker::Worker::StartThread(...)
```

The addon is a fork of better-sqlite3; its `Statement` class derives from `node::ObjectWrap`. The destructor itself contains no Node API calls — the call to `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` comes from the inlined `node::ObjectWrap::~ObjectWrap()`.

We have not captured the process stderr, so we do not have the printed assertion text. In Node v24.19.0 the only CHECK in `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` is `CHECK_NOT_NULL(env)` at `src/api/hooks.cc:142`.

**Root cause**

42.11.0 updated Node.js to v24.19.0 (#52634).

v24.19.0 backported nodejs/node#63642 (`4b5eb7b72d`, "src: add cleanup hooks to `node::ObjectWrap`"), which makes the `node::ObjectWrap` constructor and destructor call `AddEnvironmentCleanupHook` / `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook`. `ObjectWrap` is header-only, so this call is compiled into any addon built against these headers.

v24.19.0 does not include nodejs/node#63985 (`1723773d41`, "src: keep global list of addon-provided cleanup hooks"), which reworks `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` to resolve the hook through a global registry instead of the current `Environment`. From that commit message:

> This occasionally breaks down when `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook()` is called during garbage collection -- which would be an expected use case of the functionality, but one that has not been covered through our tests before 215027c8eded2e.

In v24.19.0 and v24.20.0, `src/api/hooks.cc` still has:

```cpp
void RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(Isolate* isolate,
                                  CleanupHook fun,
                                  void* arg) {
  Environment* env = Environment::GetCurrent(isolate);
  CHECK_NOT_NULL(env);
  env->RemoveCleanupHook(fun, arg);
}
```

and `Environment::GetCurrent(v8::Isolate*)` in `src/env-inl.h` returns `nullptr` when `isolate->InContext()` is false, which is the case while V8 invokes first-pass weak callbacks.

title: Backport Chromium fix for wrong macOS AX line number / line range (crbug 423048796) to 42-x-y and 43-x-y
body:
### What is being requested

Please backport Chromium commit 36ac8f31796a392340f7914d1018c3a885fc183f
("Fix wrong line number and range when using macOS Accessibility in text fields/areas",
https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8092671, https://crbug.com/423048796)
to the 42-x-y and 43-x-y release lines. It first shipped in Chromium 152 (Electron 44).

### Why

This is the bug reported in #47393 (closed as upstream in June 2025; the reporter then filed
crbug 423048796, which is now fixed). On macOS, `AXLineForIndex` returns the next line's number
unless the caret is at the start of a line, and the legacy `AXRangeForLine` handler returns nil for
every line except the first. VoiceOver uses these to put the current line on a Braille display, so
in every Electron app with a multi-line text field (native `<textarea>` included) Braille users see
the wrong line, a stale line, or nothing. Blind developers are currently unable to use VS Code
(Electron 42) with a Braille display on macOS for this reason (microsoft/vscode#319725,
microsoft/vscode#316018).

### Evidence

Same test page, same VoiceOver, same Braille display:
- Chrome 152.0.7977.66 (fixed): six differently built multi-line fields all track lines correctly.
- Electron 42.8.1 / Chromium 148 (VS Code 1.135, page loaded in its Simple Browser): all six fail.
- Neither `patches/chromium/.patches` on 42-x-y nor on 43-x-y currently carries this fix.

### The change

Small and self-contained, in `ui/accessibility/platform/browser_accessibility_cocoa.mm`
(`accessibilityLineForIndex:` uses `upper_bound` with bounds checks instead of `lower_bound`) and
`ui/accessibility/platform/ax_platform_node_cocoa.mm` (`AXRangeForLine:` forwards every line index
instead of only 0), plus a test.

_No response_

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior
Normal interface text should render using the requested proportional UI font family, such as Noto Sans, while semantic code and terminal text remain monospaced.

### Actual Behavior
In Hermes Desktop (Electron 40.10.2) and Grok Bot, normal interface text renders as a monospace font even though KDE and fontconfig resolve the requested UI families correctly.

### Testcase Gist URL
_No response_

### Additional Information
The behavior is reproducible on the currently booted `aurora-dx-nvidia-open:stable` image.

<details><summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

The same host-level Electron/Chromium font-matching behavior also affects unrelated Electron applications, while an embedded webfont bypasses it.

Changing the Hermes CSS stack to put `system-ui` first, with an explicit `Noto Sans` fallback, did not change the physical font. The reliable workaround was to bundle Noto Sans Regular/Medium/Bold as application webfonts under a private family name and put that family first. After rebuilding, proportional UI text rendered correctly while semantic code and terminal text remained monospaced.

Relevant font resolution output:

```
KDE general font: Noto Sans 10
fc-match system-ui: Noto Sans Regular
fc-match sans-serif: Noto Sans Regular
fc-match "Noto Sans": Noto Sans Regular
```

The issue was reproduced in Hermes Desktop and Grok Bot, and appears unlikely to be VS Code-specific. Package versions remain `fontconfig-2.17.0-4.fc44`, `freetype-2.14.3-1.fc44`, and `harfbuzz-14.1.0-2.fc44`.

</details>

Opening a same-process child window with `window.open('')` from a renderer (contextIsolation: false, sandbox: false) should not crash the renderer.

### Actual Behavior

After the app calls `window.open('', anyName)` (same-process child window; the returned handle can even be discarded), the renderer process crashes silently — exit code `0x80000003` (STATUS_BREAKPOINT), no JS error, no FATAL log line:

- if the child window is **hidden** (`show: false` / 1px off-screen), the renderer dies **~0.5s after the open**, with no further app activity;
- if the child window is **visible**, the renderer stays alive until the **next user interaction** (click / SPA route change) in the opener, then dies.

All same-process windows die together and the app enters a crash-reload loop. 100% reproducible in our production app (8x8 Work — large React SPA); we have not managed to reproduce it in a standalone fiddle despite extensive attempts (details below), which points at a renderer-state-dependent race.

The crash is `CHECK(!environments_.contains(render_frame))` in `ElectronRendererClient::DidCreateScriptContext` (electron_renderer_client.cc:138), reached via lazy `blink::LocalWindowProxy::Initialize` — full symbolicated stacks below. Bisected to 42.10.0; introduced by #53042.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/riurisniti/a881f20a9cfca62d3e3738d9f13f5c71

### Additional Information

Appologies for the AI generated info dump - not everyday I encouter such esoteric Electron errors so I had to make do.

Note: the gist is a faithful *environment*, not a crashing one - it replays the exact arming step and both detonation choreographies that crash our app 100% of the time, but survives standalone; see the investigation below for why.

## AI Agent result

The regression bisects cleanly to **42.10.0** and is still present in **42.11.2**. 42.9.3 is the last good version. Since #53042 was also backported to 43.x/44.x (#53040), we expect those lines to be affected as well — this currently blocks us from upgrading past 42.9.x on any line.

Renderer configuration: `contextIsolation: false`, `sandbox: false`, `nodeIntegration: false`, preload on the opener window, `webSecurity: false`.

Happy to share minidumps privately and to run instrumented builds / patches against our app, which reproduces this within seconds on every launch.

### Symbolicated crash stack

Identical stack shape (same stack-offset layout) in minidumps from **42.11.1** (`electron.exe.pdb` debug id `7097E67EA20201714C4C44205044422E1`, crash at `electron.exe+0x38bcf67`) and **42.11.2** (debug id `37048362CA69C9374C4C44205044422E1`, crash at `electron.exe+0x38d6d67`), symbolicated against symbols.electronjs.org:

```

-> v8::Isolate::InstallConditionalFeatures

title: Builtin spellchecker never marks text typed into a CodeMirror 6 editor — plain contenteditable works; same page fully checked in plain Chrome 152
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu Linux x64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not bisected

### Expected Behavior

With the builtin spellchecker enabled (`spellcheck: true` webPreference, `session.setSpellCheckerLanguages(['en-US'])`), any `contenteditable` editing host with `spellcheck="true" lang="en-US"` gets the red squiggle and `context-menu` `params.misspelledWord`/suggestions for misspelled typed text — including one driven by CodeMirror 6.

### Actual Behavior

On a page with three such editables — (1) a plain `contenteditable`, (2) a bare unmodified CodeMirror 6 `EditorView` at top level, (3) the same nested inside another editable — typing `recieve here` into each marks only (1). The CM-driven hosts (2)/(3) are never underlined and the context menu reports no misspelled word.

The marker is never created, as opposed to created-then-wiped: replacing a text node/line **after** typing leaves an existing marker intact. And since only genuinely typed text is marked (attribute toggles / blur-refocus never trigger a re-check), the miss never recovers.

**Why this looks Electron-side, not Blink or CodeMirror:** the identical repro page opened in plain Google Chrome 152.0.7977.82 (Linux, fresh `en-US` profile) spellchecks **all three** boxes, including both CodeMirror editors. The CodeMirror maintainer also could not reproduce on Chromium 152 (Linux): https://discuss.codemirror.net/t/9886. Same Chromium 152 engine, divergent outcomes — the difference is Electron's spellchecker integration.

A plain contenteditable that mimics CM's per-keystroke DOM work (replacing the edited text node or the whole line, re-asserting the selection, synchronously or on rAF) is still checked fine — so it is specifically the live CodeMirror 6 editing host that Electron's after-typing marking pass never services.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mauriciolongo/daeff5511fdc9ea402506a917f1a83e5

### Additional Information

The gist is standalone HTML with no application code (unmodified `@codemirror/view` 6.43.1 bundled inline). Load it in a `BrowserWindow` with the builtin spellchecker enabled and type `recieve here` in each box: the plain box squiggles, both CodeMirror boxes stay clean. The same file opened in plain Chrome 152 squiggles all three.

Unknown

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Signal Desktop (and other Electron apps) should start normally with a visible window and working renderer.

### Actual Behavior

Signal silently crashes at startup with no window shown. The GPU subprocess exits with `STATUS_BREAKPOINT` (`0x80000003` / exit code `-2147483645`). This is a related but distinct variant from the original reports in #32440 which showed `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (`0xC0000005`).

Windows Application Event Log (Event ID 1000):
```text
Faulting application: Signal.exe
Exception code: 0x80000003 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT)
Fault offset: 0x0000000006fefb69  ← identical across every crash attempt
```

Running with `--disable-gpu` surfaces the GPU subprocess crash explicitly:
```text
[ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc:1108] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[FATAL:gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:416] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

**Secondary issue:** Even after working around the startup crash with `--in-process-gpu`, newly spawned renderer processes (e.g. Help → About window) crash with the same exit code:
```text
Render process is gone
Error: Reason: crashed, Exit Code: -2147483645
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Hardware
- GPU: Intel® Iris® Xe Graphics — Tiger Lake (`PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_9A49`, HP subsystem `87FE103C`)
- Drivers tested: `31.0.101.5186` (Jan 2024) and `32.0.101.7088` (Jun 2026) — both affected

### Diagnostics Ruled Out
- Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS): not enabled
- Hardware Shadow Stack / CET (`UserShadowStack`): NOTSET  
- No third-party AV or EDR (Windows Defender only)
- Fault offset `0x06fefb69` is deterministic across all crash attempts

### Workaround
`--in-process-gpu` flag allows the app to start. `--disable-gpu` alone does **not** fix it (GPU subprocess still crashes).

### Related Issues
- electron/electron#32440 (closed — original report, different exit code `0xC0000005`)
- signalapp/Signal-Desktop#5721 (open — Intel integrated graphics requiring GPU flags)
- signalapp/Signal-Desktop#7828 (open — renderer crash on Windows 11)

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.

### Electron Version

44.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6.2, arm64, Retina display (scaleFactor 2)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — see note below; this may have always been the case.

### Expected Behavior

With offscreen rendering, the scale factor the page is told about should be the scale factor it is rasterised at. Either the page sees `devicePixelRatio === 1` and `capturePage()` returns an image the size of the CSS viewport, or the page sees `2` and the image is twice that.

Concretely, for a 400×300 offscreen window: `devicePixelRatio` 1 should give an 400×300 image, and a 800×600 image should be accompanied by `devicePixelRatio` 2.

### Actual Behavior

Offscreen, the page is told `devicePixelRatio` is **1** and is then rasterised at the **display's** scale factor (2). Onscreen, in the same Electron process on the same display, the two agree.

```
offscreen=true
  display scaleFactor        2
  page devicePixelRatio      1
  page innerWidth/Height     400x300
  capturePage()              800x600
  capturePage({0,0,400,300}) 800x600
  expected, if consistent    400x300

offscreen=false
  display scaleFactor        2
  page devicePixelRatio      2
  page innerWidth/Height     400x268
  capturePage()              800x536
  capturePage({0,0,400,300}) 800x536
  expected, if consistent    800x536     <- agrees
```

Two consequences, both of which bite when offscreen capture is used to render deterministic output:

1. **Layout that consults `devicePixelRatio` renders for 1× and is then rasterised at 2×.** A page that sizes anything from `devicePixelRatio` — canvas backing stores, SVG that snaps to device pixels, hairline rules — lays out for the wrong factor. The result differs from the same page captured by a headless Chromium at `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, even though every DOM measurement in the two is identical.

2. **`getBoundingClientRect()` cannot be passed to `capturePage()`.** The rect is in DIP; the rect the DOM gives you is in CSS pixels, and offscreen those differ by the display's factor. Passing an element's own rect silently captures a sub-region and rasterises it larger, which looks like a correct-sized image of the wrong content.

Neither documented way of pinning the factor works in offscreen mode:

- `--force-device-scale-factor=2` is ignored — `devicePixelRatio` stays 1 and the capture size does not change.
- `webContents.enableDeviceEmulation({ deviceScaleFactor: 2, ... })` segfaults the renderer for me on a large, script-heavy page. I have not reduced that to a minimal case, so I am not reporting it as part of this issue; on the trivial page below it does not crash.

Possibly related and long-standing: #13069 (2018) proposed `scaleFactor` in `webPreferences` plus `get/setScaleFactor`, and says the offscreen factor "was previously locked to `1.0`". That PR was closed unmerged. If the factor is still locked to 1 for the page while capture uses the display's, that would explain exactly this.

const OFFSCREEN = !process.argv.includes("--onscreen");
const W = 400, H = 300;

const PAGE = "data:text/html," + encodeURIComponent(
  `<body style="margin:0;background:#000">
     <div style="position:absolute;left:10px;top:20px;width:100px;height:50

title: [Bug]: new BrowserWindow() never returns under --ozone-platform=headless, then the process segfaults
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.10.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.3-arch1-2, Wayland session (also reproduces with the display environment variables unset)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not determined — only 40.10.2 was available to test on this machine.

### Expected Behavior

With `--ozone-platform=headless`, `new BrowserWindow()` should return and the window should load, as it does under `--headless=new`, `--ozone-platform=x11`, and `--ozone-platform=wayland`.

### Actual Behavior

Under `--ozone-platform=headless`, `app.whenReady()` resolves normally but **`new BrowserWindow()` never returns**. The constructor blocks for roughly 60 seconds, then the process dies with SIGSEGV. No window is ever created and no renderer is spawned.

Instrumenting the main process shows exactly where it stops:

```
# --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox
+0ms   start
+14ms  whenReady resolved
        <- hangs here ~60s, then SIGSEGV (exit 139, core dumped)

# --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox
+0ms   start
+56ms  whenReady resolved
+74ms  BrowserWindow constructed
+133ms did-finish-load
+134ms quit 0
```

Reproduces independently of GPU and sandbox flags:

| flags | result |
|---|---|
| `--ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--ozone-platform=headless --no-sandbox` | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--ozone-platform=headless` (sandbox on, GPU on) | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |
| `--ozone-platform=x11 --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |
| `--ozone-platform=wayland --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |

Possibly relevant: in the runs where the GPU is not disabled, the headless process still emits an **X11/GLX** error before dying, which is unexpected for a platform that should not be talking to X at all:

```
X Error of failed request:  BadMatch (invalid parameter attributes)
  Major opcode of failed request:  150 (GLX)
  Minor opcode of failed request:  5 (X_GLXMakeCurrent)
```

The core dump's crashing thread could not be symbolized (no debug symbols for the release binary), so I can only report the observable behavior, not the faulting frame.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Zeus-Deus/1797bbc852e232e83501db1b35f294a4

### Additional Information

Full reproduction — a `package.json` with `"main": "main.js"` plus the gist file:

```bash
electron . --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=/tmp/ud-a   # hang, then SIGSEGV
electron . --headless=new            --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=/tmp/ud-b   # works
```

Impact: `--ozone-platform=headless` is a common way to run Electron apps in
automated/CI-style environments without a display server. On this version it
fails in a way that is easy to misread — the app dumps core on every launch,
which on desktops that surface core dumps looks like an application crash
rather than an unsupported flag. `--headless=new` is a working substitute.
